MEMORY_SECTION.NAME: CDB105_ROM
MEMORY_SECTION.COMMENT: CDB105 firmware. The card's code reaches it through the interface page 0xf800..0xfacb.

MEMORY_SECTION.NAME: CARD_V1_SH1
MEMORY_SECTION.COMMENT: Version 1 SH-1 code of the MPEG card, decoded, as the CD-block firmware places it in buffer RAM.

COMMENTS.COMMENT: Power-on reset PC = 0x428.
Initial SP = 0x0f001000.
Manual-reset PC = 0x428.
Manual-reset SP = 0x0f001000.
Vector longword also read as descriptor clear-range start by task_initialize for task ID 14, whose descriptor pointer is zero.
Vector longword also read as descriptor clear-range end for task ID 14. Equal start/end 0x09d2 makes the loop empty.
The quoted Hitachi 1993 copyright, 34 bytes with no terminator. R reads only its first 32 bytes from area 0.
The ROM sum at 0x06f0 includes this longword, which makes the sum zero. The monitor's report sends the sum's low byte.
Value 0xe2e09ba6, which makes the sum of all big-endian ROM longwords zero modulo 2^32.
Mask interrupts at level 15. r14 is the shared zero register, and VBR selects ROM vectors. The reset vector supplies SP. Clear internal RAM before any stack write.
Entry address supplied by both power-on and manual-reset PC vectors.
Try the RAM and buffer-interface tests at most three times. Failure does not halt boot. Preserve the attempt counter on the stack because the tests reuse registers.
Store the hardware flag at 0x0f00027d and split r13 into diagnostic words. A failed buffer test adds its bits to the second word and sets hardware flag bit 7.
Initialize the MPEG card registers, compute the whole-ROM sum, then wait 120000 iterations before sampling channel status. Calls preserve the live r14 zero.
Merge the MPEG card test status into diagnostic bits 4..11. The preceding branch sets hardware flag bit 1, MPEG card present, when the test returns zero.

Read bit 2 of 0x05ffffc2: PB10, the TEST input (test pad TP3, pulled high). High selects normal runtime initialization at 0x08f8. Low, with TP3 grounded at reset, selects the diagnostic and serial-monitor path at 0x09d8. No error flag gates this.
Clear exactly 0x0f000000..0x0f000fff in words, including the future task stacks. r14 must be zero. This leaf uses PR without writing into the RAM being cleared.

Write the port registers as longwords at GBR 0x05ffff80: PADR/PBDR 0xf67b0000 (0x05d2), PAIOR/PBIOR 0x5bf63af0, PACR1/PACR2 0xff22bf1a, PBCR1/PBCR2 0x5a8a008a (0x05de). PA7, the interface chip's reset, starts low. PB10, the TEST input, stays a port pin.
Add every aligned big-endian ROM longword modulo 2^32, including metadata, code and fill. Store the sum at 0x0f000004. This routine neither compares the sum nor rejects boot.
Sum every big-endian ROM longword modulo 2^32 and store it at 0x0f000004. No comparison or startup rejection occurs in this routine.

After a 400-iteration delay, write/read words every 0x200 bytes. The comparison includes address 0x09080000, two bytes beyond the 512 KiB nominal buffer window. Its physical decoding or aliasing is not known.

Test address lines with powers of two, byte lanes with AA/55/33/CC, then the whole 512 KiB buffer with AA5555AA, its complement and zero. r13 accumulates error bits. Early pattern mismatch can leave the buffer filled with a nonzero test pattern.
Pattern mismatch contributes bit 17. Address and byte-lane errors are already in r13.
Set PA7 (bit 7 of PADR's low byte 0x05ffffc1), releasing the interface chip from reset, then write the interface registers at 0x0a000000, including 0 to 0x0a00001a.

Check writable bits at 0x0a000008/0x0a00000a, then configure a channel using 0x05ffff50..0x05ffff5f and compare four reads from 0x0a000000 with two RAM words. These are device transactions, not ordinary RAM.
Register readback mismatch contributes bit 2, and the data-transfer check still runs.
Data mismatch contributes bit 3 and skips normal interface/buffer cleanup.
Always returns zero, so the reset caller's conditional error branch is never taken.
Initialize extension/header, transfer and control state, then tail-jump into task setup. Each callee is a leaf or preserves its own PR. No reset continuation follows.

Vector 4, general illegal instruction: restart at the reset entry 0x0428 without a reset. Reset takes SP from the vector table only at a real reset, so SP stays as the exception left it, eight bytes below the interrupted SP.
Vector 4: restart at 0x0428 without a reset. Vector 12 (0x09ba), SCI1 (0x09c6) and the unused interrupt sources (0x09cc) restart the same way.
Vector 6, slot illegal instruction: return at once.
Vector 9, CPU address error: return at once.

Vector 10, DMA address error. Mask all interrupts (SR 0xf0) and stop the DMA controller as startup's 0x06bc does: DMAOR read and cleared, which also clears its address error flag, CHCR0..3 read and set to 0x40, with DE, IE and TE clear, then DMAOR 1 (DME).
Vector 10: stop all four DMA channels as startup does, 8 to the transfer control 0x0a000002, return. No task is told.
8 to the transfer control 0x0a000002, as a transfer's end writes it, without a direction bit. Return with RTE. No channel is armed again and no task is told.
Vector 11, NMI: return at once.
Vector 12, user break: restart at 0x0428.
No vector holds this address. A restart like its neighbours.
Vectors 104..107, SCI1 receive error, receive, transmit and transmit end: restart at 0x0428.

Vectors of interrupt sources the firmware does not use: IRQ0..IRQ5 (64..69), ITU0 and ITU1 (80..82, 84..86), ITU2 overflow (90), ITU3 compare match A and overflow (92, 94), SCI0 receive error, transmit and transmit end (100, 102, 103), parity error (108), A/D end (109), watchdog interval (112) and refresh compare match (113): restart at 0x0428.
Reserved vectors and TRAPA 0x2f..0x3f: return at once. Task setup reads the vector longwords 0x006c and 0x0070, both 0x09d2, as task 14's empty clear range.
Reserved vectors and TRAPA 0x2f..0x3f return at once. Slot illegal instruction, CPU address error and NMI return the same way from 0x093a, 0x0940 and 0x09b4.

Reset branches here from 0x0508 when PB10 (TEST) reads low, with SR 0xf0. SCI1 is as startup left it: clocked synchronous (SMR1 0x80), BRR1 99, TxD1 on PB11 and SCK1 on PB13. Set TE and send the low byte of the ROM sum 0x0f000004.
Reset with PB10 (TEST, TP3) low. SCI1 clocked synchronous sends the ROM sum's low byte, then after a delay a byte built from the diagnostic words, whose bit 2 stays set unless an address line failed.
Wait 0x2b98b6 passes.

The second byte, from the diagnostic words at 0x0f000000. r13 still holds 0x0f000004, so the byte has bit 2 set unless word 0x0f000000 (address lines) is nonzero, which sets r13 to 1 instead. Bits 0..3 of word 0x0f000002 (byte lanes, pattern, interface registers, interface data) are ORed in.
Bits 4..7 from word 0x0f000002 shifted right by four: bit 4 for its bit 4 or 6, bit 5 for bit 5, bit 6 for bit 7 and bit 7 for bit 8, which the four-bit card mask never sets. Send the byte.
Wait until PB10 reads high 200000 times in a row (0x30d40). A low read starts the count again.
Wait until PB10 reads high 200000 times in a row. A low read starts the count again.
The monitor. SP 0x0f001000, r10 the SCI base 0x05fffec0, r11 the state 0x0f000004. SCI1 asynchronous 8N1 (SMR1 0), SCR1 0x30 (TE and RE), BRR1 0x41. SSR1 read and cleared.
SCI1 asynchronous 8N1, BRR1 0x41 (about 9600 bps at 20 MHz), SSR1 cleared, which sends TDR1's last byte again. State at 0x0f000004 cleared, prompt ':'.
PBCR1 bits 5:4 to 10: PB10 becomes RxD1.
PBCR1 bits 5:4 to 10: PB10 becomes RxD1.

Clear the state longword 0x0f000004, over the ROM sum: +0 line length, +1 transmit write index, +2 transmit read index, +3 line ready. +4 L's address, +8 its word and +10 its mode keep what reset cleared. Queue the prompt ':'.
Poll forever with interrupts masked: receive, transmit, a completed line, L's repeat.
Poll forever with interrupts masked: receive, transmit, a completed line, L's repeat.
With RDRF (SSR1 bit 6) set: clear it and take RDR1. A tab and bytes from 0x20 up, 0x80..0xff included, go to the line 0x0f000100 + length. The length stops at 255, so later bytes overwrite byte 255.
CR: line ready, L's mode cleared, and CR stored after the line without counting.
Backspace: the length drops unless it is 0.
Every received byte is echoed, other control bytes too.

With TDRE (SSR1 bit 7) set and the ring not empty (write index +1 not the read index +2): the byte at 0x0f000200 + read index to TDR1, clear TDRE, advance the read index. The indexes are bytes, so the ring is 256 bytes with no full check.
A ready line: clear the flag and run the command its first byte names, either case: W 0x0c06, R 0x0bb6, L 0x0c42. Other lines do nothing. Then length 0 and the prompt ':'.
L's repeat, once a loop: mode 1 (+10) reads the address at +4, mode 2 writes the word at +8 there. An odd address takes a byte access, an even one a word.

R address: skip blanks after the command byte. Without an address nothing is answered. Area 0 (bits 26..24) reads 0x0400 + the low five bits, the first 32 of the identity text's 34 bytes. Area 7 keeps bits 31..24 and 2..0 only, the eight bytes from 0x0f000000. Other areas read as given.
R address: area 0 reads only 0x0400 + the low five bits, area 7 only 0x0f000000..0x0f000007. Answers '>', four hex digits and CR.
'>', then the value as four hex digits: a byte (odd address) after 00, or a word. Then CR.
W address value: areas 5 (on-chip I/O) and 7 (on-chip RAM) are refused, as is a missing value. An odd address takes the value's low byte, an even one its low word. Nothing is answered.
W address value: a byte (odd address) or word write. Areas 5 and 7 refused.
L address [value]: areas 5, 7 and 0 are refused. The address goes to +4. Without a value mode 1 (read), with one its low word to +8 and mode 2 (write). The next CR received clears the mode.
L address [value]: read or write the address once a loop until the next CR. Areas 0, 5 and 7 refused.
Hex digits from r1 into r13 until a blank or the line's end (0x0f000100 + length). A byte that is not a hex digit counts as 0. Only the last eight digits stay. r1 ends at the stop.
Skip spaces and tabs from r1. At the line's end r1 = 0.
Queue r0's low byte as two hex digits, high first.
Queue r0 at 0x0f000200 + write index (+1) and advance it. Uses r1 and r2.
An ASCII hex digit to 0..15, either case. Anything else gives 0.
r0's low nibble to ASCII 0..9 or A..F.

Clear all twelve ready heads. Initialize thirteen IDs from 0x1340..0x134c, then chain the first eleven records through +16 into the first ready head, regardless of their normal priority-table slots. The selector therefore starts task 1.
Initialize thirteen task records, chain eleven into the first ready head, then select and dispatch task 1 at 0x63dc. Initial frames hold PC/SR only.

TRAPA 0x2e (vector 0x00b8), called by task 6 for the host's reset request with IPRA..IPRD cleared. SR 0xf0 masks every interrupt. With GBR 0x05ffff00 clear TIER0, TIER1 and TIER2 (0x05ffff06, 0x05ffff10, 0x05ffff1a) and TSR0, TSR1 and TSR2 (0x05ffff07, 0x05ffff11, 0x05ffff1b).
TRAPA 0x2e: reset timers, DMA and transfer state, re-create the records of every task except 6 and 14, chain them for a fresh start and dispatch. Task 6 resumes after its trap.
Reset the software timers at 0x1c46, write the startup DMA values (DMAOR and CHCR0..CHCR3) at 0x06bc again and reset the transfer state 0x0f000248..0x0f00025b through 0x2388.
Clear ready heads 0x0f0001d8..0x0f000203. The last head 0x0f000204, where the interrupted idle task 14 waits, is kept.

Initialize the records of IDs 1, 2, 4, 12, 13, 7, 9, 8, 5, 11 and 3 (bytes 0x134d..0x1357) through 0x1058 as at startup. Records 11 and 3 are the sector lock and the transfer lock, so both come back free.
Chain IDs 1, 2, 4, 12, 13, 7, 9, 8, 5 and 6 (bytes 0x1340..0x1349) under ready head 0x0f0001d8 through their +16 links.
Task 6's record in place: ID 6 and state 0 in the first longword, +4, +12, +16 and +20 cleared, +8 the current SP, which holds the TRAPA frame. Its mailbox 0x0f0000cc..0x0f0000e7 is cleared.
Select at 0x10a8 and dispatch at 0x1118. The restarted tasks run from their entries in chain order. Task 6, in state 0, resumes after its TRAPA with PC and SR only.
TRAPA 0x28 (vector 0x00a0): with SR 0x60, initialize the record of task r11 >> 24 again through 0x1058 as at startup, keeping r10..r13, and return.
TRAPA 0x28: initialize the record of task r11 >> 24 again, as at startup.

TRAPA 0x23 at VBR=0. Set SR=0x60 and locate the current record. This saves only the exception PC/SR frame. General registers, PR, GBR and r14 are not saved here, so callers must tolerate scratch values after resumption.
Wait for a message with an exception-only frame. Queued messages make the current task ready. A matching partner link can bypass ordinary ready selection.

Record +7 counts occupied message words. If nonzero, append the current record to its ID-selected ready queue before choosing another task. The append does not clear +16, so callers require a detached record and a valid acyclic chain.

Record +20 can nominate a direct partner. Accept it only when its ID matches the current record's +4 or +5 byte, clearing the matched byte and partner link. Otherwise retain +20, clear +4, and use ordinary ready-queue selection.

Save the waiting task's exception SP and state 1. r13 identifies the selected task, while r3 still identifies the waiting task. PR is overwritten by the selector call only on the ordinary-selection path.

TRAPA 0x20, send and wait for a reply. r11 is a message: bits 31..24 name the destination and bits 23..16 the sender, which must be the caller. Post it, then hand the CPU straight to the destination, which resumes as its saved state says, and leave the sender in state 2 until the destination replies with TRAPA 0x29 or waits again.

TRAPA 0x20: post r11, run the destination at once, sender (bits 23..16) waits in state 2. Refuses a destination in state 2 or 3. A destination already in a ready queue is looked for in the queue whose head slot lies 16 bytes after its own. For the last four heads (IDs 1, 13, 9 and 14) that slot is in the disc extension's collection state at 0x0f000208..0x0f000217, followed as a record unless it reads 0. From a zero link the search goes on through the ROM longwords at 0x10 and 0x944 to an unaligned longword read at 0x00090019.
Destination record from bits 31..24, sender record from bits 23..16. Neither is checked.
A destination already in a rendezvous, state 2 or 3, is refused.
Post through the shared mailbox routine. Its result is not checked.

A destination still in a ready queue (+6 nonzero) is taken out first. The walk starts one level short: r1 is the head slot's address rather than the first record, so it compares that address, then walks the queue whose head slot lies 16 bytes on. When that queue does not hold the destination, its zero link sends the walk on through the ROM longwords at 0x10 and 0x944 to a longword read at 0x00090019, a CPU address error. For the last four heads (IDs 1, 13, 9 and 14) the slot 16 bytes on is past the heads, in the disc extension's collection state at 0x0f000208..0x0f000217: 0 acts as the zero link, anything else is followed as a record.
Found: unlink it. Its own +16 link is left as it was.
The sender waits in state 2 with its exception SP saved. The destination names it in +20 and is dispatched next with its old state.
Refused: diagnostic 4, return -1 to the caller.

TRAPA 0x29, reply. The current task answers its partner (+20), normally the sender of a TRAPA 0x20: r12 and r13 go to the partner's +24 and +28, the partner's +5 and +20 name the replier, and the replier waits in state 3 while the partner runs. The partner's next TRAPA 0x23 runs the replier again. The partner's state is not checked.
TRAPA 0x29: r12 and r13 into the partner's first two mailbox words (+24 and +28), the replier waits in state 3 and the partner runs. No partner: diagnostic 5, r0 = -1.
No partner: diagnostic 5, return -1.
TRAPA 0x21: mask at level 6, store r11 via 0x11be, and append a waiting detached destination to its ready queue. Does not switch tasks.
Store message and append destination only when state1 and not already ready. Existing occupied slot is overwritten without incrementing occupied count. No task switch inside this trap.
Only state 1 with ready offset zero is appended. Existing ready membership is preserved.

TRAPA 0x22, post and raise. Post r11 as TRAPA 0x21 does, then queue a destination in state 1 or 4 at the priority its class byte (bits 23..16) names: bit 7 the first ready head, otherwise the head of the task with that ID. The raise lasts until the destination is dispatched, which clears +6. r0 returns the post's failure (-1), the destination's state when it is neither 1 nor 4, or the ready offset written to +6.
TRAPA 0x22: post r11, then queue a destination in state 1 or 4 at the head its class byte names, bit 7 the first head.
A destination already queued is unlinked from the queue +6 names. This walk starts at the head slot's first record, and the unlinked record's +16 link is cleared.
Class bit 7: offset 0x80 and the first head. Otherwise the class byte times 4 indexes the ready table, which is not validated.
Append at the tail through the +16 links.

Requeue the current record as state 4, whose stack holds a full 80-byte context. MOV.B sign-extends the ID before indexing the table at 0x13ec. No bounds check. GAS distances include the two-byte section-base bias for longword PC rounding.
Append current record to its ID-selected ready queue, mark state 4, select and dispatch. Requires an existing full context at record +8. The ready link is not cleared before append.
Append through +16. The incoming current-record link is not cleared here, so a stale link can splice another chain or create a cycle.

r1 is an unchecked task ID. Write ID/state/lock/owner in the first record word. Nonzero stack entries receive SR=0x20 and the entry PC, an exception-only frame. Null stacks leave record +8 untouched. r2..r9 and r14 survive, r0/r10..r13 are scratch.
Unchecked task ID in r1. Initialize record, optional PC/SR frame and descriptor-selected clear range. A null stack leaves saved SP untouched.

Clear message/queue fields, then use descriptor +0x6c/+0x70 as a half-open clear range. ID 14 reads a zero descriptor pointer, hence ROM vector longwords 0x006c/0x0070. Both contain 0x09d2, making the loop empty.

Scan twelve head words in ascending address order, 0x0f0001d8..0x0f000204. First nonempty head wins. This order differs from the ID-to-head table order. Only r0/r12/r13 and T are changed. r10 survives for the lock wait continuation.
First nonempty of twelve head words 0x0f0001d8..0x0f000204. Pop head, clear record +16, return record in r12/r13 and r0=0. r10 survives. Empty queues invoke diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b.
Empty queues invoke diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b with r0=6. The trap returns at once, so the fallback below runs with the registers unchanged.
Pop the chosen head and clear its +16 link. Return the record in r12 and r13, r0=0, T=0 on a nonempty selection. The RTS delay slot supplies r13 before return.

r13 is the selected record. Its old signed state selects a table destination. Mark it running (5), clear ready offset, publish current record, then switch SP in the JMP delay slot. No state, destination or stack validity checks occur here.
Use signed record state as index into 0x1358. Mark state 5, clear +6, publish current record, switch SP in JMP delay slot. State 4 restores a full context, states 0/3/5/6 only PC/SR.

State-1 resumption. The decoded disc header is also a per-task PC table: a nonzero word at 0x09075800 + 4*task_id replaces the saved exception PC. This path checks neither the disc-present flag nor the target address. It consumes a message before RTE, so the override receives that message in r11.
State-1 dispatch reads an optional per-task PC at 0x09075800 + 4*ID, consumes a mailbox word into r11, then RTEs to the original or replaced PC.

Scan consecutive words from the task's mailbox pointer until one is nonzero. There is no count or end check. A nonzero count with empty storage can read beyond the task's assigned mailbox. The first nonzero word must name this task in its high byte. A mismatch enters diagnostic trap 0x2b with r0=7.

Message format here: high byte destination, next byte source/class, low word payload. Save the source byte at record +4 and decrement +7 modulo 256. Clear the consumed word in the RTE delay slot. r11 retains the complete message.
Dispatch for state 2: r12 and r13 from +24 and +28, the first two mailbox words, cleared, then PC and SR.
State 4 frame, low address first: MACL, MACH, GBR, PR, r13..r0, PC, SR. Advance record +8 by 80 before restoring r13. r14 and VBR are not restored.
80-byte frame: MACL, MACH, GBR, PR, r13..r0, PC, SR. Record +8 advances to post-return SP. r14 and VBR are not restored.
States 0/3/5/6 restore only PC/SR and advance SP by 8. Record +8 stays at the saved frame. General/special registers retain the incoming dispatch-path values.
Restore PC/SR and consume eight bytes. Record +8 is unchanged. No general registers, PR, GBR, MACH or MACL are restored. Their values come from the intervening execution path.
r11 high byte is destination, next byte source/class. Use destination tables without bounds checks. Record +3 filters ordinary sources, and bit7 bypasses that filter.

Destination high byte and source/class second byte select unchecked tables. Class bit7 bypasses ordinary source filter and selects alternate slots. Source mismatch or null slot reaches diagnostic trap.
Class bit7 selects an alternate table offset: 0x38 + 4*(class & 0x7f). Ordinary classes use 4*class. Null slot reaches diagnostic trap.
Increment occupied-slot count only when previous slot is zero, then overwrite slot. This is a coalescing slot, not a FIFO of every message.
Source filter mismatch enters diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b with r0=2, which returns at once.
Null message slot enters diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b with r0=3. Destination and class must select valid tables.

TRAPA 0x26, try a lock without waiting. r11 names the lock as for TRAPA 0x2a: bits 31..24 the record, bits 23..16 the owner token. A clear lock byte is set by TAS.B and the owner stored, r0 = 0. A held lock returns 0 when its owner byte equals the token, -1 otherwise.
TRAPA 0x26: take the lock without waiting. r0 = 0 when taken or held by the same owner token, -1 otherwise. Owners 0x80..0xff never match.
The stored owner is sign-extended and the token zero-extended, so owners 0x80..0xff never match.
Release the record selected by r11[31:24], owner token r11[23:16]. SR=0x60 masks interrupts through level 6 until RTE restores the saved SR.
TRAPA 0x27 with VBR=0. Release owner-matched lock or transfer ownership to a waiter and enter scheduler context saving. r11 high bytes select record and owner.
ROM literal at 0x132c.
Compare owner bytes modulo 256. Unlike the acquire busy path, this comparison tolerates high-bit owner tokens.
Record +12 is a waiter chain. Empty means clear owner and lock. Otherwise transfer ownership to the first waiter.
The waiter record first byte becomes the owner. Detach its +12 link and append it through +16 to the ready list selected by that byte. The signed byte load also feeds the table index.
ROM literal at 0x1328.
Walk the ready chain until a zero link. No local cycle, range or null-table-entry check.
Save r0..r13, PR, GBR, MACH and MACL below the eight-byte exception frame. r0 is already zero, and r10/r12/r13 contain service scratch values. r14 is not saved here.
Save 72 bytes below the PC/SR frame, store the total 80-byte frame pointer in current-record +8, then branch to 0x102e. r14 is not in this frame.
Store the resulting 80-byte frame pointer in current-record +8, then branch to the scheduler at 0x102e. No local RTE on this path. ROM literal at 0x1320.
No waiter: clear owner now and lock byte in the RTE delay slot. The delay-slot store runs with the restored caller SR and SP.
Wrong owner: diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b with r0=1. Its behavior determines whether the following RTE is reached.
Acquire the record selected by r11[31:24], using r11[23:16] as owner token. r11 low 16 bits do not affect this service.
TRAPA 0x2a with VBR=0. TAS.B acquires an empty lock, and contention appends the current record to its waiter chain. Scratch r0/r10/r12/r13, direct return restores exception PC/SR/SP.
ROM literal at 0x132c.
TAS.B sets bit 7 and reports whether the entire old byte was zero. Other nonzero bit patterns are also busy and retain their low bits.
Uncontended: store the owner byte and return zero. r1..r9, r11, r14, PR, GBR, MACH, MACL and VBR are untouched, r0/r10/r12/r13 are scratch.
MOV.B sign-extends stored owner, but r13 is zero-extended. Tokens 0x80..0xff therefore fail this same-owner comparison even when the bytes match.
Stored owner is sign-extended, token unsigned. Equal bytes 0x80..0xff take the different-owner path. Equal low tokens invoke diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b, r0=10.
Same owner: diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b with r0=10. No recursive acquisition count is maintained here.
Different owner: append the current record through +12 to the lock waiter chain. Current-record and link validity are incoming-state requirements. ROM literal at 0x1320.
The delay slot links the waiter before ready selection at 0x10a8. Selection supplies the chosen record in r13 and preserves r10 for the continuation.
Only the waiting task's PC/SR frame is saved. Its later state-6 return does not restore its original general registers or PR.
After ready selection, set waiting record state to 6, save its exception SP at +8, and branch to context dispatch at 0x1118. PR was overwritten by the BSR.
Continuation after selection at 0x10a8: state=6 and exception SP stored for r10 record. r13 must identify selected record for dispatch at 0x1118.
Record IDs the restart initializes: 1, 2, 4, 12, 13, 7, 9, 8, 5, 11, 3.
Seven state destinations: 0/3/5/6 -> 0x11aa, 1 -> 0x1130, 2 -> 0x116c, 4 -> 0x117c. No local state bounds check.
Fifteen ready-list head pointers. Null entries and signed out-of-range indices are not validated by the local release code.
Fifteen record pointers, indexed by r11[31:24]. Entries 10 and 14 alias 0x0f0001bc. Index 11 selects 0x0f000168. No local index bounds check.

Descriptor pointer per task ID 0..14. The post routine at 0x11be reads the slot word for a message's class, task creation at 0x1058 the clear range at +0x6c and +0x70. IDs 0 and 14 have none, and 3, 10 and 11 share 0x1960.
Task 1: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Class 5 to 0x0f000020. Creation clears 0x0f000020..0x0f000023.
Task 2: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 0x80 and 0x81 to 0x0f00003c, 0x0f000040 and 0x0f000044. Creation clears 0x0f00003c..0x0f000047.
Task 4: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 5 and 0x81 to 0x0f000078, 0x0f00007c and 0x0f000080. Creation clears 0x0f000078..0x0f000083.

Task 5: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 1, 4, 6, 0x80, 0x81 and 0x84 to 0x0f0000ac, 0x0f0000a8, 0x0f0000a4, 0x0f00009c, 0x0f0000b0 and 0x0f0000a0. Creation clears 0x0f00009c..0x0f0000b3.

Task 6: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0x81 and 0x83 to 0x0f0000d0, 0x0f0000d4, 0x0f0000d8, 0x0f0000dc, 0x0f0000e0, 0x0f0000e4 and 0x0f0000cc. Creation clears 0x0f0000cc..0x0f0000e7.
Task 7: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 4, 6, 7 and 0x81 to 0x0f000100, 0x0f000104, 0x0f000108, 0x0f00010c and 0x0f000110. Creation clears 0x0f000100..0x0f000113.

Task 8: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 8, 9, 0x81, 0x89, 0x8a, 0x8b and 0x8c to 0x0f00013c, 0x0f000140, 0x0f000144, 0x0f00012c, 0x0f000130, 0x0f000138 and 0x0f000134. Creation clears 0x0f00012c..0x0f000147.
Task 9: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 9 and 0x81 to 0x0f000164 and 0x0f000160. Creation clears 0x0f000160..0x0f000167.
Task 12: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3 and 0x81 to 0x0f000198 and 0x0f00019c. Creation clears 0x0f000198..0x0f00019f.
Task 13: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Class 0x81 to 0x0f0001b8. Creation clears 0x0f0001b8..0x0f0001bb.
Tasks 3, 10 and 11: every slot null, so a post to them raises the diagnostic trap. Empty clear range.
Reset disc-extension header/body, VBR and active flag, then five state words. Cleanup supplies r0=0, which the state loop relies on.
Prepare collection using state at 0x0f000208: +4 disc address, +8 encoded length. Clear only the 0x48-byte decoded header first. Authentication is not checked by this routine.
Prepare disc collection: validate nonzero address/length, compare the address with the lead-out, clear decoded header and initialize destination/count state.
Unsigned disc-address comparison against low 24 bits of [0x090001fc]. No buffer-capacity or length-alignment check appears in this preparation routine.
State +0x0c is the moving destination, +0x10 the remaining encoded bytes.
Compute ceil(length/2048). Return full count in r0, store only its low byte at state +0. This byte truncation does not enforce a maximum encoded length.

Input r0 selects raw sector slot. TRAPA 0x2a/0x27 and r11=0x0b070000 bracket copying. With VBR=0, the pair acquires/releases record 11 for owner 7. Direct returns clobber r0/r10/r12/r13, and contention can enter the scheduler. The slot value is saved on the stack.
Copy sector payload between TRAPA 0x2a and TRAPA 0x27. Decode and process the entry only when no encoded bytes remain.
VBR=0 selects acquire handler 0x12d2, record 11 and owner 7. Direct return clobbers r0/r10/r12/r13, and contention may hand control to the scheduler.
Mode byte is low byte of BE32 sector word +0x0c. Mode 1 skips 0x10, others skip 0x18.

Copy count = min(remaining,2048). State advances by this exact count. The do-while loop still copies whole longwords: zero copies one longword, and partial counts round up. Upstream guards may exclude these cases, but this routine does not enforce them.
VBR=0 selects release handler 0x1250. No-waiter return clears owner/lock and clobbers r0/r10/r12/r13, and a waiter triggers scheduler context saving.
Return immediately if bytes remain. Only the final sector saves PR/SR and decodes.
Save PR/SR, mask interrupts, decode from 0x09075848 to 0x09075800. r4 must point at loader state on entry. Decoded output precedes acceptance checks.
Invokes decoder: source 0x09075848, destination 0x09075800. Saves/restores SR and masks interrupts around decode/entry.
MOV.B sign-extends, then unsigned CMP/HI against zero accepts every nonzero byte. The field at decoded +0x44 is a presence/active value here, not a signed-positive test.
Copy decoded +0x44 into global flag, install VBR from decoded +0, call optional +0x3c. VBR and entry are supplied values. This block performs no range or alignment validation.
Loads supplied VBR value from decoded +0. No local pointer validation.
Calls nonzero entry pointer from decoded +0x3c. The entry return value is discarded.
Both decode rejection and accepted return yield r0=0 here. Callback return is discarded. Restore saved SR exactly. VBR remains supplied on acceptance and zero on cleanup.
Clear [0x09075800,0x09077c00), VBR and active flag. Leaves loader state words intact.
Clear header [0x09075800,0x09075848), VBR and active flag. The encoded source begins at 0x09075848.
Read BE32 encoded length from expansion address 0x0e000000, then source is +4. Require 1..0x5000 here. The decoder itself rejects lengths below 16. No SR save/mask here.
Expansion loader for the MPEG card's code: length at 0x0e000000, data from +4. No local SR masking.
Decoded +0 becomes global byte 0x0f0002fd. Compare decoded +1 with disc +0x45. Both MOV.B values are sign-extended before the unsigned CMP/HI.
If disc comparison byte is greater, call nonzero disc callback at decoded disc +0x40. r1 is not reloaded after callback. Subsequent +4 read relies on callback preserving r1.
Call entry read from @(4,r1), with no null/range/alignment check. The disc callback before it must preserve r1. Successful return discards entry result and returns r0=0. VBR is not installed here.
Calls @(4,r1) without zero check. The optional disc callback must preserve r1 for the expected table.
Length or decoder failure clears expansion destination/state and returns -1.
Alternate cleanup entry has no incoming edge within this cluster. It shares the saved-PR epilogue, so it is not a standalone callable function.
Calls expansion cleanup, then shares the saved-PR epilogue. No incoming branch originates in 0x19d4..0x1b79.
Clear [0x0907b000,0x09080000), global byte 0x0f0002fd and word 0x0f0007ac.
NOP padding before the shared literal pool.
Pointer to the record table at 0x1464. No instruction in 0x19d4..0x1b79 reads this literal.
Final bootstrap task: publish register values via 0x1efc, then spin without polling.
Final bootstrap task calls 0x1efc then spins at 0x1be6. It does not wait on a mailbox or poll a device register.
Idle loop: three NOPs and a delayed unconditional branch. It has no exit of its own. Task 14 runs it whenever no other task is ready, and interrupts post the messages that wake the others.

Three NOPs and a delayed unconditional branch back here. No software release condition or register reads. Task 14 runs it whenever no other task is ready, and interrupts post the messages that wake the others.
TRAPA 0x2b through vector 0x00ac returns at once. Callers pass a condition code in r0.
TRAPA 0x2b returns immediately. Callers pass a condition code in r0.
TRAPA 0x2c returns at once.
TRAPA 0x2c returns at once.
Clear 0x0f000220..0x0f000247 and 0x0f00021c, and program register bytes.

Timer reset for the restart at 0x0d94: TIOR4 0 and TIER4 4 (overflow interrupt only). Clear the timer table 0x0f000220..0x0f00023f and longwords 0x0f000240 and 0x0f000244. Unlike the startup version at 0x1c04, the time high part 0x0f00021c, TCR4 and TSTR are left as they are.
Clear the software timer table and disable the compare-match interrupt, keeping the clock running.
ITU4 overflow, vector 98 at 0x0188: clear OVF (bit 2 of TSR4 0x05ffff35) and increment longword 0x0f00021c, the high part of the timer clock.
ITU4 overflow, vector 98. Increments the timer clock high part 0x0f00021c.
ITU4 compare match A, vector 96 at 0x0180: clear IMFA. The current time is 0x0f00021c << 8 plus GRA4 bits 15..8. While the first deadline (0x0f000224) is still ahead, return with RTE.
ITU4 compare match A, vector 96. Posts every expired identifier with TRAPA 0x21, programs GRA4 for the next deadline or disables IMIA4, then reschedules through 0x102e.
Expired: save the remaining registers, keep the stack pointer in the current task record and switch to stack 0x0f0008f8.

Post the first identifier with TRAPA 0x21 and move the later entries forward. An empty table clears IMIEA. An expired next entry is posted as well, otherwise its deadline programs GRA4. Continue in the scheduler at 0x102e.

ITU4 compare match B (vector 97, ROM longword 0x0184): the deferred post. Save r0..r13, PR, GBR, MACH and MACL, keep the frame pointer in the current record and switch to the interrupt workspace 0x0f0008f8.
ITU4 compare match B (vector 97): post the waiting messages and reschedule.
Clear IMFB (TSR4 bit 1). With interrupts masked take the two pending messages at 0x0f000240 and 0x0f000244, clear both and clear IMIEB (TIER4 bit 1).
Post the first message, then the second when there is one, and reschedule at 0x102e.

TRAPA 0x24 through vector 0x0090: r11 identifier, r10 duration. Read counter 0x0f00021c before and after TCNT4 (0x05ffff36) until both reads match, then set SR 0x60. Deadline = counter << 8 plus TCNT4 bits 15..8 plus r10 - (6 * r10 >> 8).

TRAPA 0x24 starts timer r11 with duration r10. Deadline = (0x0f00021c << 8 plus TCNT4 bits 15..8) + r10 - (6 * r10 >> 8). Up to four entries ordered by deadline. A new first entry programs GRA4 and enables IMIA4. A full table returns r0 = -1.
Insert into the four entries at 0x0f000220 by signed deadline difference, after entries whose deadline is not later. A full table reaches TRAPA 0x2b with r0 9 and returns r0 = -1.
A new first entry programs GRA4 as deadline low byte << 8 | 0x7f, clears IMFA and sets IMIEA. Store the identifier and deadline and return r0 = 0.
TRAPA 0x25 through vector 0x0094: set SR 0x60 and search the four eight-byte entries at 0x0f000220 (identifier, deadline) for r11. An empty table or no match returns r0 = -1 with no timer access.
TRAPA 0x25 removes the r11 entry from the four-entry timer table at 0x0f000220 and returns r0 = 0, or -1 when absent. Removing the first entry reprograms ITU4 GRA or clears ITU4 IMIEA.
First entry removed: move the second entry forward. A remaining timer programs ITU4 GRA (0x05ffff38) as deadline low byte << 8 | 0x7f, and an empty table clears ITU4 TIER IMIEA (0x05ffff34 bit0).
Move later entries forward, clear the fourth entry and return r0 = 0. Only removal of the first entry touches the timer.
TRAPA 0x2d (vector 0x00b4), post from an interrupt handler: keep r11 at 0x0f000240, or at 0x0f000244 when the first is taken.
TRAPA 0x2d: an interrupt handler's message waits at 0x0f000240 or 0x0f000244 until ITU4 compare match B, 0x7d counts later.
Compare match B 0x7d counts later: GRB4 = TCNT4 + 0x7d, clear IMFB (TSR4 bit 1), set IMIEB (TIER4 bit 1). The message is posted from 0x1d38.
Write 0 to 0x0a000004, OR 0x60 into 0x05ffff86, write 1 to 0x0a000008 and 0x0be1 to 0x0a00001e.

Clear the interface's command flags (0 to 0x0a000004), set IRQ6 priority 6 (0x0060 into 0x05ffff86), enable the command interrupt (0x0001 to 0x0a000008), write 0x0be1 to 0x0a00001e and publish NUL CDBLOCK in CR1..CR4 (0x0a000010..0x0a000017). Host commands raise IRQ6 from here on.
Write words 0043,4442,4c4f,434b to 0x0a000010..0x0a000017: the byte sequence NUL CDBLOCK. These are CR1..CR4, the response registers the host reads.
IRQ6 vector 70 at VBR+0x118. Hardware has stacked PC/SR. Save r0..r13, PR, GBR, MACH, MACL. r14/VBR remain live. Publish full 80-byte frame in current record.

IRQ6 vector 70, raised by the interface chip when the host writes CR4: save the full task context, switch to the interrupt stack, clear the command flag at 0x0a000004, which releases IRQ6, read CR1..CR4 and dispatch.

Switch to interrupt workspace SP 0x0f0008f8. Write zero to interface +4, then read words +22,+20,+18,+16 into r2 and r1. The zero write clears the command flag and releases IRQ6. The words are CR4, CR3, CR2 and CR1.
When state byte 0x0f0007b0 bit0 is set, reject all command bytes except 05. Both routes return response r12/r13 and optional message r11.
Extract command high byte of r1 and use its high nibble for the 16-entry table at 0x1fe0. Pass sign-extended command in r3/r0.
Publish r12/r13 in four ascending interface words +16..+22, then write 1 to +30. Nonzero r11 invokes real message-post TRAPA 0x21.
Nonzero response r11 invokes TRAPA 0x21. Command05 constructs 06810002, stores it in task6 class81 slot, and makes waiting task6 ready. Scheduler then resumes its saved continuation 2798.
Requeue interrupted task through 0x102e. Scheduler may resume it with its full frame or wake a higher-priority mailbox task.
Commands 00..06 use seven pointers, and 07..0f take the reject response.
High nibble 1: commands 10..12 through the table at 0x2068 (10 at 0x9350, 11 at 0x93f0, 12 at 0x941a). Bytes above 0x12 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 1: commands 10 (play), 11 (seek) and 12 (scan) through the table at 0x2068.
High nibble 2: command 20 through the one-entry table at 0x208c to 0x22dc. Bytes above 0x20 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 2: command 20 (subcode) through the table at 0x208c.
High nibble 3: commands 30, 31 and 32 through the table at 0x20a8 (30 at 0x4d68, 31 at 0x4d8e, 32 at 0x4d96). Bytes above 0x32 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 3: commands 30 (set CD device connection), 31 (get it) and 32 (last partition reached).
High nibble 4: commands 40..48 through the table at 0x20d0. Bytes above 0x48 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 4: commands 40..48 through the table at 0x20d0.
No branch reaches 0x20ca: a second jmp @r4 after the reject branch.
High nibble 5: commands 50..56 through the table at 0x210c. Bytes above 0x56 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 5: commands 50..56 through the table at 0x210c.

High nibble 6: commands 60..67 through the table at 0x2140. 60 at 0x754e, 61 and 63 through the data-command entries 0x22e2 and 0x22e8, 62 at 0x68ba, 64 through 0x22ee, 65 and 66 at 0x6efc, 67 at 0x6f38. Bytes above 0x67 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 6: commands 60..67 through the table at 0x2140.

High nibble 7: commands 70..75 through the table at 0x2178. 70 at 0x9478, 71 at 0x9524, 72 at 0x9566, 73 through the data-command entry 0x22f4, 74 at 0x9618, 75 at 0x96c2. Bytes above 0x75 take the reject response at 0x22a6.
High nibble 7: commands 70..75 through the table at 0x2178.

Group 9, commands 90..9F, with the command sign-extended in r3. A command above 9F is rejected through 0x22a6, and so is any command while bit 1 of the hardware flag 0x0f00027d (MPEG card present) is clear.
Commands 90..9F. Rejected without bit 1 of 0x0f00027d (MPEG card present) and, except 93, without the card bit (bit 7 of 0x0f000892). 93 goes to 0xa050, the others to 0xf800.
Every command but 93 also needs the card bit, bit 7 of 0x0f000892.
Jump through the table at 0x21c0 by the low nibble: 93 to 0xa050, the others to 0xf800. r1, r2 and r3 are as the IRQ6 entry passed them.
Group A, commands A0..AF, with the same gates as group 9 and the card bit needed for every command. The table at 0x2228 sends AE to 0xa148, AF to 0xa0f0 and the others to 0xf800.
Commands A0..AF, with the card bit needed for every command. AE goes to 0xa148, AF to 0xa0f0, the others to 0xf800.
Group E: r3 is the sign-extended command byte. The unsigned compare with 0xffffffe2 accepts e0..e2. e3..ef take the reject response.
Group E: e0..e2 through the three-entry table at 0x2288. e3..ef take the reject response.
Low nibble indexes three handlers at 0x2288: e0 0xc2b6, e1 0xc39a, e2 0xc334.
Reserved high-nibble group: reject response.
High-nibble f accepts only ff. Other bytes use reject response.
Clear outgoing message r11 and tail-call reject response helper 0x91e8.
Command 06 from the group 0 table: clear the data-transfer byte 0x0f00025b and continue at 0x2568.
Command 06: clear the data-transfer byte 0x0f00025b and end the transfer at 0x2568.

Data commands pass their handler in r4 to the gate at 0x22fa: 0x22d6 for 02 (0x9292) and 0x22dc for 20 (0x9430). The group 6 and 7 tables send 61 and 63 to 0x22e2 and 0x22e8 (0x689c), 64 to 0x22ee (0x68d0) and 73 to 0x22f4 (0x95b8).
Gate: while byte 0x0f00025b is set, a transfer the host has not ended with 06, answer with the wait status at 0x91ec and post nothing. Otherwise call the handler in r4.
Data commands 02, 20, 61, 63, 64 and 73: wait status while a transfer is open, otherwise the handler. A data transfer request opens one.
A response with status bit 7 clear and bit 6 set (the data transfer request bit from 0x91a4) sets 0x0f00025b to 1.
Command ff subcode is r1 bits23..16: zero echoes r2 into both response longwords, one reads startup diagnostic longwords, other values return zero. No message.
Subcode0 echoes r2 twice, subcode1 returns startup diagnostic longwords, others return zero. Produces no message.
Reset transfer-related state at 0x0f000248..0x0f00025b. Byte 0x0f000258 becomes FF.

Transfer start, r11 = lock message: the owner task in bits 23..16 goes to 0x0f000256, the type in the low word. Status 0x0f00025a = 0. Type 0 sends one block from RAM, types 2 and 3 a partition's sectors to or from the host.
Start a transfer on DMA channel 1 under lock record 3: type 0 one RAM block to the host, type 2 a partition's sectors to the host, type 3 sectors from the host.
Types 2 and 3: a current slot 0x0f000258 of ff means no sector (0x2426). Otherwise 0x0f00024c points at the connection byte of 0x0f000259 (0x0f0005a0 + 4n, plus 1 for type 2).
Type 3, from the host: the slot's span for the put sector length (0x6e76), direction bit 1, CHCR1 0x435d, source 0x0a000000, destination the slot.
Type 2, to the host: the slot's span for the get sector length (0x6e18), direction bit 0, CHCR1 0x125d, source the slot, destination 0x0a000000.
The next slot from the links 0x0f000354 becomes current and 0x0f000257 counts one sector less.
No sector: status ff, 0x0a000002 = 8 with the direction bit (1 for type 3), 2 to 0x0a00001e and no DMA.
Type 0: no sectors (0x0f000257 = 0, 0x0f000258 = ff), the word count at 0x0f000254 from the address at 0x0f000250, CHCR1 0x125d.
Arm: the word count to 0x0f000248. 0x0a000002 = 2, then 0, with the direction bit. SAR1, DAR1, TCR1, then CHCR1 after reading it. 0x0a000002 = 4 with the direction bit and 2 to 0x0a00001e.
DMA channel 1 end (vector 74, ROM longword 0x0128): clear DE, TE and IE in CHCR1, switch to the stack 0x0f0009f8 with SR 0x60 and save r0..r9, PR, GBR and MACL.
DMA channel 1 end (vector 74): arm the next slot of a sector transfer, or mark the end, and return with RTE.
No sectors left (0x0f000257 = 0): 0x0a000002 = 8 with the direction bit. A current slot of ff, or a connection byte other than 0x88, is an error: status ff and no sectors left.
Direction bit 0 of 0x0a000002 clear, to the host: the next slot's span (0x6e18) to SAR1 and TCR1 and CHCR1 0x125d. Set, from the host: the span from 0x6e76 to DAR1 and TCR1 and CHCR1 0x435d.
The next slot becomes current, one sector less, and 0x0f000248 grows by the slot's words. Restore and return with RTE.
Command 06, end the transfer: CHCR1 = 0x1258 after reading it, the channel off. Without an owner answer ffffff with r11 = 0. After an error (status 0x0f00025a) answer ffffff and post to the owner.
Command 06: stop DMA channel 1, copy words the host sent past the channel, answer the words transferred and post the end to the owner.

r3 = the words left in TCR1. From the host (bit 0 of 0x0a000002) copy up to six words from 0x0a000000 onward from DAR1 while bit 2 of 0x0a000002 reads clear. A slot filled this way continues in the next one (0x263a).
0x0a000002 = 8. Answer the words transferred, 0x0f000248 less the words left, and return owner << 24 | 0x030001 in r11 for the owner. Clear the owner.

Next slot for the copy: with no sectors left answer. A current slot of ff or a connection byte other than 0x88 is an error. Otherwise the slot's span from 0x6e76, its words added to 0x0f000248, and up to five more words copied.
Task 6 uses state at 0x0f00025c. Save/restore incoming PR around the buffer-reset helper. Incoming GBR is not restored.
Task 6 initializes buffer metadata and local state, preserves diagnostic byte 0x0f00027d, updates device registers and waits on its internal mailbox. Setup posts no message.
Clear 0x0f00025c..0x0f000303 while retaining byte +33 (startup diagnostics). Set sentinel longwords +16/+20/+24/+28, then clear bytes +16/+24.
Fill six longwords at 0x09000218..0x0900022f with ffffffff. Set state byte +162 to ff.
Initialize 0x0f000304..0x0f000313 to longwords 0,0,255,0. Task 5 state starts immediately after this range.
Temporarily mask interrupts with SR | 0xf0. Replace register 0x0a00001a with (word & 0xffef) | 0x40, then restore the saved SR.
Write byte 0x30 to 0x05fffec2, OR 0x50 at 0x05ffff23 and OR 2 at 0x05ffff24. Readbacks are single accesses, not polling.
Internal mailbox wait via TRAPA 0x23, saved continuation 0x2798. Setup posts no message.
TRAPA 0x23 saves continuation 0x2798. After reset, task 14 runs next. Host commands, the end of a transfer, task 7, the sector buffer, task 5, the standby timer and the drive link post its messages.

Task 6 message dispatch after the wait at 0x2796 with GBR 0x0f00025c: r12 = message, r8 = class (r11 bits 23..16, sign-extended), r11 = payload low byte. Class 0x81 payload 12 goes to 0x35e4, 13 to 0x360e, and 0 calls 0x2d06 and waits again. Class 3 goes to 0x2866.
Task 6 continuation after its wait at 0x2796, GBR 0x0f00025c. In drive state 0 every message except a drive report waits again.
A drive report (class 0x83) with bit 5 of 0x0f0002a6 set and byte 0x0f0002cf not 1 clears bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 when it is set, otherwise bit 5.
Drive state byte 0x0f0002a5: state 0 continues at 0x2ad8 with r0 = class. States 17..22 use the table at 0x2818. Other states dispatch on the class from 0x2834.

Drive states other than 0 and 17..22 dispatch on class r8 with payload r11. Class 4 payloads 0..1 use the table at 0x2a30, class 5 payloads 0..4 0x29d0, class 7 payloads 0..4 0x29e4 and class 0x81 payloads 0..14 0x29f8. Class 6 indexes 0x29cc without a bound. Other classes and larger payloads wait again at 0x2796.
Task 6 in drive states other than 0 and 17..22: class 4, 5, 6, 7 and 0x81 messages through the tables at 0x29c8, drive reports (class 0x83) through 0x3aa8 and the periodic status.
Call the handler at table r0 + 4 * payload, then wait again. The tables are consecutive, so class 6 payload 1 reads the first class 5 entry.
Class 3 from 0x27d0: payload 1 releases lock 03060000 (record 3, owner task 6) with TRAPA 0x27, then task 6 waits again.
Class 0x83, a drive report: payload 0 calls 0x3aa8 from the table at 0x29c8. The periodic status at 0x28b0 follows.
Periodic status after a drive report. With interrupts masked, bit 4 of 0x0f000894 is copied to bit 4 of word 0x0a00001a. When it is set, bit 7 of 0x0f000894 sets or clears PB6 (bit 6 of 0x05ffffc3).
After each drive report: PB6 from the audio pre-emphasis bit in drive states 6 and 12, status words to CR1..CR4 when bit 1 of 0x0a000004 is set, and 0x0400 to 0x0a00001e.
Bit 4 of 0x0f000894 clear: clear bit 4 of 0x0a00001a. While bit 3 or 5 of 0x0f0002a6 is set, a command waits for its reply and PB6 is left alone.
Drive states 6 and 12 take PB6 from bit 4 of report byte 0x0f0002d1 when bit 2 of status byte 0x0f0002d0 is set and byte 0x0f0002d2 is nonzero. Other drive states clear PB6.

Status words for CR1..CR4. While bit 0 of busy flag 0x0f0007b0 is set they are 20ff ffff ffff ffff. Otherwise they come from the last status buffer written, 0x0f000274 when byte 0x0f00027c is nonzero or 0x0f00026c, with 0x2000 ORed into the first word.

A command waiting for its reply (bit 3 or 5 of 0x0f0002a6) clears bits 11..8 of the first word, the status code. Otherwise bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7 sets status code 9, low byte ff and the other words ffff.
With interrupts masked the four words go to CR1..CR4 (0x0a000010..0x0a000016) only when bit 1 of word 0x0a000004 is set. 0x0400 goes to 0x0a00001e and task 6 waits again at 0x2796.
Handler tables: class 0x83 at 0x29c8, class 6 at 0x29cc, class 5 at 0x29d0, class 7 at 0x29e4, class 0x81 at 0x29f8 and class 4 at 0x2a30.

With GBR selecting task6 state, fill 0x09000000..0x09000203 with ff. Clear bit7 of state +3, clear 0x09000210..0x09000217 (first word written twice) and longwords +132/+136/+140. Preserve PR/SP/GBR and all registers except r0/r1/r2 and T.
Fill 0x09000000..0x09000203 with ff, clear 0x09000210..0x09000217 and selected GBR-relative fields. Loops have fixed RAM endpoints, no external input.

Disc gone: notify task 5 through 0x3256, clear the TOC area through 0x2a38, post 07060000 to task 7 and write 0x0020 to 0x0a00001e. Keep bits 1, 3, 4 and 5 of 0x0f0002a6 and bit 4 of 0x0f0002a7, clear bits 7 and 6 of 0x0f00025f and cancel timer 06060000.
Disc gone: clear the TOC area, post 07060000 to task 7, write 0x0020 (DCHG) to 0x0a00001e and clear request flags.
Drive state 0: a drive report (class 0x83) with byte 0x0f0002db equal to 1 is examined from 0x2af2. Every other message waits again at 0x2796.
No branch reaches 0x2ae6..0x2af0: a check for an ADR 1 report that copies report byte 7 to 0x0f0002fe.
Report status byte 0x0f0002d0: 0x80, 0x81 and 0x83 go to 0x2bd6, 0x2bc8 and 0x2bea, 0x88..0x8f to 0x2bfa. Other values call 0x2ba0 with r0 = 1 and continue at 0x2bf4.

Drive states 17 and 18 (entered on status 81 and 80) from the table at 0x2818 with r0 = class. Class 0x81 payload 2 stages command 0c again in state 17 at 0x2c6c and only clears bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 in state 18. Other class 0x81 payloads are kept at 0x0f000280 and read the TOC: command 03, drive state 19, host status 0.

Drive states 17 and 18 (after status 81 and 80): Open Tray stages command 0c again in 17 and only clears busy in 18. Other host requests are kept and read the TOC with command 03, status 82 reads it, other reports pick the next drive state.
Class 7 payload 0 is kept and reads the TOC the same way. Other class 7 payloads and other classes wait again at 0x2796.

A valid report: status 82 reads the TOC in drive state 19 without keeping a message. 80 sets drive state 18 and 81 state 17, without the disc-gone reset. 83 and 88..8f set drive state 20. Any other status reads the TOC with drive state 21. An invalid report goes to the periodic status.
From 0x2cc6: status codes 3 and 5 set drive state 0x99 and host status 10 at 0x2bfa. Other codes go to the periodic status.
Command 03 (read TOC): byte 1 and byte 0x0f000289 (the session to read, 1 for the first) from r0, bytes 8..11 0000ff01. Setting bit 5 of 0x0f00025f makes byte 10 2. Staged through 0x325a.
Stage command 03 (read TOC) with the session in byte 1 and 0x0f000289.
Status 81, or command 0c staged: the disc-gone reset at 0x2a90, drive state 17 and host status 0. 0x2bd0 skips the reset.
Status 80: the disc-gone reset, drive state 18 and host status 6. 0x2bde skips the reset.
TOC read from drive state 17 or 18: drive state 19, host status 0.
Status 83: clear the kept message 0x0f000280, drive state 20 and host status 7.

Drive state 21, host status 0. Drive states 0 (0x2b16), 17 and 18 (0x2b8c) come here after staging command 03 at 0x2ba0. Status code 1 in drive states 19, 21 and 22 comes here from 0x2cc0 and stages no command.
Error: drive state 0x99, host status 10.

Store drive state r0 and host status r1, then reset the status buffers at 0x450a (entry 0x2c00) or store the status code at 0x44f4 (entry 0x2c06). A report continues to the periodic status, anything else waits again.
Status code 0 in drive states 19, 21 and 22: drive state 21, host status 0, store the status code and collect the TOC at 0x3858.

Clear bit 4 of 0x0f0002a7. T = 1 for a report whose checksum matched (0x0f0002db = 1) while bit 5 of 0x0f0002a6 is clear. A staged command sets bits 3 and 5, and 0x2798 clears bit 3 at the report of the frame that sent the command and bit 5 at the next, so the next frame's report is the first reply taken.
A report is taken only when its checksum matched and no staged command is still waiting for the report after the one that carried it.
Drive states 19, 21 and 22. Class 0x81 payload 2 stages command 0c and continues at 0x2bc8. Other class 0x81 payloads clear bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 and are kept at 0x0f000280 for later.
Drive states 19, 21 and 22 (TOC read and the seek after it): host requests are kept for later, status code 0 collects the TOC, code 9 ends it, code 4 in state 22 completes the seek.
Command 0c: bytes 0..10 are 0c and zeros, pending byte 1. Continue at 0x2bc8 with drive state 17.
Class 7 payload 0 is kept the same way. Other class 7 payloads and other classes wait.

A valid report: status 80, 81, 83 and 88..8f as in drive state 0. Status code 0 collects the TOC at 0x2c24, code 9 ends it at 0x39ec and code 1 sets drive state 21. Code 4 in drive state 22 completes the seek after the TOC at 0x3a84. Codes 3 and 5 are errors through 0x2b90, other codes go to the periodic status.
Drive state 20 (status 83): class 0x81 requests and class 7 payload 0 stage command 0c at 0x2c6c. Other class 7 payloads wait. Other messages are handled as in drive states 19, 21 and 22.

Class 0x81 payload 0, called from 0x27bc in every drive state: clear bytes 0x0f00025c and 0x0f00025d, longwords 0x0f000260, 0x0f000264, 0x0f000268, 0x0f000298 and 0x0f00029c and byte 0x0f00028b. Keep only bits 3 and 5 of 0x0f0002a6 and bit 4 of 0x0f0002a7.
Class 0x81 payload 0: clear the play settings and restart the other tasks through TRAPA 0x2e with interrupts masked.
Save IPRA..IPRD (0x05ffff84..0x05ffff8b), clear them and call TRAPA 0x2e, which restarts the other tasks. Then restore them and GBR and write 0x0bc1 to 0x0a00001e.
Host status 0, 6 or 7: clear bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 and return. Other host statuses continue as payload 8 at 0x30b8.
Class 0x81 payload 1 returns at once.

Class 0x81 payload 2: while bit 6 of 0x0f00025f is set, clear it and longwords 0x0f000298 and 0x0f00029c and post 07060003 to task 7. Then the disc-gone reset at 0x2a90, command 0c, drive state 17, host status 0 and a status buffer reset through 0x364c.
Class 0x81 payload 2: the disc-gone reset and command 0c, drive state 17.

Class 0x81 payload 3, play between track positions: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7. Bits 6..0 of byte 0x0f00025d, when 15 or less, become the repeat limit in the top byte of 0x0f00029c. Clear repeat count 0x0f00028b. Range start 0x0f000298 is 0x0f000264 with top byte 1 (track form), range end 0x0f00029c is 0x0f000268 below the repeat limit.
Class 0x81 payload 3: play range between track positions from 0x0f000264 and 0x0f000268.
Seek (command 09) to frame r0, which callers also store as the target 0x0f0002a0, with r7 = r8 = 0. 0x2df4 enters with a track and index in r3 and converts them through 0x326a.
Stage command 09 (seek) to frame r0, also kept as the target 0x0f0002a0. Drive state 4, host status 4.
Clear bit 2 of 0x0f0002a6. Target ffffff becomes the lead-out frame (low 24 bits of 0x090001fc) and target 0 becomes 150. Host status 0x0f00028a = 4.

Set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 and build the host status from the target through 0x3640. Stage command 09 with the frame in bytes 1..3, r7 in bytes 4..7 and r8 in byte 8 through 0x325a, after the task 5 notification 0x3256. Drive state 4, cancel timer 06060000, set bit 7 of 0x0f0002a6 and clear bits 6 and 0.

End of the play range: a zero end is the lead-out frame, a track-form start gives ffffffff, otherwise the end clamped to the lead-out through 0x35cc. It goes to 0x0f000284 and 0x0f0002dc becomes ffffffff. Bit 7 of byte 0x0f00025d set continues at 0x2ed6, clear at 0x2f00.

Class 0x81 payload 5, play the current range: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7. Bits 6..0 of 0x0f00025d of 7f keep the repeat limit and count. Otherwise a value of 15 or less becomes the limit and the count is cleared.
Class 0x81 payload 5: play the current range, keeping the position when bit 7 of 0x0f00025d is set.

Bit 7 of 0x0f00025d set: while playing (host status 3) only clear bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6. Paused or in standby (host status 1 or 2) with bit 0 of 0x0f0002a6 clear, reset 0x0f0002dc and byte 0x0f00025e and check the range at 0x2f3a. Otherwise continue at 0x2f0e.
Start of the range: clear bit 7 of 0x0f00025d and store the range start as the target through 0x3530.

Play from the target: 0x0f0002dc ffffffff, byte 0x0f00025e 0. A track-form target copies its track and index to 0x0f00028d and 0x0f00028e, a frame target of 0 becomes 150. When the target and range start forms differ the read starts at 0x2f5c at once.

Same form: 0x32c4 checks the target against the range. Inside, read at 0x2f5c. Outside with bit 7 of 0x0f00025d clear, seek to the target at 0x30e2. With it set, 0x3dac counts a repeat and restarts from the range start, or pauses at 0x30b8 when the repeats are used up.

Read (command 06) from target frame 0x0f0002a0. Longword 0x0f0002dc becomes ffffffff. With byte 0x0f0002a0 equal to 1 the target holds a track and index, converted through 0x326a. Target ffffff seeks to the lead-out at 0x2dee instead.
Stage command 06 (read) from target frame 0x0f0002a0. Drive state 4, host status 4 or 8.
Host status 0x0f00028a: 8 when bit 2 of 0x0f0002a7 is set, otherwise 4. Set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 and build the host status through 0x3640.
With bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7 or bit 6 of 0x0f00028c set, a frame target (not a track) moves by signed byte 0x0f0002a4 minus 1.

Stage command 06 with the frame in bytes 1..3, r7 in bytes 4..7 and r8 in byte 8 through 0x325a, after the task 5 notification 0x3256 unless byte 0x0f00025e is 6. Drive state 4, cancel timer 06060000, keep bits 1, 3, 4 and 5 of 0x0f0002a6.
Class 0x81 payload 4, play between frames: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7, update the repeat limit and count as for payload 3 and take the range start from 0x0f000264 through 0x3510.
Class 0x81 payload 4: play range from a start frame and a frame count.
When the first track is track 1 and the start lies more than 2250 frames before track 1, set bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7.

End: 0x0f000268 of 0 stores 0 and 00ffffff keeps the old end. Otherwise bits 22..0 count frames from the start (from 150 when the start is 0). The repeat limit stays in the top byte. Continue at 0x2e7c.
Class 0x81 payload 6, seek to a track position: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7, store 0x0f000264 as a track-form target through 0x3530 and seek at 0x2df4.
Class 0x81 payload 6: seek to a track position.
Class 0x81 payload 7, seek to a frame: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7, store the frame from 0x0f000264 (0x3510) as the target (0x3530) and seek at 0x2dee.
Class 0x81 payload 7: seek to a frame.

Class 0x81 payload 8, pause: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7. In drive state 10 a set bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 is cleared with bit 7 and posts 05060003 to task 5, then the pause is issued at 0x312a in drive state 10.
Class 0x81 payload 8: pause, or seek to the target when neither playing nor reading.
Host status 1: the same notification, then pause at 0x3106. Host status 3, or bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 set: pause at 0x3106. Otherwise seek to the target.
Seek to the target: track form at 0x2df4, frame form at 0x2dee.
Pause. With bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 set: drive state 10, clear bits 7 and 6 and post 05060003 to task 5. Otherwise a set bit 1 is cleared and posts 05060007, and the drive state is 5.
Stage command 08 (pause). Drive state 5 or 10, host status 1.

Host status 1, set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6, store the status code through 0x3648 and stage command 08 through 0x325a. Cancel timer 06060000, set bit 7 of 0x0f0002a6 and clear bits 6, 2 and 0. Drive state 5 continues at 0x4012.

Class 0x81 payload 9, stop: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7 and the target, host status 2, reset the status buffers, drive state 9. Stage command 04 after the task 5 notification, cancel timer 06060000, set bits 7 and 0 of 0x0f0002a6 and clear bits 6 and 2.
Class 0x81 payload 9: command 04, drive state 9, host status 2.

Class 6 payload 0, the standby timer expired, only while bit 6 of 0x0f0002a6 shows it running: host status 2, set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6, store the status code and stage command 05. Drive state 8, cancel timer 06060000, clear bits 6 and 2 of 0x0f0002a6.
Class 6 payload 0, the standby timer expired: command 05, drive state 8, host status 2.

Class 0x81 payload 10, scan forward: clear bit 4 of 0x0f0002a6 (payload 11 at 0x3250 sets it). Set bit 2 of 0x0f0002a6, clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7, cancel timer 06060000 and clear bit 6 of 0x0f0002a6.
Class 0x81 payloads 10 and 11: scan forward or backward with command 0a or 0b.
Host status 3 or 5 starts the scan at 0x4064. Host status 1 or 2 with a frame target seeks to it through 0x2e08, and the scan starts when the target is reached. Otherwise clear bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6.
Class 0x81 payload 11, scan backward: set bit 4 of 0x0f0002a6 and continue at 0x320c.
Shared jumps: 0x3256 to 0x418c, 0x325a to 0x4148, 0x325e to 0x2798, 0x3262 to 0x28b0 and 0x3266 to 0x2a90.
Frame of track r3, index r4, from the TOC entry through 0x420a. A data track (control bit 6) with index 0 or 1 returns its start frame with r4 = r8 = 0.
Start frame of a track and the index and end for a track-form command.
Otherwise index 0 becomes 1 on an audio track. r4 becomes the index in bits 31..24 over the start of the next track (the lead-out after the last track), r8 the track and r0 the track's start frame.

Is the target 0x0f0002a0 inside the play range 0x0f000298..0x0f00029c? T = 1 inside. Outside, r0 = 1 when the target lies before the start and 0 otherwise. Always inside while bit 6 of 0x0f00025f is set.
T = 1 when the target lies inside the play range 0x0f000298..0x0f00029c.

Frame-form range: a track-form target is inside. A frame target must satisfy start <= target < end, with a start of 0 read as 150, an end of 0 as the lead-out and both clamped to the lead-out through 0x35cc.

Track-form range, frame target: the target must reach 0x0f0002dc when that is set, 150 for a start of 0, or the start of the range's first track (clamped to the disc's tracks) for a data track at index 0 or 1. Otherwise 0x3470 compares tracks.
Track and index compare: the start (track 0 is the first track, index 0 is 1, clamped to the disc's tracks) must not lie after the current track and index at 0x0f00028d and 0x0f00028e.

End check. A zero end on a data track needs the target below the lead-out. In track 0 or the lead-out the target's track from 0x421e must lie before the end track. Otherwise the current track and index must not pass the end (track 0 is the last track, index 0 is 99).
Current track 0 with target 0 lies before the start. Otherwise the target's track from 0x421e must reach the range's first track.
Start frame from 0x0f000264: 0 stays 0, anything else is bits 22..0, at least 150.
Store position r0 as the target 0x0f0002a0 and return it. Bits 23..0 of 0 give frame 150. Top byte 0 is a frame, clamped to the lead-out through 0x35cc.
Normalize a frame or track position and store it as the target 0x0f0002a0.

Top byte nonzero is a track form: an index above 99 becomes 99 and 0 becomes 1. Track 0 is the first track. A track before the first or after the last becomes that track at index 1. The top byte becomes 1.
Clamp r0 to the lead-out frame, the low 24 bits of 0x090001fc.

Class 0x81 payload 12, from 0x27ca in every drive state: take lock 03060000 (TRAPA 0x2a) and send 5 words of the last Q record (0x0900021a when byte 0x0f000288 is 0, otherwise 0x09000226) through 0x23ba with the address at 0x0f000250 and the count at 0x0f000254. Then wait again.
Class 0x81 payloads 12 and 13: send the Q record or the TOC through 0x23ba.
Class 0x81 payload 13: the same with 0xcc words of the TOC from 0x09000068.
Status jumps: 0x363c to 0x420a, 0x3640 to 0x4300, 0x3644 to 0x43c4, 0x3648 to 0x44f4 and 0x364c to 0x450a.
No code calls this jump.

Class 5 payload 0 from task 5, only while reading (bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 set, bit 7 clear): set bit 2 of 0x0f0002a7. With bit 4 set, byte 0x0f0002a4 becomes frame 0x0f000294 minus 0x0f0002b0. Read mode byte 0x0f00025e 2, target 0x0f0002b4, clear bit 6 and read again at 0x2f5c.
Class 5 payload 0 from task 5: read again from 0x0f0002b4.
Store r0 as target frame 0x0f0002a0 and read from it at 0x2f5c.
Shared return of the class 5 handlers.
Class 5 payload 1 has no effect.

Class 5 payload 2, while reading: set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 and bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7 (status code 9 in the periodic status) and clear bits 6, 5 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7. While bit 6 of 0x0f00025f is set, clear it and 0x0f000298 and 0x0f00029c and post 07060003 to task 7. Pause at 0x312a in drive state 10.
Class 5 payload 2 from task 5: read error, status code 9, pause.
Class 5 payload 3, while reading: with bit 4 of 0x0f0002a7 set, byte 0x0f0002a4 becomes frame 0x0f000294 minus 0x0f0002b0.
Class 5 payload 4, while reading: as payload 0 with read mode 8.

Class 7 payload 0: clear longwords 0x0f000298 and 0x0f00029c, set 0x0f000284 to ffffffff and byte 0x0f00025e to 1, set bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7 and clear bits 3 and 2. Read from request frame 0x0f0002bc, or from the frame at 0x09000214 plus 166 when the request frame is 0.
Class 7 payload 0: read from request frame 0x0f0002bc, or from a default frame when it is 0.
Class 7 payload 1, a header was recognized: clear bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7 and pause at 0x3106.
Class 7 payload 1, sent after a disc header was recognized: pause (command 08).

Class 7 payload 2, a sector request: clear 0x0f000298, set 0x0f000284 to ffffffff, 0x0f00029c to 00ffffff and byte 0x0f00025e to 1. Set bit 6 of 0x0f00025f (disc authentication owns the drive) and bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7, clear bits 3 and 2, and read from request frame 0x0f0002bc.
Class 7 payload 2, a sector request: read (command 06) from request frame 0x0f0002bc, with the disc-authentication flag set.
Third failed ring seek, from 0x4134, or a read with no sector by its 150th report under authentication, from 0x3f38: post 07060003 to task 7.

Give-up after three failed ring seeks, or a read with no sector by its 150th report under authentication (post 07060003), and class 7 payload 3 at 0x3754: clear the request flags and seek back with command 09.
Class 7 payload 3, request complete: clear 0x0f000298 and 0x0f00029c, bit 6 of 0x0f00025f and bits 5, 3 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7. Seek to the frame at 0x09000214 plus 150 at 0x2dee.
Class 7 payload 4, an authentication seek: set bit 6 of 0x0f00025f, clear retry count 0x0f0002fa, set drive state 0x21 and copy request frame 0x0f0002bc to target frame 0x0f0002a0.
Class 7 payload 4, an authentication seek: drive state 0x21, request frame 0x0f0002bc copied to target frame 0x0f0002a0, and command 02 to the target frame. Retries enter at 0x3788.
Retries enter here. Clear report word 0x0f00027e, notify task 5 through 0x418c and set bit 5 of 0x0f00025f, which makes byte 10 of the command 2.
Stage command 02 with the target frame in bytes 1..3 through 0x4148. Cancel timer 06060000 and keep bits 1, 3, 4 and 5 of 0x0f0002a6.

Class 4 payload 0 and class 0x81 payload 14, while a read is held (bits 6 and 7 of 0x0f0002a7 set): the target becomes the last delivered frame, bits 23..0 of 0x0f0002ac. Inside the play range (0x32c4) read again from 0x0f0002c0 with read mode 6.
Class 4 payload 0: a read held for a full buffer continues from 0x0f0002c0.
Outside the range: 0x3dac counts a repeat and restarts at 0x2f00, or pauses at 0x30b8 when the repeats are used up.

Class 4 payload 1, while reading (bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 set, bit 7 clear): the target becomes the last delivered frame. Outside the range as at 0x37ec. Inside, set bit 7 of 0x0f0002a7, drive state 10, post 05060009 to task 5 and pause at 0x312a.
Class 4 payload 1: hold the read and pause in drive state 10.

Next session: command 03 for the session in 0x0f000289 through 0x2ba0, copy entry A1 (0x090001f8) to 0x0900020c and reset entries A0..A2 (0x090001f4..0x090001ff) to ffffffff. Continue at the periodic status.
Read the TOC of the next session announced by a B0 pointer.

TOC reports in drive state 21 need status bit 2 and track byte 0 (the lead-in). Count the report in 0x0f0002e0, and in 0x0f0002e4 when status bit 3 is set, otherwise in 0x0f0002e8. Other reports go to the periodic status.

Lead-in Q reports: counts them in 0x0f0002e0 (bit 3 of the status in 0x0f0002e4, otherwise 0x0f0002e8), stores track, A0, A1 and A2 entries, B0 session pointers, and seeks to the first frame when the TOC is complete.
ADR 1 (ADR 5 continues at 0x39b0): copy report byte 7 to 0x0f0002fe. The point (byte 3, BCD) must be 1..99, points A0..A2 continue at 0x39f4.

Track entry r1: the start (bytes 8..10, BCD minutes, seconds and frames) as a frame through 0x41b6 with control/ADR (byte 1) in bits 31..24, stored through 0x4214. Point A2 arrives with r1 = 102 and stores the lead-out through 0x3a46.

Complete when entries A2 (0x090001fc), A0 (0x090001f4) and A1 (0x090001f8) are set, the last track (byte 0x090001f9) is not below the first (0x090001f5) and every track entry from the first to the last is set. Otherwise wait for more reports.

Disc type 0x10 (byte 0x090001f6): the session's first track is the previous session's last track (word 0x0900020c), plus 1 for an audio track. With a single track whose A1 control has bit 6, the track entries are not checked.

Session done: store r4, the session's first track, at byte 0x09000000 + session number 0x0f000289 (1 for the first) and count on. With bit 7 of 0x0f00025f set (set by a B0 pointer and kept until the TOC is cleared), read the next session at 0x382c. Only status code 9 then ends the TOC.

TOC complete: entries A0..A2 come back from 0x09000200..0x0900020b (the first A0, the last A1 and A2). Byte 0x09000000 becomes the number of the last session. Entry 0 (0x09000064) becomes the lead-out when unset, with that number in its top byte.
Byte 0x0f0002a4 0, target 150 plus the frame at 0x09000214 and seek there at 0x2e2c (r6 = target, r7 = r8 = 0), then drive state 22.

ADR 5, point B0: store the frame from bytes 8..10 at entry 0 (0x09000064), and the frame from bytes 4..6 at 0x09000210 when it is larger than the one there, which moves to 0x09000214. Set bit 7 of 0x0f00025f, which marks a disc with more than one session.
Status code 9 from 0x2cd2: the TOC ends with the sessions read so far at 0x395e.

Points A0 and A1: control/ADR (byte 1), PMIN (byte 8, BCD to binary) and bytes 9..10 unchanged go to entry 0x090001f4 (A0) or 0x090001f8 (A1). The entry 12 bytes on keeps the first A0 and the latest A1 and A2. Point A2 continues at 0x38ac as track 102.

Status code 4 in drive state 22, the seek after the TOC: 0x3c74 takes the position (drive state 11) and 07060001 goes to task 7. A host request kept at 0x0f000280 is cleared and dispatched again through 0x325e. Otherwise the periodic status follows.
The seek after the TOC settled: drive state 11, 07060001 to task 7 and a kept host request dispatched again.

Class 0x83 in a served drive state. 0x2c44 rejects a report with a bad checksum or while bit 5 of 0x0f0002a6 is set. Status codes other than 8 (bits 7..4 of 0x0f0002d0) continue at 0x3b48 with the code in r2.
Report in a served drive state. Status code 8 stops the drive: task 7 is told when disc authentication owns the drive, then disc-gone or error handling. Other codes continue at 0x3b48.
Status code 8: notify task 5 through 0x418c. While bit 6 of 0x0f00025f is set (disc authentication owns the drive), clear it and longwords 0x0f000298 and 0x0f00029c and post 07060003 to task 7.
Low nibble 3, or 8 and above: drive state 0x99 and host status 10. Other values: disc-gone reset at 0x2a90, a cleared command (pending byte 0), drive state 0x12 and host status 6.
Store drive state r0 and host status r1, clear bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7, cancel timer 06060000, clear bit 6 of 0x0f0002a6 and target 0x0f0002a0, then reset the status buffers at 0x450a.

Drive report dispatch in task 6 with GBR 0x0f00025c: r2 = report status byte 0x0f0002d0 >> 4. Drive state byte 0x0f0002a5 values 4..12 select handlers from the table at 0x3b7c, 0x21 continues at 0x40d0 and other states return.
Drive report in task 6 by drive state 0x0f0002a5. State 0x21 (authentication seek) continues at 0x40d0.
Report handlers for drive states 4..12.
Drive state 4 (seek or read issued), status code in r2: code 3 starts the read at 0x3bc4, code 4 ends a seek or pause at 0x3c74, code 1 is an error at 0x3bb6. Others return.
An entry with no known caller: store r0 as the host status and continue at 0x44f4.
Status code 1 in drive states 4 and 0x21: notify task 5 through 0x418c, then drive state 0x99 and host status 10 at 0x3b16.
Status code 3 in drive state 4, the drive reads: clear frame 0x0f000294 and word 0x0f000300.
Status code 3 in drive state 4: start sector delivery through task 5 (05060000 plus the read mode) and set drive state 12.

No position (status bit 2 clear): bits 7 or 2 of 0x0f0002a6 only set drive state 12. When bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7 or bit 6 of 0x0f00028c is set, a frame target starts delivery at 0x3c2e and a track target waits for a position. Otherwise audio delivery is checked at 0x3c5a.

With a position the frame comes from the Q report through 0x42bc. Bits 7 or 2 of 0x0f0002a6 only set drive state 12. Without bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7, an audio track (bit 6 of 0x0f00028c clear) goes to 0x3c54 and a data track whose Q control lacks bit 6 only sets drive state 12.
A frame target starts delivery at 0x3c2e. A track target needs Q ADR 1 and becomes the frame plus 5, also kept in 0x0f0002dc unless bit 7 of 0x0f00025d is set.

Start delivery: the target goes to 0x0f0002b8 and 0x0f0002ac, 0x0f0002b0 is cleared and 05060000 plus read mode byte 0x0f00025e goes to task 5. Set bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 (reading), and for read mode 6 clear bit 7.
Drive state 12.
Audio: a Q control with bit 6 only sets drive state 12. Otherwise, with bit 1 of 0x0f00025c set, post 05060005 to task 5 and set bit 1 of 0x0f0002a7.
Status code 4 after a seek or pause (bit 7 of 0x0f0002a6 set): clear frame 0x0f000294. With status bit 2 take the frame from the Q report (0x42bc) and set drive state 11.
Status code 4 after a seek or pause: take the position and set drive state 11.
Drive state 5 (paused): status code 1 is an error at 0x3bb6, others return.
Drive state 6 (playing, host status 3): status codes 3 and 4 follow the position at 0x3cc2, code 1 is an error.
Playing: follow the position, read again after a jump, stop or repeat at the end of the play range.

Without status bit 2 only a read in progress (bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7) continues at 0x3d04. With it the frame comes from 0x42bc. Unless reading, in track 0 or in the lead-out, a jump (0x3de2) sets bit 2 of 0x0f0002a7 and reads again from the old frame plus 30.
Update the status from the report through 0x43c4. Outside the play range 0x3dac repeats from the range start at 0x2f00 or pauses at 0x3106.

Inside the range at index 0 of a track: when its data bit differs from the previous track's, or for the first track on a disc of type 0x10, play on at 0x2f0e with bit 7 of 0x0f00025d set, from the track's start frame for a data track or from index 1 through 0x3530 otherwise.
Repeat: while count 0x0f00028b is below the limit (top byte of 0x0f00029c), count one more (up to 14) and return T = 0. At the limit set bit 0 of 0x0f0002a7 and return T = 1.
The same check without counting.
T = 1 when frame r0 lies before r9 or more than 75 frames after it.

Drive state 7 (scanning, host status 5): status code 5 follows the position at 0x3e12. Code 4 ends the scan: 0x3dcc checks the repeats, bit 7 of 0x0f0002a6 is set and the pause completes at 0x3ff0. Code 1 is an error.

Scanning with status bit 2: frame from 0x42bc and status from 0x43c4. A Q control whose bit 6 differs from 0x0f00028c restarts the scan at 0x4064. Past the play range 0x3dcc checks the repeats and the pause is issued at 0x3106.
Drive state 8 (standby) ignores reports.
Drive state 9 (stopped) ignores reports.
Drive state 10 (paused after a read): status code 4 completes the pause with drive state 5, host status 1 and a status copy with the last delivered frame (0x4558). Code 1 is an error.

Inside the play range, or with repeats left and bit 7 of 0x0f0002a7 set, start the standby timer at 0x4012. Otherwise a read still marked in bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 ends: clear bits 7 and 6 and post 05060003 to task 5.
Drive state 11 (seek settled): status code 4 follows the position at 0x3ed4, code 1 is an error.
Drive states 11 and 12: follow the position until the target is reached, seek again after a jump, end a read after 150 reports without a sector.
Drive state 12 (read started): status code 3 follows the position at 0x3ed4, code 1 is an error.
Keep the old frame in r9. A report with status bit 2 and ADR 1 sets the frame through 0x42bc. Otherwise a known frame counts up by one and bit 4 of 0x0f0002a7 is set.
While reading (bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 set, bit 7 clear): once task 5 has set 0x0f0002b0, the target is reached when 0x0f0002b0 is at or past it. Until then word 0x0f000300 counts reports.
