The 150th such report is a read error: set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 and 0x0f0002a7, clear bits 7, 6, 5 and 2 of 0x0f0002a7 and post 05060003 to task 5. With disc authentication owning the drive the request is given up at 0x3750, otherwise pause at 0x312a in drive state 5.
Not reading: from a known old frame, a jump (0x3de2) seeks again. Set bit 2 of 0x0f0002a7, host status 8 and stage command 09 (06 in drive state 12) to the old frame plus 30 in drive state 4.
The target is reached when the frame is at or past a frame target, or when the Q track and index (status bit 2, ADR 1) are at or past those at 0x0f00028d and 0x0f00028e for a track target.
Target reached: pause in drive state 5, play on in drive state 6 or start a scan.
Target reached: clear bit 2 of 0x0f0002a7. A scan (bit 2 of 0x0f0002a6) starts at 0x4064, drive state 12 plays on at 0x4058.
Otherwise pause: drive state 5, host status 1 and the status from the report. Outside the play range 0x3dcc marks the end of the repeats. The standby timer follows at 0x4012.

Drive state 5 after a pause: a set bit 0 of 0x0f0002a7 is cleared and writes 0x0010 to 0x0a00001e. Unless bit 6 of 0x0f0002a6 is set, start timer 06060000 for word 0x0f000260 * 10000 time units (180 when the word is 0) and set that bit.
In drive state 5, start standby timer 06060000 for word 0x0f000260 seconds (180 when 0).
Drive state 12 at the target: drive state 6, host status 3, and follow the play at 0x3cc2.

Scan: outside the play range 0x3dcc checks the repeats and the pause is issued at 0x3106. Inside: drive state 7, host status 5, set bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6, store the status code and notify task 5 (0x418c).
Stage command 0a, or 0b with bit 4 of 0x0f0002a6 set, with byte 1 = 1 when bit 7 of 0x0f0002a6 is set and bytes 8..11 0000ff01.
Drive state 0x21 (seek for disc authentication): status 11 continues at 0x40e2, status 1 at 0x3bb6, other values return.

Authentication seek report. At the target position 0x0f0002a0 with bit 2 of the status byte set, report word 0x0f0002d1 goes to 0x0f00027e, words 0x0f0002d6 and 0x0f0002d8 go to 0x0f0002ec and 0x0f0002ee, and 07060002 is posted to task 7. Words 0 and ffff seek again 206 frames further on, twice at most, and the third such report gives up at 0x3750.
Requires bit 2 of the status byte and a report position (0x0f0002d3..0x0f0002d5, 24 bits) equal to the seek target 0x0f0002a0. Otherwise returns and waits for the next report.

Report word from bytes 0x0f0002d1..0x0f0002d2. 0 or ffff retries at 0x4120. Otherwise store it at 0x0f00027e, copy words 0x0f0002d6 and 0x0f0002d8 to 0x0f0002ec and 0x0f0002ee, post 07060002 (task 7, class 6, payload 2) and set drive state 0x22.
Retry count byte 0x0f0002fa: the third such report gives up at 0x3750. Otherwise the seek target advances by 206 frames and the seek is issued again at 0x3788.

Stage a drive command: longwords r1, r2 and r3 become command bytes 0..11 at 0x0f0002c4..0x0f0002cf. Byte 11 (0x0f0002cf) is the pending flag the link reads. It is cleared first, and bits 3 and 5 of 0x0f0002a6 are set.
Copy r1, r2 and r3 to command bytes 0x0f0002c4..0x0f0002cf. Byte 10 becomes 1 or 2, byte 11 is the pending flag the link reads.

Byte 10 is masked with 2 when bit 5 of 0x0f00025f was set (and clears it). Otherwise it is masked with 1 when bit 4 of 0x0f00025c is set, with 2 when bit 5 of 0x0f0002a7 or bit 6 of 0x0f00028c is set, and with 1 when neither is.
Notify task 5: a set bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7 posts 05060003 and clears bits 7 and 6. Otherwise a set bit 1 is cleared and posts 05060007.
Post 05060003 or 05060007 to task 5 by bits 6 and 1 of 0x0f0002a7.
BCD byte at r3 to binary in r0.
BCD to binary, and BCD minutes, seconds and frames to a frame count at 0x41b6.
BCD minutes, seconds and frames at r3..r3+2 to a frame count: 4500 * minutes + 75 * seconds + frames.
TOC longword for track r1 at 0x09000064 + 4 * r1. Index 102 is the lead-out entry 0x090001fc.
Store r2 as the TOC longword for track r1 at 0x09000064 + 4 * r1.

Track of frame r0 from the TOC: track r1 and offset r0 within it. At or past the lead-out (low 24 bits of 0x090001fc) r1 = 0xaa and r0 counts frames past it. Before the first track r0 counts frames to its start.
Track and offset of a frame from the TOC at 0x09000064, lead-out 0xaa.
When byte 0x090001f6 is 0x10, frames from 150 up to the first track's start belong to track 1. A frame below 150 then returns r0 = 150 - frame and leaves the address 0x090001f6 in r1.
Walk the tracks from the first (byte 0x090001f5) to the last (byte 0x090001f9) while the next track starts at or before the frame.
Frame from a Q report with ADR 1: set bit 4 of 0x0f0002a7 and store the absolute time (bytes 8..10) as frame 0x0f000294.
Frame 0x0f000294 from the absolute time of a Q report.
In the lead-in (track byte 0) the frame is 0, or while bit 7 of 0x0f00025f is set the relative time (bytes 4..6) up to 360000 frames.

Host status for target frame 0x0f0002a0. Bit 0 of byte 0x0f0002a0 selects the track form at 0x4354. A frame of 0 becomes 150 and goes to 0x0f000294. The track goes to 0x0f00028d, the offset to 0x0f000290 and index 1 to 0x0f00028e.
Host status words and Q record for target frame 0x0f0002a0.
Track 0xaa (lead-out) reads its control byte from TOC index 102. Track 1 on a disc with byte 0x090001f6 = 0x10 uses control 41.
Track form: track byte 0x0f0002a2 and index byte 0x0f0002a3, frame 0x0f000294 from the track's TOC entry, offset 0.

Control/ADR to 0x0f00028c and 0 to 0x0f00028f. A Q record (control/ADR, track, index and offset, frame) goes to 0x09000218 when byte 0x0f000288 is 1, otherwise 0x09000224, and the byte toggles. The status words follow at 0x44a6.
Advance the position by one frame: frame 0x0f000294, offset 0x0f000290 and a frame-form target 0x0f0002a0.

Host status bytes from a drive report. Without status bit 2 only the Q record and status words are written again at 0x437c. While reading (bit 6 of 0x0f0002a7) the frame is the last delivered one, 0x0f0002ac, with its top byte as the flags 0x0f00028f. Otherwise the frame is 0x0f000294 and the flags 0. The frame also becomes the target 0x0f0002a0.
Host status bytes and Q record from a drive report.

ADR 1: the track (BCD, or aa) to 0x0f00028d, the relative time to offset 0x0f000290 (0 in the lead-in), the index (BCD, kept from 9a up) to 0x0f00028e, and report byte 1 to 0x0f00028c, or 0x29 at or past the lead-out while bit 6 of 0x0f00025f is set. Continue at 0x437c.

Other ADR values: in host status 3 while not reading, advance the position (0x43a8). Copy report bytes 1..10 to the Q record (0x0900021a when byte 0x0f000288 is 1, otherwise 0x09000226), flip the byte and store the status words at 0x44a6.

Status words: host status 0x0f00028a and flags 0x0f00028b ORed with 0x0f00028f, control/ADR 0x0f00028c and track 0x0f00028d, then index 0x0f00028e with the frame (0x0f0002a0, or 0x0f000294 in the track form).
Write the eight status bytes to the next of the buffers 0x0f00026c and 0x0f000274.
Write to 0x0f000274 when bit 0 of 0x0f00027c is clear, otherwise 0x0f00026c, then toggle the bit. 0x28b0 sends the buffer written last.
Store host status 0x0f00028a in the first byte of the buffer written last: 0x0f000274 when bit 0 of 0x0f00027c is set, otherwise 0x0f00026c.

Reset the status buffers: the next buffer becomes ffffffff ffffffff with host status 0x0f00028a in its first byte and bit 0 of 0x0f00027c toggles. The next Q record (0x09000218 when byte 0x0f000288 is 1, otherwise 0x09000224) becomes ff and the byte toggles.
Reset the next status buffer and Q record to ff with the host status code.

Copy the status buffer written last into the other with frame bytes 5..7 from the last delivered frame (0x0f0002ac bits 23..0, also the target) and byte 0 from host status 0x0f00028a, then flip bit 0 of 0x0f00027c.
Write zero to 0x0a00000a then 0x0a000006. Clear the low three bits of 0x0a00001a and replace the low nibble of 0x05ffff86 with 8, preserving upper bits.

Task 5 initializes device registers and local queue state, takes two indices from the shared pool, and waits on its mailbox. Task 6's read requests, the decoder interrupt, the end of DMA channel 0, task 1 and command 30 post its messages.
Clear twelve words at 0x0f000314..0x0f000343. Install ff sentinels at +0/+1/+3 and ffffffff at +12. State +2 is the local queue count.

Twice remove a buffer index from the shared pool, then append it locally. The leaf helpers preserve PR, and the entry deliberately leaves PR at 0x45e0. Empty-pool result r1=255 is silently ignored by append, with no retry or message.
Internal mailbox wait, continuation 0x45e2. No status polling occurs here.
Mailbox wait through TRAPA 0x23, saved continuation 0x45e2. Setup neither polls hardware nor posts a message.

Task 5 message: r7 = decoder queue 0x0f000314. Class 0x84 (DMA channel 0 end), 0x80 (sector pulses locked), 6 (task 6), 1 (task 1) and 0x81 (command 30) are handled. Other messages wait again at 0x45e0.
Task 5's message handling: DMA channel 0 end (0x84), sector pulses locked (0x80), task 6 requests (class 6), task 1 finished (class 1) and command 30 (0x81).
Class 0x84 payload 0x10: a sector arrived. Class 0x80 payload 0x12: the sector pulses are locked. Class 1 payload 0x11: task 1 finished a sector. Class 0x81 payload 0x30: command 30.
Class 6 payloads 0..9 through the table at 0x4658: 0, 1 read start, 2 retry read, 3 stop, 4 nothing, 5 subcode on, 6 read after a full buffer, 7 subcode off, 8 resumed read, 9 buffer hold.
Class 6 payloads 0..9: read start, retry, stop, nothing, subcode on, read after a full buffer, subcode off, resumed read, buffer hold.
Branches to the class handlers.

Sector arrived: r6 = header of the transferred slot (+24, plus 12). The mode byte goes to +10 and the frame from the BCD header (0x4e0c) to +36. Read state +4: 4 streaming, 2 synchronizing, 3 approaching the target. Other states stop.
A sector arrived: read the frame from its header, synchronize on two sectors in a row, approach the target, stream, check the decoder status by mode and complete the sector.

State 2: two sectors in a row (frame = +32 + 1, decoder status bit 6 clear) synchronize. The frame goes to +40 and 0x0f0002b0, the mode to +7, and 06050003 tells task 6 the position. At the target the read approaches it (state 3). Past the target, or more than 48 frames before it, the read is sought again.
Not in a row: keep the frame in +32 and wait for the next sector.
State 3: when the expected frame +40 is the target, the sector must be the target itself, and the read streams (state 4), otherwise it is sought again. Before that the expected frame counts on.
State 4: the frame must follow +32. It becomes +32 and 0x0f0002b0, and 06050003 tells task 6. With decoder status bit 6 the header mode byte is rewritten with the synchronized mode +7.
Prepare the next slot for DMA (0x4cf4) and drop the oldest queued slot beyond two (0x4cca). Without a free slot the buffer is full at 0x49c6.

Out of sequence: count down the drive offset 0x0f0002a4, set 0x0f0002b0 to the expected frame (+40 when state 2 found the read past the target or more than 48 frames before it, otherwise the target) plus the attempt count +9 and count the attempt. Up to 16 attempts seek again (06050004), then a read error.
In sequence: clear the attempt count +9 and the form +11 and prepare the next slot. Without a free slot hold the read (0x47aa).

Error mask by mode: mode 1 checks decoder status bits 0x21, mode 2 form 1 0x22, form 2 0x24 (0x20 when its EDC word is 0), other modes 0x20. Bit 2 of 0x0f00025c gives mode 2 the mask 0x20 without the subheader check, which otherwise sends differing subheader copies to the retry rules.
No free slot: with only the two DMA slots queued the buffer is full (0x49c6). Otherwise stop DMA and the decoder, set flag bit 1 and wait for a slot.
No error bits: deliver. Errors in mode 1 or form 1 go to correction. Form 2 is delivered with its errors unless bit 3 of 0x0f00025c is set, which sends it to the retry rules like every other mode.
Correction, unless 0x0f000262 is 0x80: the first slot goes to task 1 (0x4b9a) and flag bit 3 is set. While correction runs, later slots are marked in the bitmap 0x0f0006a0.

Retry rules from 0x0f000263: 0x80 retries without limit (06050000), 0 is a read error (06050002). Otherwise the low nibble is the number of retries, after which bit 6 delivers the sector and a clear bit 6 is a read error. Retries count in +8.
Deliver: unless correction runs, clear flag bit 4 and the error count, complete the oldest slot (0x4c52) and end the read once the next frame +44 reaches the end frame 0x0f000284.
Seek again: stop and post 06050004 with the next frame +44 at 0x0f0002b4.
Hold for a slot: clear DE in CHCR0, stop the decoder (0x4b70) and set flag bit 1.
Class 6 payload 9, buffer hold: stop, set flag bit 5 when a read was active, post 06050001. With the buffer-full byte 0x0f00034b clear, post 06040000 with +44 at 0x0f0002b4.
Payload entries: 0 and 1 at 0x4938, 2 at 0x4950, 6 at 0x4946, 8 at 0x4954.

Payloads 0 and 1, a new read: stop an active read, flags = 0x40 (read active). Payload 6 enters at 0x4946 and clears flag bit 5 and the error count +8, payload 2 at 0x4950 clears the attempt count +9, payload 8 at 0x4954 keeps both.
A read request: target from 0x0f0002b8, a slot prepared for DMA, then the decoder's sector pulse enabled.
Clear flag bit 1. The target 0x0f0002b8 goes to +28 and +44, and with bit 31 set to 0x0f0002ac. A full buffer (0x0f00034b nonzero) stops and posts 06040001 with flag bit 5.

Prepare a slot and drop one beyond two. Read state 1, clear the pulse and subcode states 0x0f0006dc..0x0f0006dd, clear 0x0a000006, enable the sector pulse (0x0a00000a = 0x10) and set the low bits of 0x0a00001a to 2 with interrupts masked.
Buffer full: byte 0x0f00034b = ff, 8 to 0x0a00001e, and with flag bit 6 post 06040001.
Class 0x80 payload 0x12, the sector pulses are locked: read state 2, +32 = ffffffff, start DMA with the prepared slot (0x5b7c), then prepare the next one.
The sector pulses are locked: start DMA channel 0 and prepare the next slot.

Class 1 payload 0x11, task 1 finished: clear flag bit 2. With bit 6 of 0x0f000263 and the retries used up the slot is delivered. Otherwise bit 7 in either byte of task 1's result word 0x0f000718 goes to the retry rules.
Task 1 finished a sector: complete the queued slots or send the next marked slot to task 1.
Complete slots (0x4c52) until two remain or the end frame is reached. A slot marked in the bitmap goes to task 1 next. When all are done clear flag bit 3, and with flag bit 1 seek again.
Class 6 payload 3, and the end of the range: stop, flags = 0, post 06050001.

Class 6 payload 5, subcode on: clear 0x0f0006e0 and 0x0f0006e1, subcode state 0x0f0006dd = 1, 0x0f0006e2 = fe, clear 0x0f0006ec..0x0f0006ee, clear flags 5 and 6 of 0x0a000006 and enable bit 5 in 0x0a00000a.
Class 6 payload 7, subcode off: clear flag and enable bit 5 at 0x0a000006 and 0x0a00000a and the subcode state 0x0f0006dd.
Class 0x81 payload 0x30 from command 30: under the sector lock connect CD device 0 with filter 0x0f000344 (0x5510), or clear its connection for ff (0x54f0). Then 0x40 to 0x0a00001e.
Command 30: connect CD device 0 to a filter or disconnect it.

Stop: clear DE in CHCR0, stop the decoder (0x4b70). Clear flag bit 3, and when task 1 is still correcting (flag bit 2) clear it and start task 1 again with TRAPA 0x28. Flush the queue to two slots (0x4c0e) and set read state 0.
Stop a read: DMA and decoder off, task 1 started again when correcting, queue flushed to two slots.
Decoder stop: disable the sector pulse (bit 4 of 0x0a00000a), clear the low bits of 0x0a00001a with interrupts masked, pulse state 0x0f0006dc = 0.
Send a slot to task 1: set flag bit 2, slot +0 to 0x0f00071b and post 01050010.
Send the oldest queued slot to task 1 (01050010).
r1 low byte is an index, and ff is a no-op sentinel, including sign-extended -1. +0/+1/+2 are head/tail/count at 0x0f000314. Links share the pool's byte array.
Append r1 low-byte index unless ff. Head/tail/count at 0x0f000314, links at 0x0f000354. No validation, count wraps, and the caller must provide a detached tail link.
Nonempty append patches the old tail link. No index/count validation and no initialization of the new tail link: caller must supply a detached index.
Count is stored as one byte, so 255 increments to zero.
Take the head of the decoder queue at 0x0f000314 (head, tail, count, links at 0x0f000354). An empty queue returns r1 = ff. Otherwise returns r1 = slot and r2 = remaining count.
Flush: under the sector lock return queued slots to the pool until two remain, then clear the correction bitmap 0x0f0006a0..0x0f0006b9.

Sector completion: nothing happens until the decoder queue holds more than two slots. Under lock 0b050000, a byte 0x0f000788 other than ff first clears the CD device connections through 0x54f0 with r1 = 0x80.

Decoder queue 0x0f000314: once more than two slots are queued, the head slot is delivered from CD device 0. While 0x0f000788 is not ff the CD device connections are cleared first, so the slot returns to the pool.
Take the head slot, keep it at 0x0f000317 and deliver it from CD device 0 (r2 = 0x80) through 0x4fa4. The destination partition, or ff, goes to 0x0f000323.
Frame address of the delivered sector header (slot + 12) plus one goes to 0x0f000340, and with bit 31 set to 0x0f0002ac. Write 4 to 0x0a00001e and release the lock.
Trim: with more than two slots queued, return the oldest to the pool under the sector lock.
Prepare: under the sector lock take a pool slot (0x4e98). +12 = the slot, or ff, +16 = its address 0x09000230 + 0x930 * n. Append it to the queue (0x4bae).
Take a pool slot for the next transfer and append it to the decoder queue.

Command 30, filter r0 = CR3 high byte: ff or below 24 is stored at 0x0f000344 and posted to task 5 as 05810030, answered through 0x91fe. Other values take the reject response. No message returns in r11.
Command 31: the filter connected to CD device 0 (0x0f000690), ff when none.
Command 32: the last partition a sector reached (0x0f000323), ff when none. The value goes to the CR3 high byte with the status from 0x91a8.
Bitmap bit for slot r0: r2 = 0x0f0006a0 + slot / 8, r1 = that byte, r0 = 1 << (slot & 7).
Convert BCD MSF in r1 bits 31..8 to a frame address: frames + 75 * seconds + 4500 * minutes, with digit weights from 0x4e8c. The result includes the 150-frame lead of MSF 00:02:00.
BCD MSF in r1 bits 31..8 to a frame address that includes the 150-frame lead.

Frame address r1 to BCD MSF in r1 bits 23..0, the inverse of 0x4e0c: six digits by restoring division, four quotient bits each, against the weights 45000, 4500, 750, 75, 10 and 1 read backward from 0x4e94. The 150-frame lead stays in, so frame 150 gives 00:02:00. Uses r0 and r2..r4.
Frame address to BCD MSF, the inverse of 0x4e0c, by restoring division against 45000, 4500, 750, 75, 10 and 1.
Pool head/tail/count at 0x0f000348, successor bytes at 0x0f000354. Return r1=index, r2=remaining count. Empty returns r1=255/r2=0 without writes.
Take head index from pool at 0x0f000348. Return r1=index or 255 when empty, r2=remaining count. Detach taken link and reset head/tail after last removal.
Last removal resets head and tail to ff. Otherwise follow the old head's byte link. Both nonempty paths detach the returned index with link ff.
Return slot r1 to the free pool at 0x0f000348 (head, tail, count). The first entry into an empty pool also runs the pool notification at 0x51fa. ff is ignored.
Take a run of r1 slots from the head of the free pool 0x0f000348 (head, tail, count). A run of 0, or longer than the pool count, returns r0 = r1 = ff and writes nothing.
Take a run of r1 slots from the free pool head.

Follow r1 links from the head. The slot after the run becomes the head, the last slot of the run gets link ff and the count drops by r1. An emptied pool gets head and tail ff. Returns the first slot in r0 and r1.
Append the run that starts at slot r1 and ends at a link of ff to the free pool 0x0f000348. ff returns r0 = r1 = ff. An empty pool takes the run as its head, otherwise the old tail links to it.
Append a run that ends at link ff to the free pool tail, then run the pool notification 0x51fa.
Walk the run to its last slot, which becomes the tail, and add its length to the count. The pool notification 0x51fa runs after every return.
Deliver slot r1 from source r2. Routing through 0x5264 returns the destination. No destination returns the slot to the pool and r1 = ff.
Route slot r1 from source r2 through the filters at 0x5264, append it to the destination partition and post 07040000 to task 7 when notify bit 0 is set. Unrouted slots return to the pool.
Append the slot to partition r0 & 31 (0..23): records at 0x0f000600 + 6p hold head, tail, count, notify flags and a cursor cache. Links live at 0x0f000354. The new tail link is ff.
Notify byte bit 0 posts 07040000 (task 7, class 4, payload 0) for every sector. Bit 1 counts down longword 0x0f00034c and posts 07040001 at zero.
Buffered-sector word 0x0f000350 counts up. At 200 it writes 8 to 0x0a00001e, sets buffer-full byte 0x0f00034b to ff and posts 06040001 when bit 6 of 0x0f000319 is set.

Slot at position r2 of partition r1. Position 0 is the head, ff or count - 1 the tail, and other positions walk the links from the cached cursor through 0x5600. An invalid partition, an empty partition or a position past the end returns ff.
Slot at position r2 of partition r1. Records 0x0f000600 + 6p hold head, tail, count, notify flags, cursor position and cursor slot. Links live at 0x0f000354.
No branch reaches 0x50c4, which returns the cursor slot +5.

Unlink r3 slots from position r2 of partition r1. ff selects the tail position or the rest of the partition. Returns the first and last unlinked slots in r1 and r2, or r1 = ff. Removing the whole partition resets the record.
Relink the neighbors around the removed run, fix the tail and subtract the count from the partition and from buffered-sector word 0x0f000350.
Locate the run: the slot before position r2 (r4, ff at the head) and the first and last slots of the run in r1 and r2.
Release r3 slots from position r2 of partition r1 back to the free pool. The run is appended at the pool tail and the pool count grows by r3. The first release into an empty pool also runs 0x51fa.
Return r3 slots from position r2 of partition r1 to the free pool at 0x0f000348.

Pool notification: a set buffer-full byte 0x0f00034b is cleared, and with bit 5 of 0x0f000319 set, 0x0f0002ac without bit 31 goes to 0x0f0002c0 and 06040000 is posted. Otherwise bit 1 of 0x0f000319 copies it to 0x0f0002b4 and posts 06050004.
Route slot r1 from source r2: CD device sources (r2 & 31 below 16) look up their filter at 0x0f000690. Slots from 202 upward are rejected. Mode 2 sectors supply the subheader longword at slot + 16.

CD device connection 0x0f000690, filter records 0x0f000420 + 16f (mode bit 6 frame range, bits 0..3 subheader fields, bit 4 inverts the subheader result), true output +2 and false output +3 of 0x0f0005a0 + 4f.
The sector header at slot + 12 converts to a frame address through 0x4e0c.
Filter loop: filter record 0x0f000420 + 16f, connection bytes 0x0f0005a0 + 4f. Mode bit 6 requires start <= FAD < start + count (+8, +12).
Mode bits 0..3 compare file (+2), channel (+3), submode mask (+4) against value (+6) and coding mask (+5) against value (+7) with subheader bytes 0..3. Bit 4 inverts the subheader result.
A failed filter continues with its false connection (+3). A passed filter returns its true connection (+2) in r0 and r1. No filter returns ff.
Initialize the free-buffer link bytes and slot/control records. These are RAM-only initializers. Allocation and record consumers are separate routines.

Write 201 successor bytes 1..201, followed by terminator 0xff at index 201. The 202-entry chain begins at 0x0f000354. State at 0x0f000348 receives head=0, tail=201 and count=202, with its remaining initialized fields zero.

Clear 24 sixteen-byte records at 0x0f000420. Initialize 24 six-byte records at 0x0f000600 to {0xffff,0,0xffff}. Their middle word is the cursor used by the sector parser. Initialize 24 four-byte records at 0x0f0005a0 with bytes ff,ff,a0+i,ff, then four sentinel words at 0x0f000690.

Clear 24 connection ends through 0x54f0, each with the end it points to: from 0x5402 the filter sources 0x00..0x17, from 0x5408 the partition ends 0x20..0x37, from 0x540e the false outputs 0x60..0x77.
Clear 24 connection ends through 0x54f0: filter sources from 0x5402, partition ends from 0x5408, false outputs from 0x540e.
Set the true output of every filter i to partition i: 0xa0 | i at +2 of 0x0f0005a0 + 4i. Nothing else changes.
Clear the 16-byte record of filter r1 (below 24) at 0x0f000420 + 16 r1. No code reaches this routine: the only longword that holds its address, 0x8354, is never loaded.
Clear one filter record. No code reaches it.
Clear all 24 filter records at 0x0f000420: mode, subheader condition and frame range 0.

Empty partition r1 (below 24) into the free pool 0x0f000348 (head, tail, count). An empty partition changes nothing. Its run follows the pool tail through the links 0x0f000354, or becomes the head of an empty pool, which then runs the pool notification 0x51fa.
Empty a partition into the free pool.

The partition's tail becomes the pool tail and the pool count grows by the partition's count. The partition: count 0, head, tail and cursor cache ff. The buffered-sector word 0x0f000350 drops by the count.
Empty partitions 0..23 into the pool through 0x5476.
Clear connection r1 and the connection it points to. ff is ignored.
Connect r1 and r2 in both directions after clearing both.

Store connection r1 -> r2. Valid destinations are 0x80 | n with n below 16, and 0xa0 | n or 0x00..0x7f with n below 24. Anything else stores ff. Source 0x80 | n (n below 16) uses byte 0x0f000690 + n. Sources 0x00 | n, 0x20 | n, 0x40 | n and 0x60 | n (n below 24) use bytes +0..+3 of 0x0f0005a0 + 4n, where +2 is the true output and +3 the false output. Other sources store nothing.
Store a connection for CD devices (0x0f000690) or filters (0x0f0005a0).
Read connection r1 into r1 with the addressing of 0x5536. Invalid sources return ff.
Walk to position r12 of the partition at r8, starting from the cursor cache (+4 position, +5 slot) when it lies at or before r12, otherwise from the head. The cache is updated.
Follow r12 links from slot r0 through 0x0f000354, 25 at a time through an unrolled sequence.
Task 4 entry: initialize buffer metadata and command state, then wait for a message. Processing after 0x5704 is a separate continuation.

Task 4's messages, after the wait at 0x5702: copy the request 0x0f000738..0x0f00073f, r1 and r2 of the command, to 0x0f0006c0 and clear bit 0 of 0x0f000740 through 0x7794. Class 0x81 payloads 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 52 and 55 run their handlers. Class 7 payloads 40, 42, 44 and 46 run the same filter handlers. Everything else waits again.
Task 4's messages: the filter settings 40, 42, 44 and 46, Reset Selector 48, Calculate Actual Size 52 and Execute FAD Search 55. Each ends with ESEL.
Class 7: only the four filter settings.
Clear command state at 0x0f0006bc..0x0f0006d9. This is not a whole-buffer clear.

Payload 40 (Set Filter Range): under the sector lock 0b040000, filter f (0x0f0006c4, the CR3 high byte) gets the start frame (CR1 low byte and CR2) at +8 and the frame count (CR3 low byte and CR4) at +12. Free the lock, write 0x40 (ESEL) to 0x0a00001e and wait again.

Payload 42 (Set Filter Subheader Condition): under the sector lock, filter f gets the file number (CR3 low byte) at +2, the channel (CR1 low byte) at +3, the submode and coding masks (CR2) at +4 and their values (CR4) at +6. ESEL.
Payload 44 (Set Filter Mode): the mode (CR1 low byte) goes to +0 of filter f. With bit 7 set the filter is initialized instead: frame range, file, channel, masks, values and +1 cleared, mode 0. ESEL.

Payload 46 (Set Filter Connection), flags in the CR1 low byte, filter f in the CR3 high byte. Flag bit 0: the true output 0x40 | f pairs with partition 0xa0 | p (CR2 high byte) through 0x5510, or is cleared through 0x54f0 for p = ff.
Flag bit 1: the false output 0x60 | f pairs with the source of filter g (CR2 low byte), or is cleared for g = ff. Free the lock and write ESEL.

Payload 48 (Reset Selector) under the sector lock, flags in the CR1 low byte. Flags 0 empty partition p (CR3 high byte) through 0x5476. Otherwise, in this order: bit 2 empties all partitions (0x54da), bit 3 clears the partition ends (0x5408), bit 4 clears the filters (0x545c), bit 5 clears the filter sources (0x5402), bit 6 resets the true outputs (0x5428) and bit 7 clears the false outputs (0x540e). Bits 0 and 1 do nothing. ESEL.

Payload 52 (Calculate Actual Size), from a request 0x6dac normalized: count c (CR4), position (CR2), partition p (CR3 high byte). Count 0 skips to the end with size 0, freeing a lock not taken. Get sector length 0x0f0006d8 of 0 reads the sectors, 1, 2 and 3 give c times 0x490, 0x492 or 0x498 words at 0x5a02 without the lock, and larger values give 0.
52: words for the host by the get sector length, reading each sector's mode for length 0.
Length 0 (user data): under the sector lock clear the end 0x20 | p (0x54f0), then find the slot at the position (0x506c). No slot gives size 0.

Each of the c sectors adds 0x400 words, or 0x48a for a mode 2 form 2 sector (slot byte 15 = 2 and bit 5 of subheader byte 2). The next slot follows the links. A link of ff is counted as slot ff, reading its header: as the last sector it adds one sector too many, otherwise the size becomes ffffff.
The size, in words, goes to 0x0f0006bc. ESEL.

Payload 55 (Execute FAD Search) under the sector lock. Results at 0x0f0006c8: +0 the best BCD MSF so far, +4 its position, +6 the partition, +8 the result frame, +12 the result position, +14 the result partition. The target frame (CR3 low byte and CR4) becomes BCD MSF through 0x4e3e.
55: the sector with the target frame address, or the nearest frame below it, from a position to the partition's end.
Partition p (CR3 high byte) to +6, the position (CR2) to +4. Clear the end 0x20 | p (0x54f0) and find the slot at the position (0x506c).
No slot: position ffff, frame ffffff.

Walk the partition from the position to its end. A header MSF (slot + 12) equal to the target ends the search with its frame (0x4e0c) and position. Otherwise an MSF above the best and below the target becomes the best.
At the end the result is the best MSF's frame and position, or position ffff with frame 0 when no sector lies below the target. Free the lock and write ESEL.

DMA channel 0 end (vector 72, ROM longword 0x0120): switch to the stack 0x0f0009a8. The decoder status (0x0a00001c low byte) goes to +6, the slot just filled from +13 to +14 and its address from +20 to +24. Start the next transfer (0x5b84) and post 05840010 through TRAPA 0x2d.
DMA channel 0 end (vector 72): keep the decoder status, start the next transfer and post 05840010 to task 5 through TRAPA 0x2d.
DMA start from task 5: r12 = DMA channel 0, r11 = 0x0a000018, r13 = the decoder queue.
Program DMA channel 0 for a prepared slot: slot + 12, 0x492 words, CHCR0 0x436d.

Clear bit 7 of 0x0a00001a. With a prepared slot +12: DAR0 = slot + 12, TCR0 = 0x492 words (2340 bytes), CHCR0 = 0x436d after reading it, the slot moves to +13 and its address to +20, +12 = ff. Without one CHCR0 = 0x4368, the channel off.

IRQ7 (vector 71, ROM longword 0x011c), the decoder: switch to the stack 0x0f000950. The flags at 0x0a000006 masked with the enables at 0x0a00000a go to 0x0f0006de. Bit 4 is the sector pulse (0x5c32), bit 5 the subcode (0x5cb8).
IRQ7 (vector 71): decoder flags masked with their enables. Bit 4 the sector pulse, bit 5 the subcode.
Sector pulse: clear flag bit 4 at 0x0a000006. Pulse state 0x0f0006dc: 0 the first pulse, 1 a later pulse, other states only disable the pulse.
Lock on the sector pulse: two pulses one sector period apart start the decoder and post 05800012 to task 5.

Later pulse: the time since the last pulse must be within +3 counts of the interval +8. Then the decoder gets the low bits 7 at 0x0a00001a, state 2, 05800012 goes to task 5 through TRAPA 0x2d and the pulse is disabled. Otherwise count the miss in 0x0f0006e3.
First pulse: keep the time. Interval 0x8235 counts (1/75 s at 2.5 MHz) and tolerance 28 when bit 4 of 0x0f00025c is set, otherwise half of both. Clear the miss count, state 1.

IRQ7 with flag 5, one subcode frame, from 0x5c14 with r10 = 0x0a000004, r11 = 0x0a000018 and r13 = the decoder record 0x0f0006dc: +1 the subcode state (1 hunting, 2 locked), +2 the flags, +3 pack done, +4 the pack 0..31, +5 the symbol 0..23, +6 the frame 0..97 of the block, +7 missed syncs, +12 the last TCNT4. The low byte of the flags word at 0x0a000006 goes to +2, flags 5 and 6 are cleared and r1 = TCNT4.
IRQ7 flag 5: one subcode frame. Hunting counts two block starts (flag 6), locked counts frames by TCNT4 and stores the symbol in the ring. A completed pack posts 02800010 to task 2.
Other subcode states return.
Hunting: keep the time. Flag 6, a block start, counts +6 up from fe. The second one locks: no missed syncs, state 2, and this frame's symbol is stored.
Locked: the frames since the last one from the TCNT4 difference, 340 counts a frame (2.5 MHz over 7350 frames a second). A difference of 85..425 is one frame.
Up to 5525 counts: 1 + (difference - 85) / 340, four quotient bits. More, or less than 85, starts hunting again.

Advance the frame +6 and wrap it at 98: a new block starts the next pack with the symbol index at the new frame. Frames 96 and 97, the two sync frames, do not move the symbol index. Otherwise the symbol +5 advances with the frames, and past 23 the pack +4 advances and +3 is set.
Flag 6 at frame 0 clears the missed syncs. Flag 6 at frames 1..4 restarts the block there, frame and symbol 0. Flag 6 anywhere else is a missed sync, and the third starts hunting.
Hunting again: +4 to the multiple of 4 above +4 + 3, symbol 0, state 1 and +6 = ff, so the next block start locks. Nothing is stored.

Store the symbol, the low six bits of 0x0a000018, in the ring 0x09074e10 of 32 packs of 24 bytes: pack +4 + 7 - (+5 mod 8), byte +5. Symbol n of a pack arrives n mod 8 packs after its symbol 0, so the ring pack at +4 is whole when +4 advances.
A completed pack: task 2's host pack (0x0f0006ed) equal to +4 + 8, the pack the next one starts to overwrite, sets task 2's state 3 (overrun). 02800010 goes to task 2 through TRAPA 0x2d.
Time: r1 = the time high part 0x0f00021c (plus one when OVF is pending in TSR4) << 16 | TCNT4, r2 = the upper bits.
Time in ITU4 counts: the time high part and TCNT4.
Task 2 entry: clear three state words at 0x0f0006ec, then wait for a message. The following continuation reloads its state pointer after the trap.

Task 2's messages, r10 = its state 0x0f0006ec: +0 the next pack to decode, +1 the next pack for the host, +2 the state (0 idle, 1 waiting for pack 9, 2 running, 3 overrun), +4 and +5 the last P and Q results, +8 the pack's address. Class 0x80 comes from the subcode handler, class 0x81 from 20 type 1, class 3 payload 1 from the end of the transfer.
Task 2's messages: 02800010 decodes the completed packs, 02810000 sends the next pack to the host, 02030001 frees lock 3.
Class 3 payload 1: free lock 3 (03020000).

20 type 1: take lock 3 (03020000). The transfer block 0x0f000250 is the ring pack +1, 12 words at 0x0f000254. State 3 moves +1 to +0 + 9, past the packs the next pack overwrites, and back to state 2. State 2 advances +1. Then the type 0 transfer start 0x23ba.
A completed pack. State 0 becomes 1. State 1 waits for the handler's pack 9 (0x0f0006e0), then starts both indexes at 8 in state 2. States 2 and 3 decode.
Decode each pack from +0 up to the handler's pack: swap symbols 3 and 23, 2 and 5, 1 and 18 back, then the P parity (0x6032) and the Q parity (0x5fa4). Either failing sets bit 7 of symbol 0.

Q parity over symbols 0..3 of the pack at r2, a (4, 2) Reed-Solomon code over GF(64) with x^6 + x + 1: S0 the sum, S1 = s0 a^3 + s1 a^2 + s2 a + s3 by Horner's rule, times a being a shift that adds 0x43 on overflow. Both 0: result 0. One of them 0: failure 0x80. Otherwise the error S0 is at symbol 3 - k, a^k = S1 / S0 from the log table r9, and k above 3 is a failure. A correction returns 1.
Q parity of symbols 0..3, one error corrected.

P parity, a (24, 20) Reed-Solomon code, of the pack at 0x0f0006f4, r8 the antilog table and r9 the log table: the syndromes, the locator terms at 0x0f0006f8 and the correction, with its notes at 0x0f000708.
P parity of the pack, up to two errors corrected.
Syndromes S0..S3 in r4..r7: symbol 23 - j weighs a^(jk) in S_k, j = 0..23. Zero symbols are skipped.

Which terms are nonzero: 0x0f00070e bit 0 D = S0 S2 + S1^2, bit 1 S1 S2 + S0 S3, bit 2 S1 S3 + S2^2, and 0x0f00070f bit 0 S0, bit 1 S3. None: one error or none. All three: two errors. Otherwise a failure.
One error: S1 / S0 = a^j, the error S0 at symbol 23 - j (0x0f00070c). No S0 and no S3: result 0. j above 23 is a failure, and the log of 0 is 63.

Two errors at X1 and X2: the table 0x6314 maps c = sigma1^2 / sigma2 = X1/X2 + X2/X1 to their distance d, 1..23, and 0 is a failure. log X1 = (d + log sigma2) / 2 by a shift and log X2 = log sigma2 - log X1, each below 24 (notes at 0x0f00070a..0x0f00070d). The error at X2 is (S0 X1 + S1) / sigma1, the one at X1 that plus S0. Result 2.
Failure 0x80, or 0 with nothing to correct.

Locator terms at r10 = 0x0f0006f8: +3..+8 the products S0 S2, S1 S3, S1 S2, S0 S3, S1^2 and S2^2, +0 D, +1 and +2 the other two sums, +9 sigma1 = +1 / D, +10 sigma2 = +2 / D, +11 = +1 / +2 and +12 c = +11 * sigma1.
r13 = r13 * r12 in GF(64) through the log table r9 and the antilog table r8, 0 when either is 0.
r13 = r13 / r12, 0 for r13 = 0 and 0x80 for r12 = 0.
GF(64) powers of alpha, field polynomial x^6 + x + 1.
GF(64) logarithms to base alpha. The log of 0 is 63.
Two-error step: c = alpha^d + alpha^-d gives d for d = 1..23, 0 otherwise.
Command 20 type 1 (Get Subcode R-W) from 0x9440, r10 = task 2's state. No pack for the host (state 0 or 1, or +1 equal to +0): the status with bit 7, WAIT.
Command 20 type 1, Get Subcode R-W: WAIT without a pack, else the flags (bit 0 pack data error, bit 1 overrun), 12 words and 02810000 to task 2.

A pack: CR4 bit 1 in state 3 (overrun) and bit 0 when symbol 0 of the ring pack +1 has bit 7 (a parity failure), which is cleared with bit 6. The status with bit 6 (data transfer request) and 12 words. 02810000 to task 2, which sends the pack.

Task 1 begins by waiting for a message. Its local filter accepts source/class byte 5 and low payload byte 0x10, ignoring the other payload byte. Other messages return to the wait. Accepted work begins at 0x63f2.
Task 1 waits for source/class 5 and low payload byte 0x10. Accepted work begins at 0x63f2, the sector correction.

Task 1's work for 01050010: correct the sector in slot 0x0f00071b. r13 = the correction state 0x0f000710: +0 header address, +4 saved header, +8 Q result, +9 P result, +10 pairs left, +11 slot. Slot ff goes back to the wait at 0x63de without an answer.
Task 1's work for 01050010: correct slot 0x0f00071b and answer 05010011 with the result word 0x0f000718. Slot ff answers nothing.

The slot's header address 0x0900023c + 0x930 * slot (bytes 12..2351 of the sector) to +0 and its header long to +4. With mode byte 2 the header long in the slot becomes 0, since mode 2 parity is computed over a zero header.
Correct at 0x6438. A header long of 0 afterwards gets the saved one back. A nonzero one stays, even in a mode 2 header that was zeroed.
Answer 05010011 (task 5, class 1, payload 0x11), the result word being 0x0f000718, and wait again.
Correct the sector at +0 with r10 = the lane reduction table 0x685c and r11 = the log table 0x675c: a P pass, a Q pass and a P pass.
P, Q and P passes, then up to 5 Q and P pairs as 0x0f000262 allows.

The last P pass without corrections or failures (P result 0) ends it, as does 0x0f000262 = 0 (the CR4 high byte of command 04). Otherwise up to that many Q and P pairs follow, 5 for any value above 5, counted in +10.
A Q pass, then a P pass. Either one ending without corrections or failures ends it.

P pass. The 2340 bytes from the header are 1170 words, each byte of a word in its own plane. The first 1118 words are 26 rows of 43, and each column of 26 words is a P vector in each plane (ECMA-130 Annex A). P result +9 cleared, then columns 2r9 and 2r9+1 for r9 = 0..20 (0x650c) and column 42 alone (0x64be).
P pass: the 43 columns of 26 words, both bytes of each word.
Q pass: Q result +8 cleared, then Q diagonals 2r9 and 2r9+1 for r9 = 0..12 (0x65ba).
Q pass: the 26 diagonals of 45 words, both bytes of each word.
P column 42 alone: r12 = its first word, two lanes (the word's two bytes) in the low half of r3 and r4.
P column 42, two lanes.
r7 = 0x100, r6 = 0x10000 and r5 = 0x1000000 test the bits a left shift carries across lane boundaries.
26 elements 86 bytes apart. r3 = S0, the XOR of the elements. r4 = S1 by Horner's rule, r4 times alpha plus the element, so the first element carries alpha^25 and the last alpha^0.

Times alpha in every lane at once: shift left, then index the reduction table by the carry out of bit 31 and the inverted bits that crossed into bits 24, 16 and 8. Its entry clears each crossed bit and adds 0x1d to each lane that overflowed (x^8 = x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1).
Both syndromes 0 in every lane: no error. Otherwise the lanes at 0x655c with r8 = 1.
P columns 2r9 and 2r9+1: four lanes, the bytes of two words read as halfwords (rows are 86 bytes apart, so only halfword aligned). r12 = the first element, syndromes as at 0x64be.
P columns 2r9 and 2r9+1, four lanes, and the lane correction shared with column 42.
Each lane from the low byte, r8 its byte offset in the element: S0 in r5, S1 in r6. Both 0: no error. Only one of them 0: a failure, bit 7 of the P result +9.

Both nonzero: one error of value S0 at the element whose power of alpha is S1 / S0, k = log S1 - log S0 mod 255 from the log table. k above 25 is a failure. Otherwise element 25 - k (86 bytes a row) is XORed with S0 and the P result counts one.
Next lane.

Q diagonals 2r9 (low lanes) and 2r9+1 (high lanes). Element m of diagonal d is word 44m + 43d mod 1118, so element m - 1 of 2r9+1 lies just before element m of 2r9 and one long read serves both, the high lanes one element behind. r9 on the stack, then r9 = the end of the 1118 words, r12 = 2r9's first element.
Q diagonals 2r9 and 2r9+1, four lanes, one long read serving both.
Element 0 of 2r9 alone starts both syndromes, then 42 longs 88 bytes apart, taken back 0x8bc bytes past the end (0x66ac).
Element 42 of 2r9+1: only the high lanes take a Horner step, the table index marks the low lanes as not carrying.
The two parity words of each diagonal d, words 1118 + d and 1144 + d (bytes 0x8bc + 2d and 0x8f0 + 2d), read as one long each and swapped so 2r9+1 is high.
Both syndromes 0 in every lane: no error. Lanes as for P, with bit 7 and the count in the Q result +8.
k above 44 is a failure. Element 44 - k: data below 43, a parity word at 43 or 44 (0x6724).

Data element i: 88 bytes a step from 2r9's first element, 86 bytes more for 2r9+1 (r8 bit 1 clear), taken back past the end at most twice. The second byte of the word for odd r8. XORed with S0, and the Q result counts one.
Parity element: 0x8bc + 4 * r9 bytes into the sector, 52 more for element 44 and 2 more for 2r9+1.
GF(2^8) logarithms to base alpha, field polynomial x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1. Entry 0 unused.
Sixteen words XORed after a left shift of four lanes: indexed by the carry out of bit 31 and the inverted bits shifted into 24, 16 and 8.

Commands 61 and 63 (Get Sector Data, Get and Delete Sector Data) from the data-command gate. r1 = CR1 << 16 | CR2 (position), r2 = CR3 << 16 | CR4 (partition in the high byte, count). Bits 1..3 of the task 12 flags 0x0f000724 (a get, a get and delete or a put in progress) answer wait at 0x690a.
Commands 61 and 63: busy check, request check 0x6dac, then 0c8100cc for task 12 with the data transfer request.
Check the request through 0x6dac: ff rejects at 0x6900, 1 waits at 0x690a and 0 continues at 0x6930.
Command 62 (Delete Sector Data), straight from the group 6 table, without the gate or the busy check. The same request check, then 0x6910.
Command 62: request check 0x6dac, then 0c810062 for task 12. No gate and no busy check.
Command 64 (Put Sector Data): busy as for 61. Filter f = CR3 high byte of 24 or more rejects. A count CR4 of 0, or above the free pool count 0x0f00034a, waits.
Command 64: busy check, filter below 24, a count from 1 to the free slots, then 0c810064 for task 12 with the data transfer request.
Reject: the response from 0x91e8 with r1, r2 and r11 cleared.
Wait: the wait response from 0x91ec, no message.
62: record the request through 0x6a40, where one not yet taken waits. r11 = 0c8100cc with the command byte cc, for the IRQ6 handler to post to task 12, and the response from 0x91fe.
61, 63 and 64: record the request and set r11 as for 62. The response from 0x91fe, whose status byte 0x91a4 rebuilds with the data transfer request bit 0x40.
Task 12 initializes its local state, clears r11, then waits for a message.

Task 12 message dispatch after the wait at 0x6998. Class 3 (the end of a transfer) becomes 0x22. Payload 62 runs 0x6b52 and waits again. 61, 63 and 64 run 0x6bac, 0x6c16 and 0x6c80, which return the next step in r0.
Task 12 message dispatch: 61..64 from the host, class 3 at the end of a transfer.
Step 0x6f, a put without slots: 0x80 to 0x0a00001e and wait again.
Otherwise keep the step on the stack and take the transfer lock 030c0000 (record 3). Step 0x21 starts a transfer to the host at 0x6d7e, step 0x20 one from the host at 0x6d78.
0x22 ends the transfer at 0x6a6e. Other messages wait again at 0x6996.
Record a request for task 12. With bit 0 of 0x0f000724 set, a request not yet taken, return T = 1. Otherwise r1 goes to 0x0f00071c and r2 to 0x0f000720, bit 0 is set and T = 0.
Keep a request at 0x0f00071c unless one is not yet taken (T = 1).
Take the request: r12 = 0x0f00071c (CR1, CR2) and r13 = 0x0f000720 (CR3, CR4). Clear bit 0 of 0x0f000724.
Take the kept request into r12 and r13.
End of a sector transfer. A get and delete (bit 2 of 0x0f000724) returns its run, still linked from the first slot at 0x0f000725, to the free pool through 0x4f58 under the sector lock 0b0c0000.
End of a sector transfer: return a get and delete's run to the pool, deliver a put's slots, free the transfer lock.

A put (bit 3) delivers its slots in link order from source 0x88 through 0x4fa4, each under the sector lock. When connection 0x88 (0x55ae) no longer names the filter kept at 0x0f000727, 0x5510 connects them again first.
Clear bits 1..3 of 0x0f000724, set 0x0f000725 to ff, free the transfer lock 030c0000 and write 0x80 to 0x0a00001e. Returns r0 = 0.
Initialize state bytes/words at 0x0f00071c..0x0f000727. Bytes +9 and +11 become 0xff, the other fields written here become zero.
Payload 62 (Delete Sector Data): take the request. r12 and r13 stay on the stack across 0x5510, which uses them.
62: connect 0x88 with the partition's end, release the slots to the pool.

Under the sector lock 0b0c0000 connect 0x88 with the end 0x20 | p of partition p (0x5510), then release the count slots from the position of partition p to the pool (0x51be). Free the lock and write 0x80 to 0x0a00001e.
Payload 61 (Get Sector Data): take the request. Under the sector lock keep the end 0x20 | p at 0x0f000727 and connect it with 0x88 (0x5510).
61: connect 0x88 with the partition's end, find the first slot, step 0x21.
Keep the count at 0x0f000726 and the slot at the position of partition p (0x506c) at 0x0f000725. Free the lock, set bit 1 of 0x0f000724 and return step 0x21.
Payload 63 (Get and Delete Sector Data): as 61, with the end 0x20 | p kept at 0x0f000727 and connected with 0x88.
63: connect 0x88 with the partition's end, unlink the slots, step 0x21.
Unlink the count slots from the position of partition p (0x50ca) and keep the first at 0x0f000725. Free the lock, set bit 2 and return step 0x21.
Payload 64 (Put Sector Data): take the request. Under the sector lock keep filter f at 0x0f000727 and connect it with 0x88 (0x5510).
64: connect 0x88 with the filter, take slots from the pool and clear their first 24 bytes, step 0x20.
Keep the count at 0x0f000726 and take that many slots from the pool (0x4f0c), the first at 0x0f000725. Without slots return step 0x6f.
Set bit 3 of 0x0f000724. Clear the first 24 bytes of each slot of the run (sync, header and subheader), following the links to ff, and return step 0x20.

Start the sector transfer: type 3 (from the host) at 0x6d78, type 2 (to the host) at 0x6d7e. Current slot 0x0f000258, sectors left 0x0f000257 and connection index 0x0f000259 come from 0x0f000725, 0x0f000726 and the low five bits of 0x0f000727.
Start a type 3 (0x6d78) or type 2 (0x6d7e) transfer, tail-calling 0x23ba.
r11 = 030c0000 | type. The call to 0x23ba restores PR in its delay slot, so the transfer start returns straight to this routine's caller and 0x6da8 is not reached.
Check a sector request: r1 = CR1 << 16 | CR2 (position), r2 = CR3 << 16 | CR4 (partition p in the high byte, count). p of 24 or more returns ff, an empty partition returns 1.
Check a partition, position and count: ff rejects, 1 waits, 0 fits.
Position ffff becomes the last position, count - 1, in r1. Any other position at or past the count returns 1.
Count 0 returns 1. Count ffff becomes the rest of the partition from the position, in r2 with the CR3 low byte cleared. A run past the end returns 1. A request that fits returns 0.

Get span of slot r9: r7 = 0x09000230 + 0x930 * r9. Get sector length 0x0f0006d8 = 0 gives 0x400 words from +16 for mode 1 (header byte +15), from +24 for other modes, 0x48a for mode 2 form 2 (submode bit 5 at +18). 1 gives 0x490 words from +16, 2 0x492 from +12, 3 0x498 from +0.
Address and word count of a slot for the get sector length 0x0f0006d8.
Put span of slot r9: r7 = 0x09000230 + 0x930 * r9. Put sector length 0x0f0006d9 = 0 gives 0x400 words from +24, 1 0x490 from +16, 2 0x492 from +12, 3 0x498 from +0.
Address and word count of a slot for the put sector length 0x0f0006d9.

Commands 65 and 66 (Copy Sector Data, Move Sector Data): destination filter f = CR1 low byte, source partition p = CR3 high byte, position CR2, count CR4. f of 24 or more rejects. The request check 0x6dac rejects (ff) or waits (1). 65 also waits for a count above the free pool count 0x0f00034a.
Commands 65 and 66, Copy and Move Sector Data: destination filter, request check, free slots for 65, then 0d8100cc for task 13.
Command 67 (Get Copy Error): CR1 low byte ff while bits 0..2 of task 13's flags 0x0f000730 are set (a request, a copy or a move), 1 with bit 3 (an error), otherwise 0. The status byte from 0x91a8.
Command 67, Get Copy Error: ff while task 13 works, 1 after an error, else 0.
Record the request for task 13 through 0x6ff8, where one not yet taken waits. Otherwise r11 = 0d8100cc with the command byte cc and the response from 0x91fe.
Reject: the response from 0x91e8 with r1, r2 and r11 cleared.
Wait: the wait response from 0x91ec with r11 cleared.
Task 13 initializes its local state, clears r11, then waits for a message.
Task 13's messages, after the wait at 0x6fd0: low byte 0x65 runs the copy 0x704c and 0x66 the move 0x714e, whatever the class. Every message then waits again with r11 cleared.
Task 13's messages: low byte 65 copies, 66 moves.
Record a request for task 13. With bit 0 of 0x0f000730 set, a request not yet taken, return T = 1. Otherwise r1 goes to 0x0f000728 and r2 to 0x0f00072c, bit 0 is set and T = 0.
Take the request: r12 = 0x0f000728 (CR1, CR2) and r13 = 0x0f00072c (CR3, CR4). Clear bit 0 of 0x0f000730.
Clear words at 0x0f000728/72c and bytes 730,732..735, and set byte 731 to 0xff.

Copy (65): set bit 1 of the flags 0x0f000730 and clear bit 3. 0x721e takes the request and pairs devices 0x81 and 0x89. State: 0x0f000731 the slot, 0x0f000732 the position, 0x0f000733 the sectors left, 0x0f000734 the end 0x20 | p, 0x0f000735 filter f.
65: copy each sector the destination filter's chain passes into a new slot, from device 0x89. ECPY at the end.
Under the sector lock: the slot at the position of partition p (0x506c), then its route from device 0x89 through filter f's chain (0x5264). Free the lock.
Next: the position advances and the count drops. At 0 the copy ends. Otherwise 0x727c takes the lock and checks both pairs.
Error: set bit 3, free the lock and end.
A sector some filter passes: with both pairs intact, take a free slot (0x4e98). No free slot is an error.
Outside the lock copy the whole sector into the new slot (0x72c0), then check both pairs again. A changed pair returns the new slot to the pool (0x4ed4) and ends in error.
Deliver the copy from device 0x89 (0x4fa4), which routes it through filter f's chain again, and free the lock.
End: clear bit 1 and write 0x100 (ECPY) to 0x0a00001e.

Move (66): set bit 2 of the flags and clear bit 3. 0x721e takes the request and pairs the devices. Under the sector lock unlink the count slots from the position of partition p (0x50ca), the first at 0x0f000731. No run is an error.
66: unlink the run and deliver its slots from device 0x89. ECPY at the end.

Deliver the run in link order: 0x727c takes the lock and checks both pairs, then the slot at 0x0f000731 goes from device 0x89 through filter f's chain (0x4fa4), its successor to 0x0f000731, and the lock is freed. A sector no filter passes returns to the pool.
Error: set bit 3 and return every slot of the run not yet delivered to the pool (0x4ed4), with the lock held.
End: free the lock, 0x0f000731 = ff, clear bit 2 and write 0x100 (ECPY).

Take the request (0x7014) and keep the count (CR4 low byte) at 0x0f000733, the end 0x20 | p of source partition p at 0x0f000734, the position (CR2 low byte) at 0x0f000732 and destination filter f at 0x0f000735.
Take the request and pair device 0x81 with the source partition's end and 0x89 with the destination filter.
Take the sector lock 0b0d0000 and pair device 0x81 with the end 0x20 | p and device 0x89 with filter f (0x5510), which clears what each end was connected with. Returns with the lock held.
Take the sector lock and check the pairs: T = 1 when connection 0x81 (0x55ae) no longer names 0x0f000734 or 0x89 no longer names 0x0f000735, otherwise T = 0. Returns with the lock held.
Under the sector lock, T = 1 when either pair changed.
Copy slot r2 to slot r1, all 0x930 bytes, 12 longwords a pass from the end down.
Command 40 (Set Filter Range): filter f (CR3 high byte) of 24 or more rejects. Otherwise the request goes to task 4 at 0x76d4.
Command 40, Set Filter Range: task 4 sets the start frame and count.
Command 41 (Get Filter Range): filter f of 24 or more rejects. The start frame (+8) in the CR1 low byte and CR2, f in the CR3 high byte over the frame count (+12). The status from 0x91a8.
Command 42 (Set Filter Subheader Condition): filter f of 24 or more rejects, otherwise task 4.
Command 43 (Get Filter Subheader Condition): filter f of 24 or more rejects. CR1 low byte the channel (+3), CR2 the masks (+4), CR3 f over the file number (+2), CR4 the values (+6).
Command 44 (Set Filter Mode): filter f of 24 or more rejects, otherwise task 4.
Command 45 (Get Filter Mode): filter f of 24 or more rejects. The mode byte (+0) in the CR1 low byte, f in the CR3 high byte.

Command 46 (Set Filter Connection): filter f of 24 or more rejects. With flag bit 1 (CR1 low byte) a false output (CR2 low byte) of 24 or more other than ff rejects, with bit 0 a partition (CR2 high byte) of 24 or more other than ff. Otherwise task 4.
Command 46, Set Filter Connection: task 4 pairs the true output with a partition and the false output with another filter.

Command 47 (Get Filter Connection): filter f of 24 or more rejects. CR2 holds the true output's partition over the false output's filter, each the low five bits of the connection byte, or ff for a byte whose top three bits are set. f in the CR3 high byte.
Command 48 (Reset Selector): with flags 0 (CR1 low byte) a partition (CR3 high byte) of 24 or more rejects. Otherwise task 4.
Command 48, Reset Selector: task 4 empties partitions and clears connections and filters by flag.
Command 50 (Get Buffer Size): CR2 the free pool count 0x0f00034a, at most 200, CR3 24 partitions in the high byte, CR4 200 sectors.
Command 50, Get Buffer Size: free slots (at most 200), 24 partitions, 200 sectors.
Command 60 (Set Sector Length): get sector length = CR1 low byte, put sector length = CR2 high byte. Each must be ff (keep) or 0..3, otherwise reject at 0x76f4.
Command 60: get sector length from the CR1 low byte, put sector length from the CR2 high byte, ff keeps. 0x40 to 0x0a00001e.
Store the lengths other than ff at 0x0f0006d8 and 0x0f0006d9, clear r11, write 0x40 to 0x0a00001e and answer through 0x91fe at 0x76ee.
Command 51 (Get Sector Number): partition p (CR3 high byte) of 24 or more rejects. CR4 its count (+2 of 0x0f000600 + 6p), CR3 0.
Command 52 (Calculate Actual Size): the request check 0x6dac rejects (ff) or waits (1). Otherwise task 4, with r12 and r13 cleared.
Command 53 (Get Actual Size): the low 24 bits of 0x0f0006bc in the CR1 low byte and CR2.
Command 54 (Get Sector Info): partition p (CR3 high byte) of 24 or more rejects, an empty one waits. Position ffff (CR2) is the last, and one at or past the count waits.
Command 54, Get Sector Info: a sector's frame address and mode 2 subheader.

The slot at the position (0x506c) through GBR: its header (slot + 12) gives the frame (0x4e0c) for the CR1 low byte and CR2. A mode 2 sector gives the subheader longword (slot + 16) for CR3 and CR4, other modes 0.
Command 55 (Execute FAD Search): partition p of 24 or more rejects, an empty one waits. Position ffff is the last, and one at or past the count waits. Otherwise task 4 with r12 and r13 cleared.
Command 56 (Get FAD Search Results): CR2 the result position (0x0f0006d4), CR3 the partition (0x0f0006d6) over the result frame (0x0f0006d0) in the CR3 low byte and CR4.
Post to task 4: 0x7778 records r1 and r2, where a request not yet taken waits. Otherwise r11 = 048100cc with the command byte cc and the response from 0x91fe at 0x76ee.
Record the request for task 4 and post 048100cc, or wait while one is not yet taken.
Answers shared by the buffer commands: the response from 0x91fe with r11 kept.
Answers shared by the buffer commands: 0x91fe, reject, wait and status.
Reject: the response from 0x91e8 with r1, r2 and r11 cleared.
Wait: the wait response from 0x91ec with r11 cleared.
The status byte from 0x91a8 over the response in r12 and r13, with r11 cleared.
Record a request for task 4. With bit 0 of 0x0f000740 set, a request not yet taken, return T = 1. Otherwise r1 goes to 0x0f000738 and r2 to 0x0f00073c, bit 0 is set and T = 0.
Clear bit 0 of 0x0f000740, the request taken.
Clear the disc result word at 0x0f000786.
Task 7 initializes disc/header state, clears byte 0x0f00076b, then waits. Its wait at 0x77c0 is also a shared return destination of disc-header parsing.
Task 7 initializes disc/header state and waits at 0x77c0. Header-parser exits also target that wait.
Task 7 message dispatch after the wait at 0x77c0: class r11 bits 23..16. Class 6 goes to 0x7822 and class 0x81 to 0x7864. Classes 4, 3 and 7 are tested from 0x77d4.
Class 4 goes to 0x78d4, class 3 to 0x79e4 and class 7 to 0x77e6. Other classes wait again at 0x77c0.

Class 7 payload 0 is the expiry of timer 07070000. Disc state 2 or 3 stores result 0, state 7 completes at 0x8bd4 with the result unchanged and other states store result 3. A stored result also clears 0x0f000788.

Expiry of timer 07070000 (class 7 payload 0). Disc states 2 and 3 store result 0, state 7 keeps the result and other states store 3. A stored result clears 0x0f000788, which blocks later sector delivery.

Class 6: payload 0 goes to 0x8494 while busy flag 0x0f0007b0 is set and otherwise runs disc initialization 0x7abc. Payload 1 waits, 2 continues the authentication seeks at 0x8952 and 3 goes to 0x8494.
Class 6 from task 6. Payload 2 continues the authentication seeks at 0x8952.
Class 0x81 request payload r11 bits 15..0: 0 at 0x786a, 1 to 0x7e88, 4 to 0x7f10, 5 to 0x7f44, 2 to 0x7f88, 6 to 0x8228, 7 to 0x78b2, 8 to 0x8510. Other payloads return to the wait at 0x77c0.
Payload 0 continues at 0x7c06 when longword 0x0f000760 is nonzero, otherwise at 0x7b6c.
Payload 8 is the disc authentication request posted by e0 subcode 0.
Payload 7, from Abort File: with no step in progress (0x0f00076c = 0) write 0x0200 (EFLS) to 0x0a00001e and wait at 0x77c0. Otherwise state 4 (0x0f00076b) and the end at 0x82be.
Payload 7: EFLS with nothing in progress, otherwise state 4 and the end.

Class 4: payload 2 waits and 1 goes to 0x82be. Payload 0, a sector added to the partition, dispatches on disc state 0x0907adcb: 1 to 0x7954, 3 header scan at 0x86d2, 6 sector checks at 0x8a60, 7 extension read at 0x8da8 and 4 below. Other states wait.

Class 4 payload 0, a sector added to the partition: disc state 3 goes to the header scan 0x86d2, 6 to the sector checks 0x8a60, 7 to the extension read 0x8da8, 1 to 0x7954, and 4 releases sectors past the cursor.
State 4: under lock 0b070000, release the partition sectors past cursor 0x0f00078b through 0x51be and wait.
Class 4 payload 0 in disc state 1, a sector added to partition f: in state 2 (no read in progress) wait again at 0x77c0.
A sector added to partition f in disc state 1: dispatch on the step.
Under the sector lock 0b070000 take the first slot of partition f (0x0f000772) from 0x506c.
Its data: +24 for a mode 2 sector (header byte +15), +16 otherwise.

Step 0x0f00076c: 1 checks the volume descriptor at 0x7b8c. 0x14 parses from offset 0x0f000764 of this sector at 0x7c50. 0x34 skips records at 0x814e, from the sector start when the ID was before the window (0x0f00076a = 1) and from offset 0x0f000764 otherwise. 0x24 skips from the sector start. Other steps (2, 3, 4) parse from the sector start.

Class 3, the end of a transfer task 7 owns (07030001 from 06, also after an error): payload 0 waits and 1 frees the transfer lock at 0x7a52. Other payloads are compared with the halfword at 0x7a08, which is 0, so they wait.
Class 3: payload 1 frees the transfer lock.
Free the transfer lock 03070000 (record 3) and wait at 0x77c0.
Free the transfer lock 03070000.

Clear disc state, saved header identity/metadata and selected buffer fields. r5=0 selects initialization without the completion-register write in the shared tail. The common tail also clears 0x0f000760 and leaves byte 0x0f000773.

Alternate entry: clear disc result 0x0f000787 and delivery gate 0x0f000788, then use the shared workspace reset with r5=1. This entry is not called by the initial task path. It also writes 0x0200 (EFLS) to 0x0a00001e.
Clear exactly 0x0c00 bytes at 0x09074210, then reset the associated state. Clear 0x0f0007b0 only if the prior byte at 0x0907adcb was nonzero.

Payload 0, from Change Directory to the root, while no root directory frame is known (0x0f000760 = 0): request frame 0 (0x0f0002bc), which task 6 reads as the frame at 0x09000214 plus 166, the volume descriptor. Sector count 0x0f00074c = 0 and filter mode 0x0f000771 = 0, every sector. Step 1 and the request at 0x8362.
Payload 0 without a root frame: read the volume descriptor, step 1.
Step 1: the data must start 01 "CD001", a primary volume descriptor. Otherwise step 0 and the end at 0x82be, and the state stays.
Step 1: 01 CD001 and the root directory record.
The root directory record at +156: its extent (big-endian at +6) plus 150 to 0x0f000760 and its data length (big-endian at +14) over 2048 to 0x0f000766. Then the root read at 0x7c06.

Payload 0 with a root frame, or after the volume descriptor: request frame 0x0f0002bc = root frame 0x0f000760, step 2, the sector count 0x0f000766 to 0x0f00074c, table offset 0x0f000768 and record count 0x0f00076d cleared, filter mode 0x40 (the frame range), window 0x0f000758 = first ID 2 and no files, state 1 and the request at 0x8362.
Read the root directory, step 2.

Parse directory records from r1 in the sector whose data starts at r6 into the table 0x09074210, 12 bytes each: r2 = the table plus offset 0x0f000768, r8 = the record count 0x0f00076d, r9 = the sectors left 0x0f00074c.
Parse directory records into the table, up to 256.
A record length of 0 ends the sector. Table record: +0 the extent (big-endian at +6) plus 150, +4 the data length (big-endian at +14), +8 the file unit size and interleave gap (+26, +27).

Past the identifier (length at +32, then a pad byte after an even length) the system use area starts. Without one: +10 = 0, +11 = the directory flag (bit 1 of +25). Otherwise the XA fields: +10 = the file number (area +8), +11 = bits 3..7 of the attributes' high byte (area +4) with the directory flag.
After 256 records the table is full at 0x7d82. Otherwise the next record while its offset in the sector is below 2048.

The sector is done. On the directory's last sector nothing is left to read (0x0f00075c and 0x0f000764 cleared), the rest of the 256 records is cleared and the file count is the records less the directory and its parent.

More sectors: step 4, keep the table offset, sectors left and record count, and free the slot through 0x51be under the sector lock. When partition f still holds a sector (its count differs from 0x0f00078b) parse it at 0x7954, otherwise wait at 0x77c0.

The table is full: 254 files. A next record in this sector keeps its offset at 0x0f000764. At the sector's end the offset is 0 and one sector fewer is left, and when none is left nothing is left to read.
Otherwise 0x0f00075c = the frame of the sector that holds the next record: the directory's frame (record 0) plus its sectors less the sectors left.
The window keeps its first ID with the file count. No files clears the whole word 0x0f000758. State 2 and the end at 0x82be.
Place file ID 0x0f000748 & 0xffffff, kept at 0x0f000754, against the window 0x0f000758 (first ID << 8 | file count). IDs 0 and 1 (the directory and its parent) return r1 = 0 and r2 = the ID.
Place a file ID against the window: 0 in it (r2 the table index), 1 before it, 2 past it.

Below the first ID: r1 = 1, r2 = the first ID less the ID. At or past the first ID plus the count: r1 = 2, r2 = that end less the ID, plus 1. Inside: r1 = 0, r2 = the table index, the ID less the first ID, plus 2.
Payload 1, from Change Directory: ID 0 (0x0f000754), the directory itself, only writes 0x0200 (EFLS) to 0x0a00001e and waits. Disc state stays 1.
Payload 1: read directory record 0x0f00076e, step 3.

Otherwise table record 0x0f00076e: its frame to request frame 0x0f0002bc and its data length over 2048 to 0x0f00074c, step 3, window first ID 2 with no files, table offset and record count cleared, filter mode 0x40, state 1 and the request at 0x8362.
Post 06070000 (task 6, class 7, payload 0: read from request frame 0x0f0002bc) and wait at 0x77c0.
Post 06070000 to task 6.

Payload 4, Get File Info for one file: take the transfer lock 03070000, then a type 0 transfer owned by task 7 (0x23ba) of table record 0x0f00076e, 6 words (0x0f000250 and 0x0f000254). Wait at 0x77c0.
Payload 4: a type 0 transfer of one record.
Payload 5, every file of the window: the transfer lock, then a type 0 transfer of 6 words per file (the count 0x0f00075b) from table record 2.
Payload 5: a type 0 transfer of the window's records.
Payload 2, from Read Directory: place the ID through 0x7e36 and keep the result at 0x0f00076a. In the window (0) continue at 0x803a, past it (2) at 0x7fe4.
Payload 2: move the window inside the table, or read the directory again or on.

Before the window (1): read the whole directory again, from record 0's frame with its data length over 2048, counting IDs from 0x0f000750 = 0. Table from record 2 (0x0f00076d = 2, 0x0f000768 = 24), filter mode 0x40, state 1, step 0x34 and the request at 0x8362.

Past the window (2): with nothing left to read (0x0f00075c = 0) only EFLS at 0x8042. Otherwise read on from frame 0x0f00075c with the directory's sectors left, counting IDs from the first ID plus the file count, table from record 2, state 1 and step 0x34. The filter mode 0x0f000771 is not set here.
In the window at index 2 or below: step 0, 0x0200 (EFLS) to 0x0a00001e and wait. Disc state stays 1.
Inside the window: the ID becomes the first ID of 0x0f000758. The records from index r2 move down to index 2 and the table offset follows them.
With nothing left to read: the file count is the records moved, the rest of the 256 records is cleared, step 0 and EFLS. Disc state stays 1.

Otherwise the record count is the records moved plus 2. Read on from frame 0x0f00075c with the directory's sectors left, filter mode 0x40, state 1, step 0x14 (parse from offset 0x0f000764) and the request at 0x8362.
Skip records from r2 in the sector whose data starts at r6, counting IDs from 0x0f000750, until the ID 0x0f000754. r9 = the sectors left 0x0f00074c.
Skip directory records up to the ID.
The sector is done. On the directory's last sector the ID was not found: step 0, state 2 and the end at 0x82be.

Otherwise keep the ID counter and the sectors left, step 0x24 (the next sector from its start), free the slot through 0x51be under the sector lock, and parse another sector at 0x7954 or wait, as at 0x7d2c.
The ID: step 0x14, table from record 2, the sectors left kept, window first ID = the ID with no files, and the parse at 0x7c50 from this record.
Payload 6, from Read File: table record 0x0f00076e and the sector offset o, 0x0f000744 & 0xffffff.
Payload 6: the file's frames through filter mode 0x41, step 5.
An interleaved file (unit size u and gap g at +8, nonzero) starts o / u units of u + g sectors plus o mod u sectors after its frame, other files o sectors after it.

That frame to request frame 0x0f0002bc, the sectors to read 0x0f00074c less o, the file number (+10) to 0x0f000770, filter mode 0x41 (the frame range and the file number), step 5 and the request at 0x8362.
End of a file system request. Under the sector lock, except after Read File (step 5): clear device 0x8f's connection (0x54f0) and empty partition f (0x5476). Then clear partition f's notify byte.
End a request: EFLS, pause, the state after an abort.
Disc state 0, post 06070001 (task 6, class 7, payload 1: pause).
After an abort (state 4) the state becomes 2 when the step's low nibble is above 4 (Read File), otherwise 0. Step 0, 0x0200 (EFLS) to 0x0a00001e and wait at 0x77c0.

Request sectors under the sector lock: CD device 0 with filter f (0x5510), f's true output with partition f (0xa0 | f), f's false output cleared (0x54f0), partition f's end with device 0x8f, and partition f emptied (0x5476).
Connect filter and partition f, set the filter record and the notification, post 06070000.
Filter record 0x0f000420 + 16f: +8 start frame 0x0f0002bc, +12 count 0x0f00074c, +2 file 0x0f000770, +0 mode 0x0f000771, the other bytes cleared.

Partition f's notify byte: 2 for Read File (step 5), with the count 0x0f00074c to 0x0f00034c for 07040001 at its end, 1 otherwise, 07040000 per sector. 0x0f00078b = the partition's count. Free the lock and post 06070000 at 0x7efe.
Class 6 payload 3, and payload 0 while busy: host status 6 at 0x0f00028a gives result 0x11.

Task 7 class 6 payload 3, and payload 0 while busy: host status 6 gives result 0x11, disc state 7 keeps the result, a header scan with bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7 retries the next frame, other states give result 0 or 3.
Disc state 3 continues at 0x84ca. Disc state 7 completes at 0x8bd4 with the result kept. Other states close delivery gate 0x0f000788 and give result 3 from disc state 4 upward, otherwise 0.

Header scan: bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7 clear closes the gate and gives result 0. Set: count down scan count 0x0907adce. At 0 the scan ends with result 2 at 0x8780, otherwise request frame 0x0f0002bc becomes 150 + 15 - count and the sector request repeats at 0x8d9a.
Save the 04 settings 0x0f00025c, 0x0f000262 and 0x0f000263 (initialization flags, ECC count, retry count) at 0x0907add0..0x0907add2, then set them to 0, 5 and 15 until 0x8c46 restores them.

Task 7 disc authentication request. Drive state 0, 6 or 7, or nonzero 0x0f00034b, gives result 0. A first track without the data bit gives result 1. A data track continues with a timer and sector reads at 0x85f0.
Host status 0x0f00028a of 0, 6 or 7, or a nonzero byte 0x0f00034b, ends the request with result 0 at 0x8bd0.
Clear 0x0907adcf, 0x0907adca, 0x0907adcc and 0x0f000789, then set 0x0f000788 to ff.
When longwords 0x0f0002e4 and 0x0f0002e8 are both at least 0x0f0002e0 / 4 (unsigned), a TOC whose last track (0x090001f9) minus first track (0x090001f5) plus one is 30 sets 0x0f00078a to 1.
Control/ADR byte of the first track entry, bits 31..24 of 0x09000068 + 4*(first-1). Bit 6 clear (no data track) gives result 1 at 0x8bd0. A set bit continues at 0x85f0 with a timer and sector reads.
Data track: start timer 07070000 with duration 200000 (TRAPA 0x24). The e0 CR3 high byte (0x0907adb4) becomes partition byte 0x0f000772.

Data track: start timer 07070000 with duration 200000, connect filter p and partition p for the E0 CR3 partition p, choose frame 150 (or a TOC entry when bit 7 of 0x0f00025f is set), set header scan count 15 and disc state 3, then request sectors.

Under lock 0b070000, 0x5510 connects filter p true output (0x40 | p) with partition p (0xa0 | p) and 0x54f0 clears the false output (0x60 | p). The partition count (0x0f000600 + 6p + 2) becomes cursor 0x0f00078b.

Release the lock. r1 gets the lock word 0b070000, but TRAPA 0x27 reads r11 from 0x8606. After an acquire at 0x8608 that waited, r11 holds 0x11aa, the dispatch address, so the release names lock record 0, whose table entry is 0. The owner check against ROM byte 3 fails, the diagnostic trap runs with r0 1 and task 7 keeps the lock. The acquire at 0x8d28 then finds the lock held by task 7 (r0 10), and 0x8d94 frees it.
Start frame address: 150 while bit 7 of 0x0f00025f is clear. When it is set, the low 24 bits of TOC entry 0x09000068 + 4 * (n - 1), where n is the byte at 0x09000000 + byte 0x09000000.
Store it at 0x0f0002bc, set header scan count 0x0907adce to 15 and disc state 0x0907adcb to 3, then request sectors at 0x8d24.
Disc state 3 sector arrival. Under lock 0b070000, 0x506c returns the slot at cursor 0x0f00078b of partition 0x0f000772 in r1. The header parser at 0x86ee follows.
Disc state 3 sector: take the sector at the cursor through 0x506c and parse it at 0x86ee.

Sector-header state-machine block. Input r1 selects a raw slot through its low 16 bits. Source = 0x09000230 + low16(r1)*0x930. All exits branch into shared firmware blocks, so this is not a standalone subroutine with an RTS return or a complete acceptance decision. Literal header_raw_sector_stride at 0x8a8c.
Sector-header state-machine block, r1=raw slot index. Reads payload +0xf8/+0xfc. Exits branch into shared firmware, without an RTS return or complete acceptance decision.
Literal header_raw_sector_base at 0x8a90.
A mode byte other than 1 sets the scan count to 1, so the mismatch path ends the scan with result 2. Literal header_scan_count_pointer at 0x8860.
Compare all 16 identifier bytes as four big-endian longwords. Each read advances r6. These reads require the Mode 1 payload at raw sector +0x10. Literal header_system_identifier at 0x8a2c.
Literal header_system_identifier_word1 at 0x8a30.
Literal header_system_identifier_word2 at 0x8a34.
Literal header_system_identifier_word3 at 0x8a38.

Preserve PR across external service 0x51be. TRAPA 0x2a/0x27 bracket this work. r1 is a sign-extended active-slot byte, r2 an unsigned cursor byte, r3=1. With VBR=0 the pair acquires/releases record 11 for owner 7, clobbering r0/r10/r12/r13 on direct return. Contention can enter the scheduler. Service 0x51be has its own ABI.
Identifier/mode mismatch processing. External service and traps precede the scan count decision. Copied header fields are not cleared here.
Literal header_sector_lock at 0x89e8.
VBR=0 selects acquire handler 0x12d2, record 11 and owner 7. Direct return clobbers r0/r10/r12/r13, and contention may hand control to the scheduler.
Literal header_partition_pointer at 0x89f0.
Literal header_sector_cursor_pointer at 0x8858.
Literal header_partition_release_pointer at 0x8840.
Read byte +2 of a six-byte record indexed by the active slot. MOV.B sign-extends it, and MULU.W uses only the low 16 bits. Literal header_partition_pointer at 0x89f0.
Literal header_partition_records_pointer at 0x89f4.
Literal header_sector_lock at 0x89e8.
VBR=0 selects release handler 0x1250. No-waiter return clears owner/lock and clobbers r0/r10/r12/r13, and a waiter triggers scheduler context saving.

Lower the scan count, a sign-extended byte. An old value of 1 gives result 2 without storing zero. Other values store their low decremented byte, then compare cursors. Literal header_scan_count_pointer at 0x8860.
Literal header_sector_cursor_pointer at 0x8858.
Different cursors retry through 0x86d2. That block acquires another sector before 0x86ee.
Equal cursors branch to shared code at 0x77c0. No header fields are cleared here.
Set r0=2 and branch to shared handling at 0x8bd0. This is not a local return code.
Set disc state 4 before copying header fields. This does not establish disc authentication. Literal header_disc_state_pointer at 0x8a08.
Sets disc state 4 and copies header fields before subsequent state/ID checks. This is not a complete authentication decision.
Copy payload +0x10..+0x17 to 0x0f000774..0x0f00077b.
Literal header_id_pointer at 0x8844.
Skip payload +0x18..+0x1f, then copy +0x20..+0x29 to 0x0f00077c..0x0f000785.
Literal header_product_number_pointer at 0x8848.

Cursor is payload +0x2a. Add unsigned 0xce to reach +0xf8. Store BE32 extension disc address and length at 0x0f00020c/0x0f000210. Both are copied without local bounds checks, before the following state/identifier gates. Literal header_extension_fields_pointer at 0x885c.
Copies payload +0xf8/+0xfc to 0x0f00020c/0x0f000210 without local bounds checks.
TRAPA 0x21 receives r11=0x06070001. Notification semantics depend on its handler.
Literal header_notification_base at 0x89ec.
Trap vector reference assumes VBR=0. Handler effects are external to this body.
Preserve PR, acquire record 11 for owner 7 through TRAPA 0x2a with VBR=0, then call 0x54f0 with r1=0x80. A different VBR selects a different vector table.
Literal header_sector_lock at 0x89e8.
VBR=0 selects acquire handler 0x12d2, record 11 and owner 7. Direct return clobbers r0/r10/r12/r13, and contention may hand control to the scheduler.
Literal header_connection_clear_pointer at 0x886c.

Read active slot and cursor after the external call. Record byte +2 minus cursor becomes r3 for 0x51be when nonzero. The subtraction can wrap if record byte is smaller. Literal header_partition_pointer at 0x89f0.
Literal header_sector_cursor_pointer at 0x8858.
Literal header_partition_records_pointer at 0x89f4.
Literal header_partition_release_pointer at 0x8840.
Literal header_sector_lock at 0x89e8.
VBR=0 selects release handler 0x1250. No-waiter return clears owner/lock and clobbers r0/r10/r12/r13, and a waiter triggers scheduler context saving.
Only state byte 0x0f0002f9 equal to 1 enters the following ID checks. Other values branch to 0x8874 with the newly copied header fields still present. Literal header_id_gate_pointer at 0x884c.
State byte gates and eight-byte ID comparison select further checks at 0x8874 or continuation at 0x8d00. Copied fields persist on either path.
State byte 0x0f0002f8 equal to 1 bypasses the saved-ID comparison. Literal header_any_id_gate_pointer at 0x8850.
Literal header_result_word_pointer at 0x8854.
