Compare copied payload +0x10..+0x17 against eight bytes at 0x0f0002f0. Either mismatch branches to 0x8874 without undoing the copied extension fields. Literal header_id_pointer at 0x8844.
Literal header_trusted_id_pointer at 0x8868.
Matching IDs write 4 to 0x0f000787, as does the bypass path.
Literal header_result_word_pointer at 0x8854.
Count down 0x00d59f80 (14000000) iterations before branching to 0x8d00. This instruction-count delay is not a calibrated timing or hardware-equivalence claim. Literal header_delay_count at 0x8870.
14000000 decrement/compare/branch iterations precede the branch to 0x8d00.
Header recognized without the trusted-ID shortcut: disc state 5. Zone z = (TCNT4 & 31) mod 13 goes to 0x0907adcd.

Disc state 5. TCNT4 selects zone z (0..12) and column c (0..69). Check positions 0x49124 + 1470 * (z + i) + 21 * c for passes 0..2, with exceptions for zones 0 and 12. Then four seeks: 0x3f435, 0x3fe51, the first position plus 0xdea, and the first position.
Base positions 0x49124 (299300, MSF 66:30:50) + 1470 * z, then 1470 and 2940 frames further (r1, r4, r5).
Column c = (TCNT4 >> 4) & 127, less 70 when it is 70 or more, so 0..69.
Offsets: 21 * c frames for all three positions, except in zone 0, where c below 2 gives the first position 42, and in zone 12, where the first two add 21 * (c mod 39) and the third 21 * (c mod 19).
Store the three check positions at 0x0907adb8, 0x0907adbc and 0x0907adc0.
Seek phase 0x0907adcf: phases 0 and 1 take targets 0x3f435 and 0x3fe51 from 0x8a24, phase 2 the first check position plus 0xdea and phase 3 the first check position.
Store the request frame at 0x0f0002bc, post 06070004 (task 6, class 7, payload 4) and wait at 0x77c0.
A seek report arrived (class 6 payload 2). From phase 2 on, report bytes 0x0f0002ec..0x0f0002ef need byte 1 >= byte 0 / 2 and byte 3 >= byte 2 / 2, unsigned and rounded down.

Seek report (class 6 payload 2). Phases 1 and 3 need a report word within 18 or 20 of the one before. Phases 2 and 3 need report byte 1 >= byte 0 / 2 and byte 3 >= byte 2 / 2. A failure gives result 3 and closes delivery gate 0x0f000788.
A failed check closes delivery gate 0x0f000788 and gives result 3 at 0x8bd0.
Report word 0x0f00027e. Even phases keep it at 0x0907adc8, advance the phase and seek again at 0x8920.

Odd phases take the difference from the kept word, which mov.w reads back sign-extended while the new word is zero-extended. More than 18 in phase 1, or more than 20 in phase 3, closes the delivery gate and gives result 3.
Phase 1 advances to phase 2 and seeks again. Phase 3 ends the seeks at 0x8a42.
Sixteen identifier bytes compared as four big-endian longwords. No string terminator is included.
After the last seek, the first check position starts the first pass.
Check pass: position r1 becomes request frame 0x0f0002bc and disc state 6, and 0x8d24 requests 3 sectors.
One pass per check position: disc state 6 and a request for 3 sectors from the position.
Disc state 6 sector arrival. Under lock 0b070000, 0x506c returns the slot at cursor 0x0f00078b. Raw sector r6 = 0x09000230 + 0x930 * slot.
Disc state 6 sector: re-scramble it (0x8f1c) and interleave it (0x8f70) into a 294-frame stream. After the third sector, compare the stream from frame 196 with bitmap row zone + pass through 0x8e6e.
0x8f1c re-scrambles raw bytes +12..+0x92f into 0x09077c0c. The slot then goes back to the pool through 0x51be, under the lock.

Sector index 0x0907adca selects where 0x8f70 spreads the 98 frames of 24 bytes at 0x09077c00: index 0 from frame 0 and index 1 from frame 98 of buffer 0x09078530, index 2 from frame 88 of 0x09078f50, which is frame 196 of the same buffer. The three sectors form one interleaved stream.
Index 0 and 1: advance the index. A partition count past the cursor means another sector is waiting, and it is checked at once. Otherwise wait at 0x77c0.
Index 2: spread the third sector, clear the index and compare the frame bytes from 0x09079790 (frame 196) with bitmap row 0x8fb4 + 16 * zone (0x0907adcd) through 0x8e6e.
Pass count 0x0907adcc: after the third pass continue at classification 0x8b62. Otherwise count the pass, advance the zone and start the next pass at the next check position.
Classification after three passes: check score 0x0f000789 below 2 closes the delivery gate and gives result 3.

Check score 0x0f000789 below 2 gives result 3 and closes the delivery gate. Otherwise result 4. A SEGASYSTEM header also sets ID gate 0x0f0002f9 (and 0x0f0002f8 with the 30-track flag), keeps the header ID at 0x0f0002f0 and stores 1 at 0x0f000786.
Compare header bytes 0x0f00077c..0x0f000785 with SEGASYSTEM at 0x8cf4. Any difference stores result 4 at 0x0f000787 and continues at 0x8d00.

SEGASYSTEM: set ID gate 0x0f0002f9, and any-ID gate 0x0f0002f8 when 30-track flag 0x0f00078a is 1. Copy header ID 0x0f000774..0x0f00077b to 0x0f0002f0 and store bytes 1 and 4 at 0x0f000786, the word E1 reports. Continue at 0x8d00.

Store result r0 at 0x0f000787, the byte e1 subcode 0 reports. Cancel timer 07070000 with TRAPA 0x25. Disc state 2 (an e0 request) continues at 0x8c3e. Other states first release sector state from 0x8be6.
Store the result at 0x0f000787 and cancel timer 07070000. Branches arrive from the E0 request at 0x8510, the class 6 path at 0x8494, the header parser at 0x8782, and from 0x8986, 0x89ca and 0x8b74.

States other than 2: under lock 0b070000 clear the CD device connection (0x54f0 with 0x80), clear the partition notify byte, release sectors past cursor 0x0f00078b and clear the filter record mode, start and count. Continue at 0x8c3e.
Outside disc state 2: disconnect CD device 0, clear the partition notify byte, return sectors past cursor 0x0f00078b to the pool and clear filter p.
Post 06070003 (task6, class 7, payload 3) with TRAPA 0x21, then restore the three 04 settings saved at 0x0907add0.
After an E0 request, post 06070003 to task 6, restore the saved 04 settings, clear 0x0907adcb and busy flag 0x0f0007b0, write 0x0200 to 0x0a00001e and wait at 0x77c0.
Result 0x11 re-enters disc initialization 0x7abc through 0x7838. Otherwise clear disc state 0x0907adcb and busy flag 0x0f0007b0, write 0x0200 to 0x0a00001e and wait again at 0x77c0.
Every path here has stored result 4. Clear the expansion area through 0x1b5e and prepare a disc extension through 0x19ec. A return of 0 completes at 0x8bd4.

Result 4 is stored on every path here (0x883c, 0x8ba0, 0x8bcc). Clear the expansion area through 0x1b5e and prepare a disc extension through 0x19ec. With an extension, disc state 7 reads its sectors from the header's extension address.
An extension to read: request frame 0x0f0002bc = extension address 0x0f00020c and disc state 7. The sector request at 0x8d24 follows, with count byte 0x0f000208.

Sector request under lock 0b070000: filter record 0x0f000420 + 16p gets frame address 0x0f0002bc at +8 and a count at +12 (15 from 0x0907adce in state 3, 3 in state 6, byte 0x0f000208 otherwise), then mode 0x40 (frame range).
Filter record 0x0f000420 + 16p gets a frame range (count 15, 3 or 0x0f000208 by disc state), partition notify bit 0 is set, CD device 0 is connected to filter p and 06070002 goes to task 6.
Set partition notify bit 0 (0x0f000600 + 6p + 3) and connect CD device 0 (0x80) with filter p through 0x5510.

Release the lock, post 06070002 (task 6, class 7, payload 2) and wait at 0x77c0. r1 gets the lock word 0b070000, but TRAPA 0x27 reads r11 from 0x8d26. After an acquire at 0x8d28 that waited, r11 holds 0x11aa, so the release names lock record 0, fails its owner check with diagnostic 1, and task 7 waits at 0x77c0 still holding the lock.

Disc state 7 sector arrival. Under lock 0b070000, 0x506c returns the slot at the cursor. 0x1a38 copies its payload and returns the bytes still to come, or 0 once the last sector has been decoded and checked. The value goes to 0x0907adc4.
Disc state 7 sector: collect it through 0x1a38. After the last sector has been decoded and checked the request completes with result 4 kept.
Release the slot through 0x51be and read the partition count, under the lock.
A return of 0 completes at 0x8bd4 with the result kept. Otherwise collect the next sector when one is waiting past the cursor, or wait at 0x77c0.
Compare 106 columns of frame bytes from r1 with bitmap row r2 (16 bytes, most significant bit first). Column k spans byte count k of 0x9104. A row bit of 1 expects byte a8, a 0 expects 59.

Compare 106 columns of interleaved bytes with one bitmap row: a8 where the bit is set, 59 where it is clear. A column of n bytes is good when at least (n - m) / 2 match, rounded down, with m 1 for a mask column, 2 for column 8 and 0 otherwise. 11 bad columns in a row stop the walk. 85 good columns add 1 to check score 0x0f000789.
Threshold: the column byte count, less 1 when mask bit k of 0x90c4 is set (less 2 in column 8), halved and rounded down.
At least the threshold of matching bytes makes a good column and ends a run of bad columns. The walk stops after 11 bad columns in a row.
Every 32 columns load the next row and mask words. The bit counter is byte 0x0907add3.
85 or more good columns add 1 to check score 0x0f000789.
Re-apply the CD-ROM scrambler of ECMA-130 Annex B (x^15 + x + 1, first bytes 01 80 00 60) to 1170 words from r6, writing them to r7. Each stored word holds its scrambled byte pair in swapped order.
Re-apply the ECMA-130 CD-ROM scrambler to raw sector bytes 12..2351, byte pairs swapped.
r1 holds the generator state in a shifted form. This block runs twice per word and leaves the next two scrambler bytes in bits 15..0, the second byte high.
Spread r6 frames of 24 bytes from r5 into buffer r9 from frame r4. Byte k of a frame goes to offset k of the 24 halfwords at 0x90d4 after the frame start.
Interleave 24-byte frames: each byte moves to its own position 3 to 108 frames later (offsets at 0x90d4).
The offsets (72..2615) give each of the 24 bytes its own position in a frame 3 to 108 frames later. Every position is covered once, so consecutive frames interleave without overlap.
Bitmap of the SEGA logo: 17 rows of 106 bits, 16 bytes per row, row 0 at the bottom. The checks use rows 0..14.
One bit per column, most significant first. A set bit lowers that column's threshold.
24 byte offsets from a frame start, 72..2615.
Bytes per column, 106 entries, 884 in total.
The status byte in r0: 0 (BUSY) while 0x0f0002a6 has bit 3 or 5, 9 (ERROR) with bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7, otherwise byte 0 of the status buffer 0x0f000274 when 0x0f00027c is set, else 0x0f00026c.
The status byte of a response: BUSY while a command waits for its reply, ERROR after a read error, otherwise byte 0 of the last status buffer.
Status byte with 0x40 ORed in through r2, the data transfer request bit, for a command that starts a transfer to the host.
Status byte with the data transfer request bit 0x40.
Replace response high byte from local status: +0x4a bits0x28 force zero, +0x4b bit8 forces 9, otherwise select cached status byte by state +0x20. OR in r2 status mask.
Reject entry sets status mask ff and joins cached response construction. r11 is cleared by caller.
Cached response with 0x80 in r2, the wait bit. The negative r2 rebuilds the status byte at 0x91aa.
Cached response with the wait bit 0x80.
Command 00 clears r11 and returns cached response. Alternate entry 0x91f6 sets task6 state +0x4a bit3 while preserving outgoing message.
Cached response keeping the message in r11: status mask 0, then 0x9200.
Flag 0x0f0007b0 bit0 selects sentinel response 00ffffff/ffffffff. Otherwise read cached pair +0x10 or +0x18, with selector +0x20.
Optional low 24 response bits come from state longword +0x50, keeping the r13 high byte.
State +0x4a mask0x28 clears response high byte. Otherwise +0x4b bit8 forces low28 bits09ffffff and r13=ffffffff. Negative r2 then rebuilds status high byte.
Command 01: CR2 = hardware flag 0x0f00027d << 8 | 1, CR3 and CR4 = longword 0x0f0002fc. The status byte comes from 0x91a8. No message.
Command 01: hardware flag, version 1 and longword 0x0f0002fc (MPEG version, drive information, CD block revision). No message.
Command 02 through the gate: host status 0x0f00028a of 0 answers with the wait status. Otherwise post 0681000d (task 6 payload 13, the TOC) with CR2 = 0xcc words and CR3, CR4 = 0.
Command 02: 0xcc words of TOC through task 6 payload 13. Wait status before the drive has a host status.
Shared with 20: r11 = 06810000 | r0 and the data transfer request status at 0x91a4. Bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6 is not set.
Command 03, session r1 = CR1 low byte: host status 0 answers with the wait status. CR3 and CR4 are ffffffff when session count byte 0x09000000 is ff or below r1. No message.
Command 03: session count and lead-out, or a session's first track and start. No message.

Session 0 returns TOC entry 0 (0x09000064). Session n returns its first track (byte 0x09000000 + n) in bits 31..24 over that track's start frame minus 150, or over bits 23..0 of 0x09000214 when the track entry is ffffffff.
Command 04: CR4 high and low bytes go to 0x0f000262 and 0x0f000263 unless ff, CR2 to the standby word 0x0f000260 unless ffff.
Command 04: standby word and bytes 0x0f000262/0x0f000263, then task 6 payload 0 (reset) or 8 (pause).

CR1 low byte with bit 7 clear is stored at 0x0f00025c, and with bit 0 set posts 06810000 (payload 0, the reset request). Otherwise post 06810008 (payload 8, pause). Both through 0x91f6, which sets bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6.
Command 05 produces message 06810002, destination task6, class81, payload0002, then sets state +0x4a bit3 and builds response. Later task6 work is separate.
Return message 06810002 and mark pending flag at task6 state+74. Response uses cached status. Task 6 handles the message later.

Command 10: CR3 high byte to play mode 0x0f00025d. Start r1 = CR1 low byte and CR2, end r2 = CR3 low byte and CR4, 24 bits each. Both ffffff post 06810005 (payload 5, play the current range) through 0x91f6.
Command 10: play range from two track or frame positions, task 6 payload 3, 4 or 5.
A start of ffffff takes the range start 0x0f000298: bits 23..0 of a track-form start (top byte nonzero), a frame start with bit 23 set, or 0.
An end of ffffff takes the range end 0x0f00029c: bits 23..0 after a track-form start, 00ffffff (keep the end) for a nonzero frame end, or 0.
Both 0 post payload 4. Two nonzero positions of different kinds (bit 23) take the reject response at 0x91e8.

Bit 23 in either position posts 06810004 (play frames). Otherwise 06810003 (play tracks) with bits 23..16 of both cleared. The start goes to 0x0f000264 and the end to 0x0f000268, then 0x91f6 sets bit 3 of 0x0f0002a6.

Command 11, position r1 = CR1 low byte and CR2: ffffff posts 06810008 (payload 8, pause) and 0 posts 06810009 (payload 9, stop). Bit 23 set posts 06810007 (seek to a frame), clear 06810006 (seek to a track and index), with the position less bit 23 at 0x0f000264. All through 0x91f6.
Command 11: task 6 payload 6 (track), 7 (frame), 8 (pause) or 9 (stop).
Command 12, direction r1 = CR1 low byte: 0 posts 0681000a (payload 10, forward) and 1 posts 0681000b (payload 11, backward) through 0x91f6. Larger values take the reject response.
Command 12: task 6 payload 10 (forward) or 11 (backward).

Command 20 through the gate, type = CR1 low byte. Type 0 posts 0681000c (payload 12, the Q record) at 0x92a6 with CR2 = 5 words and CR3, CR4 = 0. Type 1 continues at 0x6354. Other types take the reject response.
Command 20 type 0: 5 words of Q record through task 6 payload 12. Type 1 at 0x6354.

Command 70 (Change Directory): r1 = CR1 << 16 | CR2 and r2 = CR3 << 16 | CR4, kept at 0x0f000744 and 0x0f000748. Filter f, the CR3 high byte, of 24 or more rejects. State 4 (0x0f00076b, an abort in progress) waits.
Command 70: ffffff posts payload 0 (the root), other IDs in the window that name a directory payload 1.
File ID ffffff, the root: keep f at 0x0f000772, set disc state 0x0907adcb to 1 and post payload 0.
Other IDs need state 2, otherwise 0x96e4. The ID must be in the directory table (0x7e36), which gives its index in r2.
Table record r2 (0x09074210, 12 bytes each), attribute byte +11: with any of bits 3..7 (the XA attributes) bit 7, the XA directory bit, must be set, otherwise bit 1, the ISO 9660 directory flag.
Keep the index at 0x0f00076e and f at 0x0f000772, set disc state 1 and post payload 1.

Command 71 (Read Directory): CR1..CR4 kept at 0x0f000744. Filter f of 24 or more rejects, state 4 waits and states other than 2 go to 0x96e4. Otherwise keep f, set disc state 1 and post payload 2. Task 7 places the file ID.
Command 71: posts payload 2, task 7 places the ID.
Command 72 (Get File System Scope): CR1..CR4 kept at 0x0f000744. State 4 waits and states other than 2 go to 0x96e4.
Command 72: the window's file count, first ID and end flag.

The end flag, bit 24 of r13, is set when nothing is left to read (0x0f00075c and 0x0f000764 both 0). r13 low bits = the window's first ID (0x0f000758 >> 8), r12 = its file count (0x0f00075b). Answered through 0x91a8, no message.
Command 73 (Get File Info), through the data-command gate: CR1..CR4 kept at 0x0f000744, r2 = the file ID. State 4 waits and states other than 2 go to 0x96e4.
Command 73, through the data-command gate: 6 words per file, payload 4 for one ID, 5 for ffffff.
One file: its index from 0x7e36 must be in the table and goes to 0x0f00076e, then 6 words and payload 4.
ID ffffff, every file of the window: 6 words for each of the 0x0f00075b files, none rejects, and payload 5.

Command 74 (Read File): CR1..CR4 kept at 0x0f000744. The CR1 low byte and CR2 are the sector offset, the CR3 high byte filter f, the CR3 low byte and CR4 the file ID. f of 24 or more rejects, state 4 waits and states other than 2 go to 0x96e4.
Command 74: an ID in the window and an offset below its sectors post payload 6.
The index from 0x7e36 goes to 0x0f00076e before the check that the ID is in the table.
The file's data length (+4) in sectors, rounded up, goes to 0x0f00074c. An offset below it keeps f, sets disc state 1 and posts payload 6, otherwise reject.
Command 75 (Abort File): in state 4 answer with r11 = 0 and post nothing. Otherwise post payload 7.
Command 75: payload 7, or no message in state 4.
States other than 2 and 4: 1 (a read in progress) waits, others reject.
Shared ends of 70..75: state checks, post, reject, wait and the Get File Info response.
Post: r11 = 07810000 | the payload and the response from 0x91fe.
Reject: the response from 0x91e8 with r11 cleared.
Wait: the wait response from 0x91ec with r11 cleared.
Get File Info: r12 = 6 words per file, r13 = 0, r11 = 07810000 | the payload and the data transfer request response from 0x91a4.
Call the response entry in r0 and return.

ITU3 input capture B (vector 93): a falling edge on TIOCB3 (PB3) moves one byte. Clear IMFB in TSR3 and the full-save flag. Link state at 0x0f000304: out bytes +0..+11, received sum +12, byte count +13, full-save flag +14.

ITU3 input capture B (vector 93), one strobe per byte on TIOCB3. A frame is 13 SCI0 transfers: 11 command bytes and their inverted sum out, 11 report bytes and their inverted sum in, then an answer byte (00 for a matching sum). PB2 low starts or restarts a frame.
Within a frame: PB2 (bit 2 of 0x05ffffc3) low restarts it from byte 0. Otherwise the count goes up by one.
Out byte count - 1 goes to TDR0. From count 2 on, the byte in RDR0 goes to report byte count - 2 (0x0f0002d0..0x0f0002da) and is added to the sum.
Clearing SSR0 starts the transfer. A frame start continues through the scheduler at 0x102e, other strobes return with RTE.

Count 13: the received byte is the checksum. It must equal the inverted sum of the 11 report bytes. A match sets valid flag 0x0f0002db and answers 00, a mismatch answers 01. SCR0 bit 6 (RIE) enables the receive interrupt for the final byte.
No frame running (count 0 or 0x80): save the full context in the current task record and switch to stack 0x0f0008f8. PB2 high sets count 0x80 and waits.
PB2 low: count 0x80 resends the packet already at 0x0f000304. Count 0 builds a new one, a null packet (eleven zeros, checksum ff) while pending byte 0x0f0002cf is 0, otherwise the staged command.
Frame start: clear valid flag 0x0f0002db and the sum, then send byte 0 with count 1.
Copy command bytes 0x0f0002c4..0x0f0002ce, set out byte 11 to the inverted sum of bytes 0..10 and clear the pending byte.

SCI0 receive (vector 101) after the answer byte: save the full context and switch to stack 0x0f0008f8. The drive's final byte in RDR0 is 0 for a new packet next frame (count 0), anything else resends the last one (count 0x80).
SCI0 receive (vector 101) after the answer byte. The drive's final byte selects a new packet (00) or a repeat of the last one. Posts 06830000, the drive report, to task 6.
Clear RIE, post 06830000 (task 6, class 0x83) with TRAPA 0x21 and continue through the scheduler at 0x102e.

Decoder wrapper. Helper code and constants occupy 0x9904..0x9ce3. Custom register ABI: r1 source, r2 destination, r3 byte length, r0 result (0 or -1). Default decompiler calling conventions are not authoritative for this routine. N = byte length >> 3. Rejects N < 2, processes N-1 eight-byte blocks and checks an XOR trailer after writing output.
Decode loop. Remaining count determines block schedule.
Helper returns here after its manipulated return chain.
Compare intermediate-state XOR accumulators with the final input block.
Restore caller PR and return 0 on match, -1 otherwise.
NOP padding (0x0009) between function bodies.
Literal 0x0f00078c, loaded at 0x9924.

Seed the descending-count schedule and start mixing r4/r5. r13 is fixed scratch, and r12 becomes the marker arithmetic base (0x99ec). r0..r11 are interleaved payload/schedule temporaries, not an ordinary ABI.
Seed count-derived state and code-as-data constants.
Saved wrapper PR is 0x993c, not the seed caller PR (0x9b86). Subtracting marker base produces 0xffffff50. This address difference is data.
Scratch +8 holds k, the remaining payload count, descending from N-1 to 1.
Code-as-data: base 0x99fc, then reads at +4 and +0x10 below. Keep instruction spelling/addresses exact, even where register work looks dead.
Reads 0x63a37301 from instructions at 0x9a00 and stores it at scratch +0x1c.
Reads 0x6009301c from instructions at 0x9a0c.
r7 = r6 survives the return. XOR at 0x9b98 later forces r7 to zero.
Pointer to 0x99ec, used in return-address differences.
Pointer to marker start at 0x99e4.
Hitachi.PublicKeyCipher. is read as arithmetic constants. The name does not establish a public-key scheme.
Mix schedule/payload, and insert 0x9b3c into the saved return chain. Called by 0x9c64. Returns to 0x9c68 with one extra saved word still on stack.
Mix state and insert 0x9b3c in saved return chain.
Both executed and read at 0x99ac: this instruction pair is 0x63a37301.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x99ac.
Saved PR is 0x9c68. Dereference it at 0x9a0a to read 0xe77f6203.
Both executed and read at 0x99be: this instruction pair is 0x6009301c.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x99be.

Stack edit interleaved with arithmetic. Top-first before: 9c68,9bf4,993c. After 0x9a40: 9c68,9bf4,9b3c,993c. Original outer caller lies below both. The extra word delays return to wrapper until the continuation finishes.
Top-first: 9c68,9bf4,993c becomes 9c68,9bf4,9b3c,993c.
MOVA materializes the continuation address, a return target rather than a call.
Final schedule/payload stage. Produces r4/r5, then returns through 0x9c58. Some scratch and accumulator calculations do not affect the output.
Final stage assigns emitted r4/r5 at 0x9b30/0x9b32.
With this call nesting [SP+8] is the wrapper PR 0x993c. Subtract 0x99ec and rotate twice: 0xffffff50 -> 0xfffffd43.
These accumulator loads affect scratch/temporary work, but not final r4/r5. These loads contribute scratch writes even though their values do not affect emitted words.
Overwrites r3 after accumulator-dependent work.
Unsigned low-half x high-half product, read from MACL, then three rotations.
Only now assign the emitted pair. Trailer accumulation used earlier intermediate words.
NOP padding (0x0009) between function bodies.
Entered via RTS at 0x9bf6, not BSR. No PR push on entry: the original wrapper return (0x993c) is already on stack. r8 carries the old first accumulator from 0x9c9a. Load the second into r9.
Entered by RTS at 0x9bf6. No PR push, the saved wrapper return is already on stack.
Trailer XORs this intermediate r4/r5 pair. Output mixing continues afterward. First accumulator stored at 0x9b6e, second at 0x9cae.
Finally consume the original block return and resume wrapper at 0x993c.
Consume saved 0x993c and return to wrapper.
NOP padding (0x0009) between function bodies.
Per-block entry: r4/r5 input, scratch +8 descending count. Every valid block traverses all helpers and the inserted continuation.
Per-block entry. All 423 helper instructions execute for each valid block. Custom register/stack convention.
Instruction pair 0x40044804 is also read via live PR+0x10 at 0x9c34.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x9c34.
Seed left r7 == r6, so this makes r7 zero for every payload/count.
SHLL seeds T, then ROTCL r5/r4 rotates the 64-bit payload pair. r9 is zero here. ROTCL r9 consumes T but always emits T=0.
Everything through BT preserves T, including SHLL8/SHLR8/SHLR16.
Invariant false branch: T=0 from 0x9bd2. Always call the middle mix. Retain this non-delayed BT and the following BSR/NOP pair for exact reproduction.
T is always zero. BT always falls through to BSR 0x9c60.
PR popped here is the inserted 0x9b3c, not the original wrapper return.
Pop inserted 0x9b3c, then RTS enters the continuation.
Post-accumulation output mixing, called from continuation at 0x9b74.
Post-accumulation mixing, code constant from live PR+0x10.
STS.L on entry saved PR without changing it. Live PR is still 0x9b78.
Read PR+0x10 = 0x9b88, the instruction pair 0x40044804.
Final stage assigns r4/r5. Return here, then through continuation at 0x9b78.
NOP padding (0x0009) between function bodies.
Middle mixing always runs. Helper at 0x99fc rewrites saved return words.
Always runs and invokes the saved-return editor.
OR r0,r0 preserves both r0 and T.
r7=127 is overwritten, but these bytes are read at 0x9a0a as 0xe77f6203. Removing this apparently dead assignment changes the transform.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x9a0a.
Carry old accumulator A in r8 into the inserted continuation.
Called by continuation after XOR updates. Commit accumulator B at 0x9cae. Scratch +0x18/+0x1c now carry schedule words into the output stage.
Commit second accumulator and continue mixing.
Store old B XOR intermediate r5, before the remaining output mixing.

DMA channel 2 end (vector 76, ROM longword 0x0130), the channel the card's video data request drives. Save r0..r13, PR, GBR, MACH and MACL, keep the frame pointer in the current record and switch to the interrupt workspace 0x0f0008f8.
DMA channel 2 end (vector 76), the card's video data channel: clear IE, set bit 1 of 0x0f000892 and post 08890008 to task 8's entry 51.
Clear IE in CHCR2 (bit 2 of 0x05ffff6f) and post 08890008, task 8's offset 8, entry 51.
Set bit 1 of 0x0f000892, which makes 9C wait, and continue through the scheduler at 0x102e.

98, entry 8 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. Keep CR1:CR2 at 0x09075380, since service 89 (stub 0xf8ee) changes r1, then r11 = the r12 it returns, the status byte over r12's low 24 bits.

98 (CDC_MpGetTc), entry 8, replaced by the known cards: the frame bank, picture type and temporal reference in CR1 and CR2, the time code in CR3 and CR4, read from the card at 0x0a100022, from entry 37's record, or by the bank in 0x0a100006 from the records at 0x090752e4 and 0x090752f4. The wait path returns with r11 nonzero.
With bit 6 of the word 0x0f000868 clear and bit 3 of 0x0f000897 set: the wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896). That path returns with r11 as above, which the IRQ6 exit posts.
Bit 3 clear: write 6, 4 and 5 to the card register 0x0a100022, each read back after five nops. r12 = the word for 6, r13 = the low byte for 4 << 16 | the word for 5, r2 = 0.
Bit 6 set, with bit 3 of the word and bit 0 of CR2 clear: r2 = bits 6 and 7 of the byte 0x09075312, r12 = the word 0x0907530c and r13 = the longword 0x09075304, which entry 37 keeps.
Otherwise r2 = bits 6 and 7 of the card register 0x0a100006, r12 = the longword 0x090752e4 + 4 * r2 and r13 = the longword 0x090752f4 + 4 * r2.

r12 = r2 << 16 | bits 13 and 14 << 8 | bits 0..5 of r12. r13 takes bits 0..5, 6..11, 13..18 and 19..26 of r13 into its bytes from the low one up, the pictures, seconds, minutes and hours of an MPEG time code.
The status byte from r11 over r12, then r11 = 0: nothing is posted.

99, entry 9 of the ROM table: the status byte through service 89 (stub 0xf8ee). r12's low 24 bits stay as the IRQ6 entry passed them, the current task record's address. r13 = the longword 0x090752a4. Nothing is posted.
99 (CDC_MpGetPts), entry 9: the longword 0x090752a4 in r13.

9F, entry 15. With bit 3 of 0x0f000897 set: the wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896). That path returns without clearing r11, which the IRQ6 entry and the group dispatch leave as the interrupted code had it, and the IRQ6 exit posts it when nonzero.
9F (CDC_MpGetPictSiz), entry 15: the picture size from the card register 0x0a100022 at indexes 0 and 1, 12 bits each. Waits with bit 3 of 0x0f000897.
Bit 3 clear: the status byte through service 89. GBR = 0x0a100000, which stays set.
Write 0 to the card register 0x0a100022, read it after five nops, write 1 and read it again. r13 = (first word & 0x0fff) << 16 | (second word & 0x0fff), r11 = 0: nothing is posted.
A1, entry 17 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. CR1's low byte selects a window setting 0..4, and bit 0 of CR2's low byte writes the settings to the card. GBR = 0x0f000854.

A1 (CDC_MpSetWinFpos, CDC_MpSetWinFrat, CDC_MpSetWinDpos, CDC_MpSetWinDsiz, CDC_MpSetWinDofs), entry 17, replaced by the known cards: setting 0..4 from CR1's low byte, values from CR3 and CR4 into 0x0f00085a..0x0f000865, or for the display position and offset into 0x0907531c..0x09075323 and their sum into 0x0f000856. Doubled while bit 3 of 0x0f000854 is set. Bit 0 of CR2 writes 0x0f000856..0x0f000865 to 0x0a100002..0x0a100011.
Setting 1: CR4 to the word 0x0f000864 and CR3 to 0x0f000862, each unless its bit 14 is set.
Setting 4: CR4 to 0x09075322 and CR3 to 0x09075320, each unless its bit 15 is set. The longwords 0x0907531c and 0x09075320 added give the words 0x0f000856 (high) and 0x0f000858 (low).
The other settings: with bit 3 of the word 0x0f000854 set, CR3 and CR4 are each doubled, keeping bit 15.
Setting 0: CR4 to 0x0f000860 and CR3 to 0x0f00085e, each unless its bit 15 is set.
Setting 2: CR4 to 0x0907531e and CR3 to 0x0907531c, each unless its bit 15 is set, then the sums to 0x0f000856 and 0x0f000858 as for setting 4.
Setting 3: CR4 to 0x0f00085c and CR3 to 0x0f00085a, each unless its bit 15 is set.
Any other setting: the reject response through entry 66 (stub 0xf892), r11 = 0.
With bit 0 of CR2 set, the words 0x0f000856..0x0f000864 to the card registers 0x0a100002..0x0a100010. Then the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a), r11 = 0.
Write 0x7fff to MPEG card register 0x0a10001a.
Task 8, the MPEG task, writes 0x7fff to MPEG card register 0x0a10001a, clears two RAM state regions and waits for a message at 0xa022.
Preserve the inherited PR across the RAM initializer. No device read or message post.
Trap 0x23 saves continuation 0xa024. The common state-1 resume may replace it with the decoded-disc task-8 pointer at 0x09075820 before delivering r11.
The low byte is a BYTE offset, with no scaling, range or alignment check here. The table's six entries use offsets 0,4,8,12,16,20. Upper message bytes are ignored.
Use low message byte as an unchecked byte offset into the six-pointer table at 0xa034. State-1 resumption can instead use the decoded-disc task-8 hook at 0x09075820.

Six MPEG task handler pointers, selected by byte offsets 0,4,8,12,16,20. Five are expansion entry stubs. Offset 24 reads the following card-address literal, since this dispatcher has no local range or alignment check.
93. With the expansion's version byte 0x0907b000 at 0, no card extension loaded, the response is ff000000 with r13 = 0 and no message.

93. Rejected with ff000000 without a loaded extension. CR2 bit 0 set with the card bit clear posts 08810004 (task 8 activation at 0xa41c). Otherwise the card bit is cleared when bit 0 is clear, the channels stop and 08890000, 088a0000, 088c0000, 09810000 and 08810000 are posted. The response comes from entry 68.
CR2 bit 0 (bit 0 of r1) clear goes to 0xa078. Set with the card bit clear: after the response, post 08810004, which task 8 takes at 0xa41c. Set with the card bit set: the reset at 0xa07c.
CR2 bit 0 clear: clear the card bit, then reset.
Stop the card channels (0xa490), clear the bytes 0x09075388..0x0907538a, then post 08890000, 088a0000, 088c0000 and 09810000. 08810000 is posted after the response.
The response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a). r11 is kept for the IRQ6 exit to post.
AF, from group A's table without the expansion table. r12 = r13 = 0, then the status byte through 0x91a8 (service 89) with r1 and r2 kept.
AF, without the expansion table: writes CR4 to a card register at 0x0a100000 or 0x0a180000 plus an even offset, or reads it.
The card register: 0x0a100000, or 0x0a180000 with bit 1 of CR1's low byte set, plus CR2's low byte rounded down to even.
Bit 0 of CR1's low byte clear: CR4 to the register, then the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a).
Bit 0 set: r13 = the register's word, sign-extended, and r12 the status byte alone. Nothing is posted either way.

AE, from group A's table without the expansion table. r12 = r13 = 0, then the status byte through 0x91a8 (service 89) with r1 kept. r13 becomes the word the firmware keeps for a card register, sign-extended. Nothing is posted.
AE, without the expansion table: the word the firmware keeps for a card register, from 0x0f000854 by offset or 0x0f000884.

With bit 1 of CR1's low byte set, the word 0x0f000884, kept for 0x0a180008. Otherwise from 0x0f000854 by CR2's low byte rounded down to even: below 0x16 at that offset, 0x16..0x1c at the offset - 4, from 0x1e on at the offset - 6.
ITU2 input capture B (vector 89, ROM longword 0x0164): a falling edge of TIOCB2, one of the card's two interrupt lines. Save the full frame and switch to 0x0f0008f8.

ITU2 input capture B (vector 89), a falling edge of TIOCB2: three reads of 0x0a100000 ANDed into the video status word 0x0f000846, the MPEG interrupt flags with MPST, MPCM for an interval, entries 38..40, and work for task 8's entry 35 through 0x0f000896 and 088c0010.
Clear IMFB in TSR2. r1 = the AND of three reads of the card register 0x0a100000, five nops apart, so a bit counts as set only when every read has it.
With the card bit (bit 7 of 0x0f000892) clear, only count at 0xa340.
The word 0x0f000850 becomes r1 masked with the old word 0x0f000852 or 0x030f, and 0x0f000852 becomes ffff.
The video status word 0x0f000846 takes bits 0..3, 5, 6 and 8 (0x016f) from r1 inverted. With bit 4 of r1 set they are ORed in, with it clear they replace the old ones.
r4 collects work for task 8. Bit 6 of r1 clear: r4 bit 1, and with bit 2 or 6 of 0x0f000893 set, entry 40 through 0xf82a with r13 = 0x0f000890.
Bit 13 clear: set bit 0 of 0x0f000891 and bit 10 of the MPEG interrupt flags 0x0f000848 (bit 2 of 0x0f00084a). With that bit set in the mask 0x0f00084c too, write 0x2000 (MPST) to 0x0a00001e.
Bit 12 clear: set bit 2 of 0x0f000891. Bit 11 clear: r4 bit 0.
Bit 15 clear: set bit 4 of the MPEG interrupt flags (bit 4 of 0x0f00084b), and write MPST when the mask has it.

Bit 4 clear: r4 bit 2. With bit 0 or 4 of 0x0f000893 set, bits 0 and 6 of the word 0x0f000868 set and the state 0x0f00089c at 4 or 5, bit 0 calls entry 38 and bit 4 entry 39. Then write 0x1000 (MPCM) to 0x0a00001e.
Any bit in r4 is ORed into 0x0f000896 and posts 088c0010, task 8's offset 16, entry 35. Continue through the scheduler at 0x102e.
The card bit clear: add 0x0100 to the word 0x0f00089e when bit 4 of r1 is clear and 1 when bit 5 is clear. Nothing is posted.
Capture B with the card bit clear: count bits 4 and 5 of the status word clear in 0x0f00089e and 0x0f00089f.
Configure the MPEG card windows at 0x0a100000/0x0a180000 and channel registers. The channel-start helper changes GBR to 0x05ffff00, used by the remaining writes.
Collect register/channel readback failures into r8 bits 0..3. Stop the channels, then return that mask in both r0 and r1.
Task 8, message payload 4, posted by 93 to activate the card. Write 0x7fff to 0x0a10001a and start the card channels (0xa460).
Task 8 payload 4: 0x7fff to 0x0a10001a, card channels start (0xa460), MPEG state and card bit cleared (0xa4d0), entry 34 (the ROM's 0xa4f0 sets the card bit), MPED, then entry 32.
Clear the MPEG state with the card bit (0xa4d0), then call entry 34 through the stub 0xf812. On the known cards that is the ROM table's 0xa4f0, which sets the card bit.
Write 0x0800 (MPED) to 0x0a00001e and jump to entry 32 through the stub 0xf80a, task 8's wait 0xa022 on the known cards.
Mask status bits and start the three configured channels. GBR remains 0x05ffff00.
Stop the configured channels and clear their selected status bits, keeping r8.
Clear 24 longwords, descending from 0x0f00089c through 0x0f000840 inclusive. The +4 compensates for predecrement stores. PR, SP, GBR, VBR and r14 survive.
Clear 24 internal-RAM longwords and 83 buffer-RAM longwords in descending order. Returns with T=1, with no device reads, calls or message posting.
Clear 83 longwords, descending from 0x090753e8 through 0x090752a0 inclusive. Exit r0=0, r11=r12=0x090752a0, T=1. No code bytes are used as data.
Entry 34 of the ROM table, which task 8's activation calls through the stub 0xf812. First entry 33 through the stub 0xf80e, 0xa52c in the ROM table.

Entry 34 of the ROM table, from task 8's activation: entry 33, 0x8209 to 0x0a180008 and 0 to 0x0a180000, then 0x67818022 to 0x0f000890 (the card bit among it), -1 to 0x0f000850, 0x0101 to 0x0f000898..0x0f00089d and 20 to 0x090752e0.
Read 0x0a180008 and discard the word, then write 0x8209 to 0x0f000884 and 0x0a180008, and 0 to 0x0a180000.

0x67818022 to 0x0f000890: 0x67, 0x81, 0x80 (the card bit) and 0x22 in bytes 0x0f000890..0x0f000893. Then -1 to 0x0f000850, 0x0101 to the words 0x0f000898, 0x0f00089a and 0x0f00089c, and 20 to the word 0x090752e0.
Entry 33 of the ROM table. From 0x0f000854: 0x88fe0096, 0x002602c0, the word 0x01e0 at +8, the words 1 at +14 and +16, 0xfff3ff7e at +20 and 0xffff47af at +24.
Entry 33 of the ROM table: MPEG state from 0x0f000854, then card registers 0x0a100020, 0x0a10001a, 0x0a100014, 0x0a100002 and 0x0a100000.
Card registers: 0x47af to 0x0a100020, 0xff7e to 0x0a10001a, 0xfff3 to 0x0a100014, 0x0096 to 0x0a100002 and 0x88fe to 0x0a100000. GBR stays 0x0a100000.
Copy the words 0x0f000856 and 0x0f000858 to 0x09075320 and 0x09075322.
Longword 0x0f000890: keep the bits in 0xd8000400 and set those in 0x27818000, the card bit among them.
94, entry 4 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. CR3's high byte without bit 7 but with bit 1 is rejected through entry 66 (stub 0xf892).

94 (CDC_MpSetMode), entry 4, replaced by the known cards: the mode from CR1's low byte (2 rejected, 4 the sector buffer mode, bits 0 and 1 still picture and high definition), decode timing and output from CR2 into 0x0f000868 for 0x0a100014, the scan mode from CR3's high byte (bit 1 rejected) into bit 7 of 0x0f000891. Leaving the buffer mode runs entry 33.
Bit 1 of 0x0f000897 gives the wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896).
r6 and r7 = the word 0x0f000868. CR1's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 2 sets bit 6 of 0x0f000892 and clears bit 7 of r7, and the byte's other bits are not used.
Bit 2 clear. With bit 6 of the word clear, bit 2 of 0x0f000897 gives the wait response, otherwise the word 0x0f00086a without bit 14 goes to 0x0a10001a.
Bits 0 and 1 at 2 are rejected through entry 66.
With bit 6 of 0x0f000892 set: clear it, write 0 to 0x0a10001a, set bit 7 of r7 and call entry 33 through the stub 0xf80e, GBR kept.
Bit 1 clear sets bit 3 of the word 0x0f000854, set clears it. The word goes to 0x0f000854 and 0x0a100000.
Bit 0 set: clear bit 6 of r7 and set bit 0 of the word. Clear: set bits 6 and 7 of r7, and bit 0 of the word becomes bit 5 of 0x0f000890 inverted. The word goes to 0x0f000854 and 0x0a100000 again.
CR2's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 0 clear sets bit 1 of r7, set clears it. CR2's high byte the same way for bit 0.
A changed r7 goes to 0x0f000868 and 0x0a100014.
CR3's high byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 0 clear sets bit 7 of 0x0f000891, set clears it.
With bit 0 of 0x0f000890 set and bits 0 and 6 of the word 0x0f000868 not both set, clear bits 0, 1 and 4 of 0x0f000890.
The response through r2, entry 68 (stub 0xf89a) here, then r11 = 0: nothing is posted.
95, entry 5. With bit 3 of 0x0f000892 set: the wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896), nothing stored. Otherwise r4 rebuilds the byte 0x0f000890, bit 4 cleared first.

95 (CDC_MpPlay), entry 5: rebuilds the byte 0x0f000890 from CR1's low byte and CR2's bytes, and with CR4's low byte bit 5 of it and the decode bit, bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854 for 0x0a100000. Waits with bit 3 of 0x0f000892.
CR2's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 0 clear sets bit 2, bit 0 set clears it.
CR2's high byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 0 clear sets bit 6, bit 0 set clears it.
CR1's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 0 set clears bits 0, 1 and 4. Bit 0 clear sets bits 0 and 1 when bits 0 and 6 of the word 0x0f000868 are both set, otherwise changes nothing.
Bit 0 set with bits 2, 3, 6 and 7 all set also sets bit 4.
CR4's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set. With bit 3 of the new byte or bit 1 of 0x0f000897 set, the byte is stored and the wait response follows.
Otherwise bit 0 set sets bit 5 of the byte and clears bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854, bit 0 clear clears bit 5 and sets bit 0. The word goes to 0x0f000854 and to the card register 0x0a100000.
Store the byte at 0x0f000890, then the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a).
The response, then r11 = 0: nothing is posted.
96, entry 6 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. Bit 3 of 0x0f000892 gives the wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896).

96 (CDC_MpSetDec), entry 6, replaced by the known cards: the audio mute from CR1's low byte into 0x0f000884 for 0x0a180008, the pause (CR2) and freeze (CR4) as bits 2 and 3 of 0x0f000868, bits 0..2 and 4..6 of 0x0f000893 and intervals at 0x0f00088c and 0x0f000888. A new freeze runs entry 37.
CR1's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: with bit 0 of 0x0f000897 set, the wait response. Otherwise its bits 0, 1 and 2 become bits 11, 10 and 8 of the word 0x0f000884, which goes to 0x0a180008.

CR2, unless it is ffff or the state 0x0f00089c is 6. Each value changes bit 2 of the word 0x0f000868, which goes to 0x0f000868 and 0x0a100014. Another value than 0 and 1: the words 0x0f00088c and 0x0f00088e take it, bits 0..2 of 0x0f000893 become 5 and bit 2 of the word is set.
0: with bit 1 of 0x0f000893 set, set its bit 2 and bit 2 of the word. Otherwise bits 0..2 become 2 and bit 2 of the word clears.
1: clear bits 0..2 of 0x0f000893 and set bit 2 of the word.
CR4, unless it is ffff, the same way with bits 4..6 of 0x0f000893, bit 3 of the word and the words 0x0f000888 and 0x0f00088a. Another value makes bits 4..6 5.
0: with bit 5 of 0x0f000893 set, set its bit 6 and bit 3 of the word. Otherwise bits 4..6 become 2, bit 3 of the word clears and entry 37 runs through the stub 0xf81e.
1: clear bits 4..6 of 0x0f000893 and set bit 3 of the word.
The response through r2, entry 68 (stub 0xf89a) here, then r11 = 0: nothing is posted.
97, entry 7 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. With bits 6 and 0 of the word 0x0f000868 set, only the status response.

97 (CDC_MpOutDsync), entry 7, replaced by the known cards: in still picture the frame bank from CR2 into 0x0f000868, in states 4 and 5 entries 38 and 39 and a decode pulse on 0x0a100000, then 2 added to 0x0f000842 and MPCM. With VSYNC timing in the movie mode only the status response.
Bit 6 clear: bits 0 and 1 of CR2 become bits 4 and 5 of the word, which goes to 0x0f000868 and 0x0a100014, and fffb to 0x0a100016.
With the state 0x0f00089c at 4 or 5 and bit 1 of 0x0f000893 clear: bit 0 of 0x0f000893 calls entry 38 through the stub 0xf822 and bit 4 entry 39 through 0xf826.

Then with bit 6 of the word set, fffd to 0x0a100016. Clear: bit 1 of 0x0f000897 gives the wait response, otherwise bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854 goes clear to 0x0a100000 and, five nops later, set again, and is kept.
Add 2 to the word 0x0f000842 and write 0x1000 (MPCM) to 0x0a00001e.
The response through r2, entry 68 (stub 0xf89a) here, then r11 = 0: nothing is posted.

A0, entry 16 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace and can jump to. With bit 6 of the word 0x0f000868 clear, bits 0 and 1 of CR2 become bits 4 and 5 of the word, which goes to 0x0f000868 and 0x0a100014, and fff7 to 0x0a100016.

A0 (CDC_MpDisp), entry 16, replaced by the known cards, whose A0 can jump here: in still picture the frame bank from CR2 into 0x0f000868, then bit 0 of CR2's high byte clears bit 1 of 0x0f000854 for 0x0a100000, and clear sets it.
Bit 1 of 0x0f000897 gives the wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896).
Bit 0 of CR2's high byte set clears bit 1 of the word 0x0f000854, clear sets it. The word goes to 0x0f000854 and 0x0a100000, then the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a), r11 = 0.

Entry 38, which the known cards keep, called by 0xa190. Count down the word 0x0f00088c. At 1 it is reloaded from 0x0f00088e, bit 2 of 0x0f000893 is set, and the word 0x0f000868 gets bit 2 and goes to 0x0a100014.
Entry 38: count down 0x0f00088c. At 1 reload it from 0x0f00088e, set bit 2 of 0x0f000893 and bit 2 of 0x0f000868 for 0x0a100014.
Entry 39, which the known cards keep. As entry 38 with the word 0x0f000888 reloaded from 0x0f00088a, bit 6 of 0x0f000893 and bit 3 of 0x0f000868.
Entry 39: count down 0x0f000888. At 1 reload it from 0x0f00088a, set bit 6 of 0x0f000893 and bit 3 of 0x0f000868 for 0x0a100014.
Entry 40, which the known cards keep, called by 0xa190 with r13 = 0x0f000890. Bit 2 of 0x0f000893 clears bit 2 of the word 0x0f000868. Bit 6 clears bit 3 and calls entry 37 through 0xf81e.
Entry 40: clear the 0x0f000868 bits entries 38 and 39 set, running entry 37 for bit 6, and clear bits 2 and 6 of 0x0f000893.
The word goes to 0x0f000868 and 0x0a100014, and bits 2 and 6 of 0x0f000893 are cleared.

Entry 35, task 8's offset 16, posted by 0xa190 as 088c0010. The known cards replace it. Bit 3 of 0x0f000892 stays set until the end, so 95 and 9C wait meanwhile. The bits of 0x0f000896 are taken in order, each cleared first.
Task 8 offset 16, entry 35: the bits of 0x0f000896 call entries 43..45, 47..49 with entry 36, and 73..75, 85, 46, 41 and 42 by state, count intervals in 0x0f000842, then wait through entry 32.
Bit 0: bit 5 of 0x0f000891 is set around entry 43, then the state 0x0f00089c at 4 calls entry 44, at 5 entry 45.
Bit 1: bit 4 of 0x0f000891 is set around entry 47, then the state at 4 calls entry 48, at 5 entry 49.
With bit 7 of 0x0f000890 and bit 6 of 0x09075370 set, entry 36 through 0xf81a returns a message in r11, or 0. A nonzero r11 is posted.
Bit 2: set bit 1 of 0x0f000891 and call entry 75. The state 0x0f00089c at 3 calls entry 74, other states go on at 0xac4c.
Past the literal at 0xac48: the state 0x0f00089c at 5 calls entry 46, at 6 entry 41.
The state 0x0f00089d at 3, 5 or 6 calls entry 73, 85 or 42.
With bits 0 and 6 of the word 0x0f000868 set, add 1 to the word 0x0f000842, the counter the MPEG status reports.

With both states at 4 (the word 0x0f00089c 0x0404), bits 0 and 1 of 0x0f000890 set and bit 0 or 1 of 0x0f000893 set, set bit 7 of 0x0f000890. Otherwise clear it, and with bit 6 of 0x09075370 set clear that bit and post 088a000c.
Clear bit 1 of 0x0f000891.
Clear bit 3 of 0x0f000892 and jump to entry 32 through 0xf80a, task 8's wait.

Entry 41, called by entry 35 for the state 0x0f00089c at 6. The known cards replace it. Write the word 0x0f000868 with bits 2 and 3 clear to 0x0a100014, the kept word unchanged. The threshold r1 is 1, or the word 0x090752e0 with bit 2 of 0x0f000890 set.
Entry 41, the video part in state 6: once the video partition holds enough sectors, post 08890008, restore the state from 0x0f000898 and start decoding.
r10 = the sector count of partition n (0x0f000602 + 6n), n the byte 0x0907532b. A count of 0 returns. Otherwise clear bit 4 of 0x0f000846, and a count below the threshold returns.

Post 08890008, task 8's offset 8, entry 51. The byte 0x0f000898 becomes the state 0x0f00089c and bit 2 of 0x0907535c is set. With bit 1 of 0x0f000897 set around it, set bit 5 of 0x0f000890 and clear bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854, which goes to 0x0a100000 too.
Write the word 0x0f000868 to 0x0a100014 again and return. The returns before leave the register without bits 2 and 3.

Entry 42, called by entry 35 for the state 0x0f00089d at 6. The known cards replace it, and their own entry 42 calls it through the ROM table. r10 = the sector count of partition n, n the byte 0x0907532f. A count of 0 returns. Otherwise clear bit 4 of 0x0f000845, and below 4 return.
Entry 42, the audio part in state 6: once the audio partition holds 4 sectors, post 088a000c and restore the state from 0x0f000899.
Post 088a000c, task 8's offset 12, entry 72. The byte 0x0f000899 becomes the state 0x0f00089d and bit 7 of 0x0f000895 is set.

Entry 37, called by entry 40. The known cards replace it. Store the low byte of the card register 0x0a100006 at 0x09075312 and look for its low 6 bits among the low 6 bits of the bytes 0x090752e7 + 4k, k = 0..3.
Entry 37: match the low 6 bits of 0x0a100006 against four records at 0x090752e4 and copy the match to 0x09075304.
A match copies the longword 0x090752f4 + 4k to 0x09075304 and the matched 6 bits to the word 0x0907530c. Without one 0x09075304 is kept and the word becomes ffff.

Entry 36, called by entry 35. The known cards replace it. r11 = 088a000c when the byte 0x090752ad (sign-extended) over the word 0x090752a8 is above the byte 0x090752ae over the word 0x090752a4, unsigned, otherwise 0. 0x090752a4 is the longword 99 answers.
Entry 36: r11 = 088a000c when 0x090752a8 with 0x090752ad is above 0x090752a4 with 0x090752ae.
Entry 66: status ff, the reject response, with the MPEG status from 0xaeb0.
Entry 66: status ff with the MPEG status.
Entry 67: the wait response (entry 90) keeping only its status byte, with the MPEG status.
Entry 67: the wait response's status byte with the MPEG status.
Entry 68: the status response (entry 89) with r12 = 0, with the MPEG status.
Entry 68: the status response with the MPEG status from 0x0f00089c, 0x0f000891, 0x0f000842 and 0x0f000844.
MPEG status: bits of the word at 0x0f00089c and bit 0 of 0x0f000891 (as bit 3) are swapped into the high half of r12, word 0x0f000842 is ORed into its low half, and r13 = longword 0x0f000844.
90, entry 0 of the ROM table: the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a). Nothing is posted.
90, entry 0: the status response through entry 68.
91, entry 1: the status byte through entry 89 (stub 0xf8ee) with the low 24 bits of the longword 0x0f000848 in r12, and r13 = 0. The longword is cleared.
91, entry 1: the status byte with the longword 0x0f000848, which is cleared, in r12's low 24 bits.
Clear bit 5 of 0x0f000845 and bit 7 of 0x0f000847. Nothing is posted.
92, entry 2: the low 24 bits of r1 (CR1's low byte and CR2) to the longword 0x0f00084c, then the status response through entry 68. Nothing is posted.
92, entry 2: CR1's low byte and CR2 to 0x0f00084c, then the status response through entry 68.

9A, entry 10 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace and call. r8 and r9 collect the current parts set and cut, r3 = bit 0 of CR3's high byte, the next connection. CR2's low byte (the audio partition) and CR4's low byte (video) above 23 and not ff are rejected through entry 66, unless bit 7 of CR1's or CR3's low byte leaves the part alone.

9A (CDC_MpSetCon), entry 10, replaced and called by the known cards: the audio (CR1, CR2) and video (CR3, CR4) connections, current or next by bit 0 of CR3's high byte, into 0x0907532c, 0x09075328, 0x09075334 and 0x09075330 with states to 2 and request bits in 0x09075388, or cuts. Posts 09810001 to task 9's card work loop.
Bit 3 of 0x0f000892 gives the wait response through entry 67.

Audio, unless bit 7 of CR1's low byte is set. A partition for the current connection needs the state 0x0f00089d at 1, for the next bit 5 of 0x0f000894 clear. ff, a cut, needs the state at 1, 2 or 3, for the next not at 5. Otherwise the wait response.
Video, unless bit 7 of CR3's low byte is set, the same way with the state 0x0f00089c and bit 1 of 0x0f000894. Bit 6 of 0x0f000892 also gives the wait response.
The reject response through entry 66 (stub 0xf892), r11 = 0.
The wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896), r11 = 0.

Audio, unless bit 7 of CR1's low byte is set. A current partition: CR1:CR2 to 0x0907532c, 0 to the word 0x09075326, set bit 7 of 0x09075371, clear bit 4 of 0x0f000845 and bits 4..7 of 0x09075370, the state 0x0f00089d = 2 and bit 2 of 0x09075388 set.
A next partition: CR1:CR2 to 0x09075334, 0 to the word 0x0907534a, and bit 5 of 0x0f000894 and bit 3 of 0x09075388 set.
A current cut in state 2 or 3 sets bit 2 of 0x0907534d and bit 0 of r9. A next cut with bit 5 of 0x0f000894 set: with bit 7 of 0x0907534c clear, set bit 3 of 0x0907534d, otherwise clear both bits.

Video, unless bit 7 of CR3's low byte is set. A current partition: CR3:CR4 to 0x09075328, 0 to the word 0x09075324, set bit 3 of 0x0f000890, clear bit 4 of 0x0f000846, the state 0x0f00089c = 2 and bit 0 of 0x09075388 set.
A next partition: CR3:CR4 to 0x09075330, 0 to the word 0x09075348, and bit 1 of 0x0f000894 and bit 1 of 0x09075388 set.
A current cut in state 2 or 3 sets bit 0 of 0x0907534d and bit 1 of r9. A next cut with bit 1 of 0x0f000894 set: with bit 5 of 0x0907534c clear, set bit 1 of 0x0907534d, otherwise clear both bits.

Without a current cut, with both current partitions set and bit 0 clear in CR2's and CR4's high bytes, go on at 0xb214. Otherwise clear bit 6 of 0x0907532a, in the video connection's high byte of CR4.
With bit 6 of 0x0907532a set: clear bit 2 of 0x09075388, and after a current video cut with the audio state at 2, set bit 2 of 0x0907534d.
Bits 0 and 2 of 0x0f000890 with both current partitions set bit 4 of 0x0f000890.
The status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a). r11 = 09810001 goes to task 9, whose card work loop takes the bits of 0x09075388.

9D, entry 13 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. With bit 0 of CR1's low byte set, a stream number (CR2's high byte) above 31 is rejected through entry 66, and with bit 0 of CR3's low byte a video stream number (CR4's high byte) above 15.

9D (CDC_MpSetStm), entry 13, replaced by the known cards: stream modes, numbers and channels for audio (CR1, CR2) and video (CR3, CR4) into the records 9E returns, current or next by bit 0 of CR3's high byte.

Bit 0 of CR3's high byte clear, the current streams: bit 1 or 2 of 0x0f000892 gives the wait response through entry 67. Bit 0 or 4 of CR1's low byte sets bit 1 of 0x09075371, of CR3's low byte bit 3 of 0x0907535c. The records 0x0907533c and 0x09075338, or 0x09075344 and 0x09075340 for the next streams.

CR1's low byte to byte 1 of the first record, CR2's high byte to byte 2 when its bit 0 is set and CR2's low byte to byte 3 when its bit 4 is set. CR3's low byte and CR4 go to the second record the same way. Then the status response through entry 68, r11 = 0.
The reject response through entry 66 (stub 0xf892), r11 = 0.
9B, entry 11. CR3's high byte to 0x0907532c, then the status byte through service 89 (stub 0xf8ee). r12 keeps only the status byte, r13 starts as the high byte of 0x0907532c.

9B (CDC_MpGetCon), entry 11: two connection records, current (0x0907532c, 0x09075328) or next (0x09075334, 0x09075330) by CR3's high byte, under masks. A current record's last byte becomes ff when its state 0x0f00089c or 0x0f00089d is 1, a next record's when its bit in 0x0f000894 is clear.
Bit 0 of that byte clear: the records 0x0907532c for r12 and 0x09075328 for r13. The last byte of the first becomes ff when 0x0f00089d is 1, of the second when 0x0f00089c is 1.
Bit 0 set: the records 0x09075334 and 0x09075330. The last byte of the first becomes ff when bit 5 of 0x0f000894 is clear, of the second when bit 1 is clear.
r12 takes the first record's low 24 bits and r13 the second's, then r12 is masked with 0xff0701ff and r13 with 0x0137c1ff. Nothing is posted.
9E, entry 14. CR3's high byte to 0x0907533c, then the status byte through service 89. r12 keeps only the status byte, r13 starts as the high byte of 0x0907533c.
9E (CDC_MpGetStm), entry 14: two stream records, current (0x0907533c, 0x09075338) or next (0x09075344, 0x09075340) by CR3's high byte, under masks.
Bit 0 of that byte clear: the records 0x0907533c for r12 and 0x09075338 for r13. Set: 0x09075344 and 0x09075340.
r12 takes the first record's low 24 bits and r13 the second's, then r12 is masked with 0xff22ffff and r13 with 0x0122ffff. Nothing is posted.
DMA channel 3 end (vector 78, ROM longword 0x0138), the channel the card's audio data request drives. Save the full frame as 0x9ce4 does and switch to 0x0f0008f8.
DMA channel 3 end (vector 78), the card's audio data channel: clear IE, set bit 2 of 0x0f000892 and post 088a000c to task 8's entry 72.
Set bit 2 of 0x0f000892, clear IE in CHCR3 (bit 2 of 0x05ffff7f) and post 088a000c, task 8's offset 12, entry 72. Continue through the scheduler at 0x102e.
9C, entry 12. r10 collects the parts that change. Any of bits 1..3 of 0x0f000892, or bit 0 of 0x0907537b, gives the wait response through 0xb834.
9C (CDC_MpChgCon), entry 12: accepted parts of CR2 move 0x0f00089c or 0x0f00089d from 4 to 5, then entry 88, the status response and 08810014 to task 8.
Keep CR2 at 0x09075374 and CR3 at 0x09075376.
CR2's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: with bit 0 set, bit 1 of 0x0f000894 must be set. Then 0x0f00089c must be 4, and bit 0 of r10 is set. Otherwise the wait response.
CR2's high byte the same way, with bit 5 of 0x0f000894 and 0x0f00089d, for bit 1 of r10.

Each part in r10 moves its byte, 0x0f00089c or 0x0f00089d, from 4 to 5. Then entry 88 (stub 0xf8ea) and the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a). r11 = 08810014 goes to task 8, whose offset 20 jumps to entry 64.

Entry 88 of the ROM table, called in the ROM only by 9C. CR2's low byte at 0x09075375 with bits 7 and 0 clear: entry 58 (stub 0xf872), bit 0 of 0x0f000894 cleared, 0x0f00089c = 1, entry 60 (stub 0xf87a).
Entry 88, from 9C: parts with bit 0 clear call entry 58 or 59 (stopping DMA channel 2 or 3), clear their bit of 0x0f000894, return to state 1 and call entry 60. Then 0x0907537b = 1.
CR2's high byte at 0x09075374 with bits 7 and 0 clear: entry 59 (stub 0xf876), bit 4 of 0x0f000894 cleared, 0x0f00089d = 1, entry 60.
0x0907537b = 1, which makes a later 9C wait until something clears it.
A2, entry 18: CR2 to the card register 0x0a100012 and to 0x0f000866, then the status response through 0xb826.
A2 (CDC_MpSetBcolor), entry 18: CR2 to 0x0a100012 and 0x0f000866.
A3, entry 19. With bit 1 of 0x0f000897 set: the wait response through 0xb834.
A3 (CDC_MpSetFade), entry 19: two gains of -8..7 from CR2 into the high byte of 0x0f000854 and 0x0a100000, others rejected.
CR2's low and high bytes, signed, must each lie in -8..7. Otherwise the reject response through 0xb842.
The high byte of the word 0x0f000854 becomes (low byte + 8) << 4 | (high byte + 8). The word goes to 0x0f000854 and to the card register 0x0a100000, then the status response.
A4, entry 20. With bit 1 of 0x0f000897 set: the wait response through 0xb834. Otherwise the word 0x0f00086c is rebuilt, its high byte in r3 and its low byte in r4.
A4 (CDC_MpSetVeff), entry 20: the word 0x0f00086c for 0x0a10001c from CR2's low byte, CR3 and CR4, and bits 4..7 of 0x0f000854 for 0x0a100000 from CR2's high byte.
CR4's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bit 0 clear sets bit 5, bit 0 set clears it. CR4's high byte the same way for bit 4.
CR3's low byte, unless it is ff: bits 12..15 become 15 for 0, the value - 1 for 1..9 and 9 for 10 and above. CR3's high byte the same way for bits 8..11.
CR2's low byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bits 0..2 become its bits 0..2 inverted.
The word goes to 0x0f00086c and to the card register 0x0a10001c.
CR2's high byte, unless its bit 7 is set: bits 4..7 of the word 0x0f000854 become its bits 0..3 inverted, and the word goes to 0x0a100000. Then the status response.
A5, entry 21 of the ROM table, which the known cards replace. Bit 1 of the word 0x0f000868 set gives the reject response through 0xb842.

A5 (CDC_MpGetImg), entry 21, replaced by the known cards: rejected with output to VDP2, waits while bit 8 of 0x0a100000 is set, otherwise 0x00fe to 0x0a100016 and the display size's product in r12's low 24 bits. r13 stays 0x0a000000.
Read the card register 0x0a100000 into the word 0x0f000852. Its bit 8 set gives the wait response through 0xb834.

Write 0x00fe to 0x0a100016, then the status byte through service 89 (stub 0xf8ee). r12's low 24 bits = the word 0x0f00085a times the word 0x0f00085c, that one halved first while bit 3 of the word 0x0f000854 is set. r13 stays as the IRQ6 entry passed it, 0x0a000000. Nothing is posted.
Shared ends of 9C, A2, A3, A4 and A5: the status response through entry 68 (stub 0xf89a), r11 = 0.
Shared ends of 9C, A2..A4 and A5: entry 68 (0xb826), 67 (0xb834) or 66 (0xb842), each with r11 = 0.
The wait response through entry 67 (stub 0xf896), r11 = 0.
The reject response through entry 66 (stub 0xf892), r11 = 0.

ITU2 input capture A (vector 88, ROM longword 0x0160): a falling edge of TIOCA2, the card's other interrupt line. Save the full frame, switch to 0x0f0008f8, call entry 56 through 0xf86a and continue through the scheduler at 0x102e. Nothing is posted.
ITU2 input capture A (vector 88), a falling edge of TIOCA2: entry 56. Nothing is posted.
Entry 56 of the ROM table, which the known cards keep. Clear IMFA in TSR2. With DE of CHCR3 set, clear it, call entry 57 through 0xf86e and set it again. Otherwise just call entry 57.
Entry 56: clear IMFA, entry 57 with channel 3 paused, then the audio error bit 5 of 0x0f000845 and bit 20 of the MPEG interrupt flags, with MPST when masked in.
Set bit 5 of 0x0f000845 and bit 20 of the MPEG interrupt flags (bit 4 of 0x0f000849). With that bit in the mask (bit 4 of 0x0f00084d), write 0x2000 (MPST) to 0x0a00001e.

Entry 57, which the known cards keep. Read 0x0a180008 and discard the word, write the word 0x0f000884 with bit 14 set to it, wait 8 loop passes and write the word with bit 14 clear. 0x0f000884 does not change.
Entry 57: bit 14 of 0x0a180008 set and cleared again over the kept word 0x0f000884.

Entry 58, called by entry 88 for 9C's low byte, the video part. The known cards replace it. Clear DE and TE and set IE in CHCR2, clear the byte 0x0907535c, the longword 0x09075314, bit 1 of 0x0f000892, the byte 0x09075351 and bits 3 and 4 of 0x0f000890, then write 3 to 0x0a00000c.
Entry 58, from entry 88: stop DMA channel 2 with IE set and clear the video part's bytes, then 3 to 0x0a00000c.
Entry 59, called by entry 88 for 9C's high byte, the audio part, which the known cards keep. Clear DE and TE and set IE in CHCR3, clear bit 2 of 0x0f000892 and the byte 0x09075371.
Entry 59, from entry 88: stop DMA channel 3 with IE set and clear the audio part's bytes.

Entry 61, which the known cards keep and no ROM code calls. With bit 1 of 0x0f000897 set around it, clear bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854, write the word to 0x0a100000, wait 8 loop passes, then set the bit and write the word again.
Entry 61, no ROM caller: bit 0 of 0x0a100000 low for 8 loop passes and back.
Entry 60, called by entry 88 after entry 58 and after entry 59. The known cards replace it. Toggle bit 1 of 0x0f000890.
Entry 60, from entry 88: toggle bit 1 of 0x0f000890.
Clear the disc result word, card status 0x0f0007ac..0x0f0007af, busy flag 0x0f0007b0 and check bits 0x0f0007b1.
Task 9 starts by waiting for a message. Expansion processing follows at 0xba48. Reaching this wait does not load or execute an expansion.
Task 9 waits for a message before expansion processing at 0xba48.
Task 9 message dispatch after the wait at 0xba46: payload low byte 0 goes to 0xbbc6. Otherwise 0x0f000892 bit7 selects 0xba5e when set and the request path at 0xbae8 when clear.
Task 9 continuation. Payload 0 goes to 0xbbc6, 0x0f000892 bit7 set goes to 0xba5e and other requests continue at 0xbae8.
The card work loop, with the card bit set. Bits 0, 1, 2 and 3 of 0x09075388 call entries 54, 53, 69 and 70 through their stubs, in that order. The byte is read again after each call.

Task 9 with the card bit set and a nonzero payload: bits 0..3 of 0x09075388 call entries 54, 53, 69 and 70, bits 0..3 of 0x09075389 jump to entries 78, 77, 80 and 79, which return through entry 76 (0xbad6). Repeats until no bit is set, then waits at 0xba46.
Byte 0x09075389: the lowest of bits 0, 1, 2 and 3 that is set jumps to entry 78, 77, 80 or 79 without a return address. Entry 76 in the ROM table is 0xbad6, the recheck below.
Recheck: any of bits 0..3 set in either byte runs the loop again. Otherwise task 9 waits at 0xba46.

Payload 1 returns to the wait. Payloads 2 and above clear 0x0f0007b1 and call the five checks listed at 0xbc28 with r0 = 1. A nonzero result sets bit n of 0x0f0007b1. 0xbb1e then acts on 0x0f0007b1 and request byte 0x0907538a.

Payload 1 returns to the wait. Payloads 2 and above run the five checks listed at 0xbc28 with r0 = 1. Entries 0 and 2 return zero, entries 1, 3 and 4 are the card checks at 0xbcc4, 0xbe7c and 0xbf04. Results collect in 0x0f0007b1 before 0xbb1e acts on them and on request byte 0x0907538a.

After the five checks: any bit set in 0x0f0007b1 goes to 0xbb6e. Otherwise request byte 0x0907538a selects the action, bit 0 first. With neither bit set task 9 waits again at 0xba46 and leaves the request byte and the busy flag 0x0f0007b0 set.

After the card checks. A failed check clears the expansion for E0 through 0x1b5e (card status 0001) or sets status byte 1 for E2. Otherwise E0 runs the expansion loader 0x1b06 (status byte 0x0f0007ad = 2, whatever the result) and E2 expansion entry 86 through 0xf8e2 (status byte 0x0f0007ac = 3 for r13 = 0, else 2). Then the request byte and busy clear and 0x0800 (MPED) goes to 0x0a00001e.
Request 1 (E0 subcode 1): the expansion loader 0x1b06. Card status byte 0x0f0007ad becomes 2 whatever the loader returns. Byte 0x0f0007ac is kept, and a failed load has already cleared the word.
Request 2 (E2): expansion entry 86 through the stub 0xf8e2, which returns its result in r13. Card status byte 0x0f0007ac becomes 3 for r13 = 0 and 2 otherwise. Byte 0x0f0007ad is kept.

A check failed. Request bit 0, or no bit, clears the expansion area, the MPEG version 0x0f0002fd and word 0x0f0007ac through 0x1b5e, then stores word 0x0001. Bit 1 alone sets byte 0x0f0007ac to 1 and keeps byte 0x0f0007ad.
Both failure paths clear card status word 0x0f0007ae.
Store word 0x0f0007ac: byte 0x0f0007ac from r2, byte 0x0f0007ad from the low byte of r1.
Clear the request byte and the busy flag, write 0x0800 (MPED) to 0x0a00001e and wait again at 0xba46.
Task 9 payload 0, posted by 93 when it stops or resets the card. Write 3 to 0x0a00000c and 0 to 0x0a10001a. With the card bit set, post 08090004, which task 8 takes at 0xa41c, and wait again.
Task 9 payload 0 from 93: 3 to 0x0a00000c, 0 to 0x0a10001a. With the card bit set it posts 08090004 to task 8, otherwise clears the MPEG state and writes MPED.
With the card bit clear, clear the MPEG state (0xa4d0), write 0x0800 (MPED) to 0x0a00001e and wait again.
Check entries 0 and 2 return 0 without accessing hardware.
Returns -1. Not in the check table at 0xbc28 and not referenced elsewhere in the ROM.
Returns -1. No reference in the ROM.

Not referenced in the ROM. Card identity: write ffff to 0x0a10001a, read 0x0a10000a and 0x0a100008 once and discard them, then read them again as a longword with 0x0a100008 in the high half. It must read ffffffff.
No reference in the ROM. Expects ffffffff from 0x0a100008 and 0x0a10000a with ffff at 0x0a10001a, and SEGA with fffe.
The second pass writes fffe to 0x0a10001a and expects 0x53454741, SEGA.
Write ffff to 0x0a10001a. Returns 0 when both passes matched, -1 otherwise.

Check 1, the video data request. CHCR2 = 0x1908: DMA channel 2 moves words from an incrementing source to a fixed destination on each ITU1 capture A (IMIA1). TIOR1 = 0x0d makes GRA1 capture falling edges of TIOCA1, the card's video data request, and TIER1 = 1 enables IMIA1. Then 0x0fff to 0x0a10001a.

Check 1: an MPEG-1 video sequence header of 18 words from 0x0907539c to 0x0a10001e on DMA channel 2, one word per falling edge of TIOCA1, the card's video data request (ITU1 capture A). Passes when TE is set after 0x500 loop passes.
Fill 16 words at 0x0907539c from the generator 0xbf94.

Make the block an MPEG-1 video sequence header: start codes 0x000001b3 at +0, 0x000001b5 (extension) at +12 and +28, 0x000001b2 (user data) at +16 and 0x000001b8 (group of pictures) at +20. The random size, aspect ratio and picture rate at +4 stay. At +8 bit 13, the marker bit after the bit rate, is set and bits 1..0, the quantizer matrix flags, cleared.
TE of CHCR2 (bit 1) already set fails the check.
SAR2 = 0x0907539c, DAR2 = 0x0a10001e, TCR2 = 18 words. Clear IE and TE and set DE: the channel waits for 18 captures.
Wait 0x500 loop passes and read CHCR2, then clear IMIEA and IMIEB in TIER1, IMFA and IMFB in TSR1, and DE and TE in CHCR2.
Returns 0 when TE was set, all 18 words moved, and -1 otherwise.

Not referenced in the ROM. Reads back what the card made of check 1's header at 0x0907539c. From the header longwords at +4 and +8 it writes four words at +0: aspect ratio and width, picture rate and height, then two from the longword at +8.
No reference in the ROM. Compares what 0x0a100022 returns for registers 3..0 with fields of check 1's header.
A word from the generator 0xbf94. With r0 = 0 the four words are compared as they are and ffff goes to 0x0a10001a.
Otherwise eight words of a 15-bit shift register seeded with the random word go to +8..+22, the random word to 0x0a100024 and fffe to 0x0a10001a.

For r9 = 3, 2, 1, 0: write r9 to 0x0a100022 and read a word back from it. It must equal word r9 at 0x0907539c, XORed with the next shift register word when r0 was set. For r9 = 3 only the bits in 0xc3ff are compared.
Write ffff to 0x0a10001a. Returns 0 when all four matched, -1 otherwise.
Check 3, the audio data request. Read 0x0a180008 and 0x0a180000, then write 0x8209 to 0x0a180008 and 0 to 0x0a180000.
Check 3: 0x8209 to 0x0a180008, then four zero words to 0x0a180000 on DMA channel 3, one per falling edge of TIOCA0, the card's audio data request (ITU0 capture A). Passes when TE is set.

CHCR3 = 0x1808: DMA channel 3 moves words from an incrementing source to a fixed destination on each ITU0 capture A (IMIA0). TIOR0 = 0x0d makes GRA0 capture falling edges of TIOCA0, the card's audio data request, and TIER0 = 1 enables IMIA0.
Clear 18 words at 0x0907539c.
TE of CHCR3 already set fails the check.
SAR3 = 0x0907539c, DAR3 = 0x0a180000, TCR3 = 4 words. Clear IE and TE and set DE.
Wait 0x500 loop passes and read CHCR3, then clear TIER0, TSR0 and DE and TE in CHCR3. Returns 0 when TE was set, all 4 words moved, and -1 otherwise.
Check 4, a test of the card memory behind 0x0a100030..0x0a100037. The card must report ready (0xbfca).

Check 4: fills the card memory behind 0x0a100030..0x0a100037, 512 blocks of 1024 bytes, with seed + block + byte offset, reads four words back from each quarter, then clears it without checking the clear.
A seed from 0xbf94. 0xc014 fills the memory with the pattern for it.
Four reads through 0xc082, one in each quarter of the memory: address r7 << 14 | (random & 0x3fff) in 8-byte units, for r7 = 0..3.
Ready again, then clear the memory through 0xc0f4, whose result is not checked. 0x0fff to 0x0a10001a and return 0.
Any failure returns -1, without the clear.
Random word: state 0x090753e8 becomes (low word of the state times 0x93a5, both signed) >> 8, plus TCNT4 (0x05ffff36) read as a signed word, plus 89. Returns the new state in r0. Uses r12 and r13.
Random word from the state at 0x090753e8 and TCNT4.
Not referenced in the ROM. Clears bit 7 of the word at 0x0f000868, then polls as 0xbfca does with that word in place of 0xff7f.
No reference in the ROM. The ready poll with bit 7 of the word at 0x0f000868 cleared.
Card ready, with r11 = 0xff7f.
Card ready: up to 33 polls of bit 0 of 0x0a100034, each after writing r11 to 0x0a100014.
Up to 33 times: write r11 to 0x0a100014 and read 0x0a100034. Bit 0 set returns 0. Otherwise write ffff to 0x0a100034, read 0x0a100036, write 0 to it and try again. Returns -1 after the last try.
Not referenced in the ROM. Sets bit 7 of the word at 0x0f000868 and writes the result, sign-extended, as a longword to 0x0a100014.
No reference in the ROM. Sets bit 7 of the word at 0x0f000868 and writes it to 0x0a100014.

Fill the card memory with the pattern for seed r0. For each of 512 blocks b: wait for ready as 0xbfca does, then write b << 7 to the address register 0x0a100030 (8-byte units, 1024 bytes a block), 0xfe00 to 0x0a100032 and 0xfffc to 0x0a100034.
Fill the card memory with seed + block + byte offset: per block the address (8-byte units) to 0x0a100030, 0xfe00 to 0x0a100032, 0xfffc to 0x0a100034, then 512 words to 0x0a100036.
512 words a block: wait while bit 2 of 0x0a100034 is set, at most 81 reads, then write seed + b + o to 0x0a100036, o the byte offset 0, 2 .. 0x3fe.
Returns 0, or -1 at 0xc07e when a wait runs out.
Compare four words at address r8 (8-byte units) with the fill pattern for seed r0: seed + (r8 >> 7) + (r8 & 0x7f) * 8, then that plus 2, 4 and 6.
Read four words at address r8 with 0xfa04 and compare them with the fill pattern for seed r0.
After ready: r8 to 0x0a100030, 0xfa04 to 0x0a100032, 0xfffc to 0x0a100034, then four reads of 0x0a100036, each once bit 2 of 0x0a100034 is clear.
Returns 0 when all four matched, -1 on a mismatch or when a wait runs out.
As 0xc014, with every word set to r0 instead of the pattern.
Fill the card memory with r0.
Get MPEG ROM, entry 86 of the ROM table. Clear the page count 0x0f0007ae and copy the filter byte 0x09075398 to 0x09075399. r10 = the page 0x0907538c, r9 = the end 0x09075390, both set by E2.

Get MPEG ROM, ROM table entry 86, run by E2 through the stub 0xf8e2. Clears the page count 0x0f0007ae, then for each page from 0x0907538c to 0x09075390 takes a free slot, copies 2048 bytes from 0x0e005000 + 2048 * page between 24 and 280 cleared bytes and files the slot from CD device 3 through the filter. r13 = 0 after the last page, -1 without a free slot.
While page < end (unsigned): take a free slot through 0xc1f0. ff (-1) means none left.
Keep the slot at 0x0907539a. 0xc20a gives the slot address in r1 and page << 11 in r2, so the source is 0x0e005000 + 2048 * page. It is not wrapped: pages from 246 on read from 0x0e080000 and up.
Clear the 24 bytes before the data (r5 = 0), copy 2048 bytes, clear the 280 bytes after them (r5 = 1), then file the slot through the filter (0xc256).
The next page. Add 1 to the page count 0x0f0007ae and read the end again.
Every page filed: r13 = 0.
No free slot: r13 = -1. The pages filed so far stay where the filter sent them, and 0x0f0007ae counts them.

Entry 81 of the ROM table: under the sector lock as task 9 (0x0b090000), take the free pool head through 0x4e98. The slot goes to 0x0907539a as a word and to r0 sign-extended, ff (-1) when the pool is empty.
ROM table entry 81: the free pool head under the sector lock as task 9, kept at 0x0907539a, ff when the pool is empty.
Entry 84: r1 = 0x09000230 + 0x930 * r1, the slot address, and r2 = r2 << 11, the page offset.
ROM table entry 84: the slot address for slot r1 and the page offset r2 << 11.
Entry 82: clear from r1, 24 bytes when bit 0 of r5 is clear, 280 bytes when set, and advance r1 past them.
ROM table entry 82: clear 24 or 280 bytes from r1 by bit 0 of r5.
Entry 83: copy 2048 bytes from r2 to r1 a longword at a time and advance both.
ROM table entry 83: copy 2048 bytes from r2 to r1.

Entry 87: under the sector lock as task 9, pair CD device 3 (0x83) with the filter at 0x09075399 through 0x5510, then deliver the slot at 0x0907539a from 0x83 through 0x4fa4. The page goes where the filter's chain sends it.
ROM table entry 87: pair CD device 3 with the filter at 0x09075399, then deliver the slot at 0x0907539a from device 3, under the sector lock as task 9.

E0: reject while busy flag 0x0f0007b0 bit0 or 0x0f000892 bit7 is set. The IRQ6 entry already rejects busy states. CR2 low byte (r1 bits 7..0) selects subcode 0 (disc) or 1 (MPEG). Other values are invalid.

E0 Authenticate Device. CR2 low byte 0 posts 07810008 to task 7 (disc) and 1 posts 09810002 to task 9 (MPEG). An accepted request keeps its message at 0x09075384 and sets busy flag 0x0f0007b0 until the task clears it.

Subcode 0: store r1/r2 (CR1..CR4) at 0x0907adb0/0x0907adb4. CR3 high byte (r2 bits 31..24) must be at most 23. Set disc state 0x0907adcb to 2 and store message 07810008 (task7, class 81, payload 8) at 0x09075384.
Subcode 1: requires bit1 of hardware flag 0x0f00027d. Set request byte 0x0907538a to 1 and store message 09810002 (task9, class 81, payload 2) at 0x09075384.
Accept: build the cached response through 0x91fe (status mask 0, no pending mark), reload r11 from 0x09075384 and set busy flag 0x0f0007b0 to 1. The IRQ6 entry then posts r11.
Reject: reject response through 0x91e8, r11 cleared in the delay slot so nothing is posted.
E2: reject while busy, while bit1 of 0x0f00027d is clear, while byte 0x0f0002fd is zero or while 0x0f000892 bit7 is set. The expansion loader copies decoded byte +0 to 0x0f0002fd on success.
E2 Get MPEG ROM. Requires nonzero 0x0f0002fd (a loaded expansion), filter at most 23, offset at most 0x7ff and offset plus count at most 0x800. Posts 09810004 to task 9.
Filter r2 bits 31..24 at most 23, offset r1 bits 23..0 at most 0x7ff, offset plus count r2 bits 15..0 at most 0x800 (unsigned).

Store offset at 0x0907538c, offset plus count at 0x09075390 and filter byte at 0x09075398. Set 0x0907538a to 2, store message 09810004 (task9, class 81, payload 4) at 0x09075384 and join the accept path.
E1: reject while busy. CR2 low byte selects subcode 0 (disc) or 1 (MPEG). Other values are invalid. Produces no message and leaves the busy flag unchanged.
E1 Get Authentication Result. Subcode 0 returns word 0x0f000786 in CR2, whose low byte 0x0f000787 is the disc result. Subcode 1 returns words 0x0f0007ac and 0x0f0007ae in CR2 and CR4. No message.
Subcode 0: r3 = word 0x0f000786 << 16. Byte 0x0f000787 is the disc authentication result.
Subcode 1: reject while 0x0f000892 bit7 is set. Otherwise r3 = word 0x0f0007ac << 16 | word 0x0f0007ae.
0x91a8 supplies the status byte in r12 bits 31..24. Response CR1 = status << 8, CR2 = r3 bits 31..16, CR3 = 0, CR4 = r3 bits 15..0.
A6, entry 22. CR1's low byte selects the position (0) or the size (1), CR2's low byte a bank 0..3. A larger value goes to the reject at 0xc48c.
A6 (CDC_MpSetImgPos, CDC_MpSetImgSiz), entry 22: position or size for bank 0..3, rounded down to even, at 0x0907539c + 8 * bank + 4 * selection.
CR3 and CR4, each rounded down to even, go as two words to 0x0907539c + 8 * bank + 4 * selection.
Clear the longword 0x09075384.
