The movie mode. While frozen (bit 3 of the word clear) with CR2's bit 0 clear, as the ROM: r12 = the word 0x0907530c and r13 = the longword 0x09075304, which entry 37 keeps. The bank r2 is bits 6 and 7 of the card register 0x0a100006, where the ROM takes those of the byte 0x09075312 that entry 37 kept.

Frozen with CR2's bit 0 set: r2 = the bank the register shows, and the register's low 6 bits are looked for among the low 6 bits of the records 0x090752e4 + 4k of the other three banks. The ROM takes the path below instead.
One match answers that bank with its records 0x090752e4 + 4k and 0x090752f4 + 4k. None or several answer the register's 6 bits as the picture, the record 0x090752f4 and bank 0x80.

Otherwise, as the ROM: r2 = bits 6 and 7 of 0x0a100006, and r12 and r13 = the records 0x090752e4 and 0x090752f4 of that bank. When the record's low 6 bits differ from the register's, r12 takes the register's and r2 gets bit 7. The ROM has no such check.

r12 = r2 << 16 | bits 13 and 14 << 8 | the low byte of r12, where the ROM takes bits 0..5. r13 takes bits 0..5, 6..11, 13..18 and 19..26 of r13 into its bytes from the low one up, the pictures, seconds, minutes and hours of an MPEG time code.
The status byte from r11 over r12, then r11 = 0: nothing is posted.

A1, Set Window, entry 17, over the ROM's 0x9ed8. CR1's low byte selects the window setting 0 to 4, CR3 and CR4 are its x and y, and bit 0 of CR2's low byte writes the window words to the card. GBR = 0x0f000854.

Setting 0, the frame buffer window position: CR4 and CR3, each unless its bit 15 is set, halved to 0x0f000860 and 0x0f00085e. The halved CR4 takes CR3's bit 0 as its bit 15. The ROM stores them as given, doubled while bit 3 of the word 0x0f000854 is set.
Setting 1, the frame buffer window ratio: CR4 to 0x0f000864 and CR3 to 0x0f000862, each unless its bit 14 is set.

Setting 4, the display window offset: CR4 to 0x09075322 and CR3 to 0x09075320, each unless its bit 15 is set. The longwords 0x0907531c and 0x09075320 added give the words 0x0f000856 (high) and 0x0f000858 (low).
Settings 2 and 3: with bit 3 of the word 0x0f000854 set, CR3 and CR4 are each doubled, keeping bit 15.
Setting 2, the display window position: CR4 to 0x0907531e and CR3 to 0x0907531c, each unless its bit 15 is set, then the sums as for setting 4.
Setting 3, the display window size: CR4 to 0x0f00085c and CR3 to 0x0f00085a, each unless its bit 15 is set.
Any other setting: the reject response through entry 66, r11 = 0.
With bit 0 of CR2 set, the words 0x0f000856..0x0f000864 go to the card registers 0x0a100002..0x0a100010. Then the status response through entry 68, r11 = 0.

Entries 43, 47 and 50 call it first. In the movie mode (bit 6 of the word 0x0f000868) with bit 15 of the status word 0x0f000850 clear, the capture B status bit for Sega's VDERR (video decode error): with bit 2 of 0x0f000897 set around it, the word 0x0f00086a without bit 13 goes to 0x0a10001a, the kept word unchanged. Then with bit 1 of 0x0f000897 set around it the decode bit, bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854, is cleared and the word written to 0x0a100000, then set to bit 5 of 0x0f000890 inverted, 95's decode switch, and written again.

Entry 71, entry 54's audio step for a picture search with audio. It runs entry 69's steps with bit 1 of 0x0f000895 set, which changes three things: a sector it cannot use stays for entry 54 to drop, a packet without a PTS is taken too, and no state is set. It returns by jumping to the address at 0x0907537c. r10 tells what it found: bit 0 no sector, bit 1 a timestamp taken, bit 2 an audio cut, bit 3 a PTS, bit 4 an audio packet.

Entry 69, task 9's card work for bit 2 of 0x09075388, a new audio connection. Each call looks at the sector at the audio position and returns. The first audio packet with a PTS is kept for entry 73's DMA channel 3: the source at 0x090752c8, the count at 0x090752dc and the destination at 0x090752d0. The audio state becomes 3 and bit 2 is cleared. Other sectors are skipped.
An audio cut (bit 2 of 0x0907534d): the bit, buffer empty and bit 6 of the video layer byte 0x0907532a cleared, the job's bit 2 cleared and the audio state 1. r10 = 4.

A sector at the position: under the sector lock as task 9, entry 92 pairs the device end 0x8c with the audio partition's end, then entry 94 gives the slot. None sets bit 4 of the audio status, buffer empty, with r10 = 1.
The sector is at 0x09000230 + 0x930 * slot. Bit 0 of the layer byte 0x0907532e, the audio layer, takes the sector's data below.
The system layer: a system header 000001bb at +36 skips the sector, and the packet start code there must be an audio stream's, 000001c0 to 000001df.
Not audio data: bit 5 of the audio status and flag bit 21, Sega's ASERR, with MPST when its mask bit is set. The sector is skipped.
Skip the sector. For entry 71 nothing moves. Otherwise with bit 2 of the mode release it through entry 93 under the sector lock, or add 1 to the position.
With bit 1 of the stream mode the stream ID's low 6 bits must equal the stream number 0x0907533e.
Bit 0 of the mode with the submode's EOR bit, +18, or bit 1 with a system end code at +2320, 24 bytes before the last longword of a form 2 sector's data, sets bit 7 of 0x09075370, the stream's end.
Entry 52 reads the packet header from +40. A bad one is not audio data, an empty packet is skipped.
Entry 69 skips a packet without a PTS. Entry 71 takes it either way, bit 3 marking a PTS.

The PTS less 783 is the audio timestamp 0x090752ad over 0x090752a4, as in entry 72: below 783 it becomes 0 without bit 32, and with bit 32 the low 32 bits become the PTS less 784. 0x090752b0 is cleared.

The data: an odd start sends its first byte alone as the high byte of the word 0x09075366 to 0x0a180002, keeping the start at 0x09075360 and the length at 0x09075364 (bit 4 of 0x09075370). Otherwise words go to 0x0a180000, and an odd length leaves the last byte (bit 5).
The audio layer: mode 1 gives 2048 bytes from +16 and clears the job's bit. Modes 0 and 2 check the channel number, +17, with bit 5 of the stream mode, and the EOR bit.
A system end code at +24 with bit 1 of the mode stops the audio: the job's bit cleared and the state 1. Either way the sector is skipped.
Otherwise 2324 bytes from +24 when bit 5 of +19, the coding information byte, is set, 2048 otherwise. Entry 72 takes bit 5 of the submode, +18.
The source, the count and the destination go to 0x090752c8, 0x090752dc and 0x090752d0, and the job's bit 2 is cleared. For entry 69 the audio state becomes 3.
Entry 71 returns through the address at 0x0907537c.
nop, padding
nop, padding
A next audio cut (bit 3 of 0x0907534d): the bit, the job's bit 3 and bit 5 of 0x0f000894 (a next audio connection) cleared.

Entry 70, task 9's card work for bit 3 of 0x09075388, a new next audio connection. As entry 69 with the next audio's records, it keeps the first audio packet with a PTS for the switch: its data at 0x090752cc, 0x090752de and 0x090752d4, its PTS less 783 as the next audio timestamp 0x090752b9 over 0x090752bc, the odd byte bits in bits 0 and 1 of 0x09075370 and the stream's end in bit 3. Bit 3 of 0x0907534c then marks the connection prepared for entry 75, and bit 3 is cleared. It pairs no device end.
A sector at the position through entry 94 under the sector lock. None waits.
Not audio data: bit 5 of the audio status and flag bit 23, Sega's ANERR (next audio stream data error), with MPST when its mask bit is set. The sector is skipped.
Skip the sector: with bit 2 of the next mode release it, otherwise add 1 to the next position.
The stream number check, and the stream's end as in entry 69, into bit 3 of 0x09075370.
Entry 52. A bad header is not audio data. An empty packet or one without a PTS is skipped.
The PTS less 783, as in entry 69, is the next audio timestamp.
The data as in entry 69, with bits 0 and 1 of 0x09075370 and the words 0x09075368, 0x0907536c and 0x0907536e.

The audio layer as entry 72 reads it, the form from the submode, +18. A system end code at +24 with bit 1 of the mode drops the next connection: the job's bit 3 and bit 5 of 0x0f000894 cleared. Either way the sector is skipped.
The data goes to 0x090752cc, 0x090752de and 0x090752d4, bit 3 of 0x0907534c is set and the job's bit 3 cleared.
nop, padding before the literals
nop, padding

A mode without bit 7: an audio stream number (CR2's high byte) above 31 or a video stream number (CR4's high byte) above 15 gives the reject response through entry 66. The ROM checks only a mode with bit 0 set.

9D, Set MPEG Stream, entry 13, over the ROM's 0xb2c4. The audio stream's mode is CR1's low byte with its stream and channel numbers in CR2, the video stream's CR3's low byte and CR4. Bit 0 of CR3's high byte selects the next streams. A mode with bit 7 set, Sega's no change, leaves its part alone throughout.

A mode without bit 7 whose part is in state 5 (audio 0x0f00089d, video 0x0f00089c) gives the wait response through entry 67, and so does bit 1 or 2 of 0x0f000892, for the next streams too. The ROM checks bits 1 and 2 for the current streams only, and no state.

The current streams, bit 0 of CR3's high byte clear: a mode without bit 7 whose part's state is not 1 sets bit 1 of 0x09075371 (audio) or bit 3 of 0x0907535c (video). The ROM sets them for a mode with bit 0 or 4, in any state.
The records 0x0907533c and 0x09075338, or 0x09075344 and 0x09075340 for the next streams.

A mode without bit 7 goes to byte 1 of its record, the stream number to byte 2 when the mode's bit 0 is set and the channel number to byte 3 when its bit 4 is set. The ROM stores a mode with bit 7 as well. Then the status response through entry 68, r11 = 0.
The reject response through entry 66, r11 = 0.
The wait response through entry 67, r11 = 0.
Zero padding from the end of the last literal pool to the end of the decoded block.

Diagnostic words from startup's tests: 0x0f000000 the address lines that failed, 0x0f000002 bit 0 byte lanes, bit 1 the pattern, bit 2 interface registers, bit 3 interface data, bits 4..7 the MPEG card mask. Command FF returns both words.

The ROM sum from 0x06f0. In the monitor, the monitor's state instead: +0 line length, +1 and +2 the transmit ring's write and read indexes, +3 line ready, +4 L's address, +8 its word, +10 its mode (1 read, 2 write).
In the monitor: the line, up to 255 bytes and the CR, over RAM that holds task records after a normal reset.
Record 11: lock byte +2, owner +3, waiter link +12. Callers with r11=0x0b070000 select this record with owner token 7.
Current task-record pointer, read by lock services and replaced by task dispatch.
Twelve ready-head words scanned in ascending address order through 0x0f000204. First nonempty queue wins, and +16 links form each ready chain.
In the monitor: the 256-byte transmit ring, over RAM that holds ready heads, timers, the transfer state and task 6's state after a normal reset.

Transfer state: +0 words programmed, +4 pointer to the connection byte, +8 type 0 address, +12 type 0 word count, +14 owner task, +15 sectors left, +16 current slot, +17 partition or filter, +18 status (ff after an error), +19 data-command gate.
Initialization flags, the CR1 low byte of command 04: bit 1 R-W subcode on audio tracks, bit 2 no Mode 2 subheader check, bit 3 Form 2 retries, bit 4 single speed.
Disc flags: bit 5 double speed for the next staged command, cleared by it. Bit 6 disc authentication owns the drive. Bit 7 a B0 report announced another session, kept until the TOC is cleared.
Bit 0 names the status buffer written last: set for 0x0f000274, clear for 0x0f00026c. The status builders flip it.
Play range start (top byte 1 for a track position) and end (top byte the repeat limit).

Command flags: bit 0 stopped, set by a stop, cleared by a seek, pause, read or ring seek. Bit 2 scan requested. Bit 3 busy, cleared at the report of the frame that sends the command or when a request is only answered. Bit 4 scan backward. Bit 5 reply not yet taken, cleared one report later. Status code 0 while bit 3 or 5 is set. Bit 6 standby timer running. Bit 7 the last positioning command was not a read: set by a seek, pause or stop and at a scan's end, cleared by a read or ring seek. Only with it set does status code 4 count as settled, and status code 3 starts no delivery. The disc-gone reset and the reset request clear bits 0 and 7.

Read flags: bit 0 repeats used up, PEND at the next pause. Bit 1 R-W subcode during audio play. Bit 2 retry, host status 8. Bit 3 read error, status code 9. Bit 4 the latest report gave or advanced the frame. Bit 5 a data read. Bit 6 reading, sectors delivered through task 5. Bit 7 the read held by a full buffer.
Staged drive command, 12 bytes: command, frame address (bytes 1..3), parameters, byte 10 = 1 or 2, byte 11 = pending flag.
Latest drive report, 11 bytes: status, then Q-subcode fields or the ring-seek word, frame and two words. Byte +11 is 1 when the checksum matched.
Lead-in reports taken: all at 0x0f0002e0, those with status bit 3 at 0x0f0002e4, the others at 0x0f0002e8.
Link state: outgoing packet +0..+11, received sum +12, byte count +13 (0x80 = repeat the packet), full-save flag +14.

Task 5 decoder queue, 48 bytes cleared at entry. Head/tail/count in the first three bytes, read state +4, flags +5, decoder status +6, slots +12 (prepared), +13 (in DMA) and +14 (done), frames at +28 (target), +32, +36, +40 and +44 (next). Reset setup transfers pool indices 0 and 1 here, leaving 200 pool entries.

Buffer command results: +0 the actual size from 52 in words, +4 task 4's copy of the request, +12 the frame address search from 55 (+12 best BCD MSF, +16 best position, +18 partition, +20 result frame, +24 result position, +26 result partition), +28 and +29 the get and put sector lengths from 60.

Decoder interrupt record, shared by the sector pulse and the subcode handler: +0 pulse state, +1 subcode state, +2 the flags taken, +3 pulse tolerance or subcode pack done, +4 subcode pack, +5 symbol, +6 frame of the block, +7 missed pulses or syncs, +8 pulse interval, +12 the last TCNT4 time.

Task 2's subcode state: +0 next ring pack to decode, +1 next ring pack for the host, +2 state (0 idle, 1 waiting for pack 9, 2 running, 3 overrun), +4 and +5 the last P and Q results, +8 the address of the pack being decoded. Locator terms follow at 0x0f0006f8 and the P correction's notes at 0x0f000708.

Correction state: +0 header address of the slot being corrected, +4 its saved header long, +8 Q result, +9 P result (bits 0..6 corrections in the last pass, bit 7 a vector that failed), +10 Q and P pairs left, +11 slot from task 5.
Task 12 state: +0 request CR1, CR2, +4 request CR3, CR4, +8 flags (bit 0 a request not yet taken, bit 1 get, bit 2 get and delete, bit 3 put), +9 first slot, +10 count, +11 connection end or filter.

Task 13's request and state: +0 r1 (CR1, CR2), +4 r2 (CR3, CR4), +8 flags (bit 0 a request not yet taken, bit 1 copying, bit 2 moving, bit 3 an error), +9 the current slot, +10 the position, +11 the sectors left, +12 the source partition's end 0x20 | p, +13 the destination filter.
Task 13 flags: bit 0 a request not yet taken, bit 1 a copy runs, bit 2 a move runs, bit 3 the copy or move failed, which command 67 reports.
Task 4's request: +0 r1 (CR1, CR2) and +4 r2 (CR3, CR4) of the last command posted to task 4, +8 bit 0 a request task 4 has not taken. Task 4 copies it to 0x0f0006c0.
Bit 0 set while task 4 has not taken the request at 0x0f000738.

File system state: +0 CR1, CR2 and +4 CR3, CR4 of the last file system command, +8 sectors left to read, +0xc ID counter of a skip, +0x10 the placed file ID, +0x14 window (first ID << 8 | file count), +0x18 frame of the sector with the next record (0: none), +0x1c root directory frame, +0x20 next record's offset, +0x22 root directory sectors, +0x24 table offset, +0x26 window result, +0x27 state (0 none, 1 reading, 2 ready, 4 aborting), +0x28 step, +0x29 record count, +0x2a table index, +0x2c file number, +0x2d filter mode, +0x2e filter.
32-byte scratch window, output accumulators at +0x10 and +0x14.
MPEG task state cleared by 0xa4d0: 96 bytes through 0x0f00089f.
Kept copy of the card register 0x0a100000: bit 0 the decode bit, bit 1 set while the display is off, bit 3 clear for high definition, bits 4..7 from A4, the high byte from A3.

Kept copy of the card register 0x0a100014, the decoder's modes: bit 0 VSYNC timing, bit 1 output to VDP2, bit 2 clear while paused, bit 3 clear while frozen, bits 4 and 5 the frame bank, bit 6 movie mode, bit 7 clear in the sector buffer mode.

Play flags, the first byte of the longword that activation sets to 0x67818022: bits 0 and 1 play, bit 2 automatic video transfer, bit 3 a current video connection, bit 4 synchronized play, bit 5 decode off, bit 6 automatic audio transfer, bit 7 the synchronized pause entry 35 keeps.

Decode flags: bit 0 decode stopped, from card status bit 13 clear. Bit 2 from card status bit 12 clear. Bits 5, 4 and 1 set while entry 35 runs its entries for event bits 0, 1 and 2. Bit 6, in the known cards' code, from a GOP start until a picture with a later temporal reference. Bit 7 an interlaced scan.

Card flags: bit 0 a video switch at a stream's end (known cards' code only), bit 1 a DMA channel 2 end, bit 2 a DMA channel 3 end, bit 3 entry 35 running, bit 6 the sector buffer mode, bit 7 the card bit, which opens the MPEG commands and task 9's card work.

Pause flags: bits 0..2 the pause (2 paused, 5 an interval, 0 released), bits 4..6 the freeze the same way. Bit 7, in the known cards' code, the synchronized pause the ROM keeps in bit 7 of the play flags.
Connection flags: bits 0 and 4 the video and audio transfers, which a cut clears. Bits 1 and 5 a next video and audio connection. Bit 4 goes to bit 4 of 0x0a00001a, and with it set bit 7 drives PB6.
Card events for task 8's entry 35, set by the capture B handler 0xa190: bit 0 for bit 11 of the card's status word clear, bit 1 for bit 6, bit 2 for bit 4 (an interval).
Set while code uses a card register: bit 0 0x0a180008, bit 1 0x0a100000, bit 2 0x0a10001a, bit 3 the word 6 read through 0x0a100022. Commands that use the same register wait.

BOOKMARK.DESCRIPTION: Power-on reset PC = 0x428.
Initial SP = 0x0f001000.
Manual-reset PC = 0x428.
Manual-reset SP = 0x0f001000.
The quoted Hitachi 1993 copyright, 34 bytes with no terminator. R reads only its first 32 bytes from area 0.
Value 0xe2e09ba6, which makes the sum of all big-endian ROM longwords zero modulo 2^32.
Entry address supplied by both power-on and manual-reset PC vectors.
Sum every big-endian ROM longword modulo 2^32 and store it at 0x0f000004. No comparison or startup rejection occurs in this routine.
Vector 4: restart at 0x0428 without a reset. Vector 12 (0x09ba), SCI1 (0x09c6) and the unused interrupt sources (0x09cc) restart the same way.
Vector 10: stop all four DMA channels as startup does, 8 to the transfer control 0x0a000002, return. No task is told.
Reserved vectors and TRAPA 0x2f..0x3f return at once. Slot illegal instruction, CPU address error and NMI return the same way from 0x093a, 0x0940 and 0x09b4.
Reset with PB10 (TEST, TP3) low. SCI1 clocked synchronous sends the ROM sum's low byte, then after a delay a byte built from the diagnostic words, whose bit 2 stays set unless an address line failed.
Wait until PB10 reads high 200000 times in a row. A low read starts the count again.
SCI1 asynchronous 8N1, BRR1 0x41 (about 9600 bps at 20 MHz), SSR1 cleared, which sends TDR1's last byte again. State at 0x0f000004 cleared, prompt ':'.
PBCR1 bits 5:4 to 10: PB10 becomes RxD1.
Poll forever with interrupts masked: receive, transmit, a completed line, L's repeat.
R address: area 0 reads only 0x0400 + the low five bits, area 7 only 0x0f000000..0x0f000007. Answers '>', four hex digits and CR.
W address value: a byte (odd address) or word write. Areas 5 and 7 refused.
L address [value]: read or write the address once a loop until the next CR. Areas 0, 5 and 7 refused.
Initialize thirteen task records, chain eleven into the first ready head, then select and dispatch task 1 at 0x63dc. Initial frames hold PC/SR only.
TRAPA 0x2e: reset timers, DMA and transfer state, re-create the records of every task except 6 and 14, chain them for a fresh start and dispatch. Task 6 resumes after its trap.
TRAPA 0x28: initialize the record of task r11 >> 24 again, as at startup.
Wait for a message with an exception-only frame. Queued messages make the current task ready. A matching partner link can bypass ordinary ready selection.

TRAPA 0x20: post r11, run the destination at once, sender (bits 23..16) waits in state 2. Refuses a destination in state 2 or 3. A destination already in a ready queue is looked for in the queue whose head slot lies 16 bytes after its own. For the last four heads (IDs 1, 13, 9 and 14) that slot is in the disc extension's collection state at 0x0f000208..0x0f000217, followed as a record unless it reads 0. From a zero link the search goes on through the ROM longwords at 0x10 and 0x944 to an unaligned longword read at 0x00090019.
TRAPA 0x29: r12 and r13 into the partner's first two mailbox words (+24 and +28), the replier waits in state 3 and the partner runs. No partner: diagnostic 5, r0 = -1.
Store message and append destination only when state1 and not already ready. Existing occupied slot is overwritten without incrementing occupied count. No task switch inside this trap.
TRAPA 0x22: post r11, then queue a destination in state 1 or 4 at the head its class byte names, bit 7 the first head.
Append current record to its ID-selected ready queue, mark state 4, select and dispatch. Requires an existing full context at record +8. The ready link is not cleared before append.
Unchecked task ID in r1. Initialize record, optional PC/SR frame and descriptor-selected clear range. A null stack leaves saved SP untouched.
First nonempty of twelve head words 0x0f0001d8..0x0f000204. Pop head, clear record +16, return record in r12/r13 and r0=0. r10 survives. Empty queues invoke diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b.
Use signed record state as index into 0x1358. Mark state 5, clear +6, publish current record, switch SP in JMP delay slot. State 4 restores a full context, states 0/3/5/6 only PC/SR.
State-1 dispatch reads an optional per-task PC at 0x09075800 + 4*ID, consumes a mailbox word into r11, then RTEs to the original or replaced PC.
Dispatch for state 2: r12 and r13 from +24 and +28, the first two mailbox words, cleared, then PC and SR.
80-byte frame: MACL, MACH, GBR, PR, r13..r0, PC, SR. Record +8 advances to post-return SP. r14 and VBR are not restored.
Restore PC/SR and consume eight bytes. Record +8 is unchanged. No general registers, PR, GBR, MACH or MACL are restored. Their values come from the intervening execution path.

Destination high byte and source/class second byte select unchecked tables. Class bit7 bypasses ordinary source filter and selects alternate slots. Source mismatch or null slot reaches diagnostic trap.
TRAPA 0x26: take the lock without waiting. r0 = 0 when taken or held by the same owner token, -1 otherwise. Owners 0x80..0xff never match.
TRAPA 0x27 with VBR=0. Release owner-matched lock or transfer ownership to a waiter and enter scheduler context saving. r11 high bytes select record and owner.
Save 72 bytes below the PC/SR frame, store the total 80-byte frame pointer in current-record +8, then branch to 0x102e. r14 is not in this frame.
TRAPA 0x2a with VBR=0. TAS.B acquires an empty lock, and contention appends the current record to its waiter chain. Scratch r0/r10/r12/r13, direct return restores exception PC/SR/SP.
Stored owner is sign-extended, token unsigned. Equal bytes 0x80..0xff take the different-owner path. Equal low tokens invoke diagnostic TRAPA 0x2b, r0=10.
Continuation after selection at 0x10a8: state=6 and exception SP stored for r10 record. r13 must identify selected record for dispatch at 0x1118.
Record IDs the restart initializes: 1, 2, 4, 12, 13, 7, 9, 8, 5, 11, 3.
Seven state destinations: 0/3/5/6 -> 0x11aa, 1 -> 0x1130, 2 -> 0x116c, 4 -> 0x117c. No local state bounds check.
Fifteen ready-list head pointers. Null entries and signed out-of-range indices are not validated by the local release code.
Fifteen record pointers, indexed by r11[31:24]. Entries 10 and 14 alias 0x0f0001bc. Index 11 selects 0x0f000168. No local index bounds check.

Descriptor pointer per task ID 0..14. The post routine at 0x11be reads the slot word for a message's class, task creation at 0x1058 the clear range at +0x6c and +0x70. IDs 0 and 14 have none, and 3, 10 and 11 share 0x1960.
Task 1: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Class 5 to 0x0f000020. Creation clears 0x0f000020..0x0f000023.
Task 2: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 0x80 and 0x81 to 0x0f00003c, 0x0f000040 and 0x0f000044. Creation clears 0x0f00003c..0x0f000047.
Task 4: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 5 and 0x81 to 0x0f000078, 0x0f00007c and 0x0f000080. Creation clears 0x0f000078..0x0f000083.

Task 5: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 1, 4, 6, 0x80, 0x81 and 0x84 to 0x0f0000ac, 0x0f0000a8, 0x0f0000a4, 0x0f00009c, 0x0f0000b0 and 0x0f0000a0. Creation clears 0x0f00009c..0x0f0000b3.

Task 6: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0x81 and 0x83 to 0x0f0000d0, 0x0f0000d4, 0x0f0000d8, 0x0f0000dc, 0x0f0000e0, 0x0f0000e4 and 0x0f0000cc. Creation clears 0x0f0000cc..0x0f0000e7.
Task 7: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3, 4, 6, 7 and 0x81 to 0x0f000100, 0x0f000104, 0x0f000108, 0x0f00010c and 0x0f000110. Creation clears 0x0f000100..0x0f000113.

Task 8: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 8, 9, 0x81, 0x89, 0x8a, 0x8b and 0x8c to 0x0f00013c, 0x0f000140, 0x0f000144, 0x0f00012c, 0x0f000130, 0x0f000138 and 0x0f000134. Creation clears 0x0f00012c..0x0f000147.
Task 9: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 9 and 0x81 to 0x0f000164 and 0x0f000160. Creation clears 0x0f000160..0x0f000167.
Task 12: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Classes 3 and 0x81 to 0x0f000198 and 0x0f00019c. Creation clears 0x0f000198..0x0f00019f.
Task 13: slot words for classes 0..13, then 0x80..0x8c from +56. Class 0x81 to 0x0f0001b8. Creation clears 0x0f0001b8..0x0f0001bb.
Tasks 3, 10 and 11: every slot null, so a post to them raises the diagnostic trap. Empty clear range.
Prepare disc collection: validate nonzero address/length, compare the address with the lead-out, clear decoded header and initialize destination/count state.
Copy sector payload between TRAPA 0x2a and TRAPA 0x27. Decode and process the entry only when no encoded bytes remain.
Invokes decoder: source 0x09075848, destination 0x09075800. Saves/restores SR and masks interrupts around decode/entry.
Loads supplied VBR value from decoded +0. No local pointer validation.
Calls nonzero entry pointer from decoded +0x3c. The entry return value is discarded.
Expansion loader for the MPEG card's code: length at 0x0e000000, data from +4. No local SR masking.
Calls @(4,r1) without zero check. The optional disc callback must preserve r1 for the expected table.
Calls expansion cleanup, then shares the saved-PR epilogue. No incoming branch originates in 0x19d4..0x1b79.
Final bootstrap task calls 0x1efc then spins at 0x1be6. It does not wait on a mailbox or poll a device register.

Three NOPs and a delayed unconditional branch back here. No software release condition or register reads. Task 14 runs it whenever no other task is ready, and interrupts post the messages that wake the others.
TRAPA 0x2b returns immediately. Callers pass a condition code in r0.
TRAPA 0x2c returns at once.
Clear the software timer table and disable the compare-match interrupt, keeping the clock running.
ITU4 overflow, vector 98. Increments the timer clock high part 0x0f00021c.
ITU4 compare match A, vector 96. Posts every expired identifier with TRAPA 0x21, programs GRA4 for the next deadline or disables IMIA4, then reschedules through 0x102e.
ITU4 compare match B (vector 97): post the waiting messages and reschedule.

TRAPA 0x24 starts timer r11 with duration r10. Deadline = (0x0f00021c << 8 plus TCNT4 bits 15..8) + r10 - (6 * r10 >> 8). Up to four entries ordered by deadline. A new first entry programs GRA4 and enables IMIA4. A full table returns r0 = -1.
TRAPA 0x25 removes the r11 entry from the four-entry timer table at 0x0f000220 and returns r0 = 0, or -1 when absent. Removing the first entry reprograms ITU4 GRA or clears ITU4 IMIEA.
TRAPA 0x2d: an interrupt handler's message waits at 0x0f000240 or 0x0f000244 until ITU4 compare match B, 0x7d counts later.

Clear the interface's command flags (0 to 0x0a000004), set IRQ6 priority 6 (0x0060 into 0x05ffff86), enable the command interrupt (0x0001 to 0x0a000008), write 0x0be1 to 0x0a00001e and publish NUL CDBLOCK in CR1..CR4 (0x0a000010..0x0a000017). Host commands raise IRQ6 from here on.

IRQ6 vector 70, raised by the interface chip when the host writes CR4: save the full task context, switch to the interrupt stack, clear the command flag at 0x0a000004, which releases IRQ6, read CR1..CR4 and dispatch.
Nonzero response r11 invokes TRAPA 0x21. Command05 constructs 06810002, stores it in task6 class81 slot, and makes waiting task6 ready. Scheduler then resumes its saved continuation 2798.
High nibble 1: commands 10 (play), 11 (seek) and 12 (scan) through the table at 0x2068.
High nibble 2: command 20 (subcode) through the table at 0x208c.
High nibble 3: commands 30 (set CD device connection), 31 (get it) and 32 (last partition reached).
High nibble 4: commands 40..48 through the table at 0x20d0.
High nibble 5: commands 50..56 through the table at 0x210c.
High nibble 6: commands 60..67 through the table at 0x2140.
High nibble 7: commands 70..75 through the table at 0x2178.
Commands 90..9F. Rejected without bit 1 of 0x0f00027d (MPEG card present) and, except 93, without the card bit (bit 7 of 0x0f000892). 93 goes to 0xa050, the others to 0xf800.
Commands A0..AF, with the card bit needed for every command. AE goes to 0xa148, AF to 0xa0f0, the others to 0xf800.
Group E: e0..e2 through the three-entry table at 0x2288. e3..ef take the reject response.
Command 06: clear the data-transfer byte 0x0f00025b and end the transfer at 0x2568.
Data commands 02, 20, 61, 63, 64 and 73: wait status while a transfer is open, otherwise the handler. A data transfer request opens one.
Subcode0 echoes r2 twice, subcode1 returns startup diagnostic longwords, others return zero. Produces no message.
Start a transfer on DMA channel 1 under lock record 3: type 0 one RAM block to the host, type 2 a partition's sectors to the host, type 3 sectors from the host.
DMA channel 1 end (vector 74): arm the next slot of a sector transfer, or mark the end, and return with RTE.
Command 06: stop DMA channel 1, copy words the host sent past the channel, answer the words transferred and post the end to the owner.
Task 6 initializes buffer metadata and local state, preserves diagnostic byte 0x0f00027d, updates device registers and waits on its internal mailbox. Setup posts no message.
TRAPA 0x23 saves continuation 0x2798. After reset, task 14 runs next. Host commands, the end of a transfer, task 7, the sector buffer, task 5, the standby timer and the drive link post its messages.
Task 6 continuation after its wait at 0x2796, GBR 0x0f00025c. In drive state 0 every message except a drive report waits again.
Task 6 in drive states other than 0 and 17..22: class 4, 5, 6, 7 and 0x81 messages through the tables at 0x29c8, drive reports (class 0x83) through 0x3aa8 and the periodic status.
After each drive report: PB6 from the audio pre-emphasis bit in drive states 6 and 12, status words to CR1..CR4 when bit 1 of 0x0a000004 is set, and 0x0400 to 0x0a00001e.
Handler tables: class 0x83 at 0x29c8, class 6 at 0x29cc, class 5 at 0x29d0, class 7 at 0x29e4, class 0x81 at 0x29f8 and class 4 at 0x2a30.
Fill 0x09000000..0x09000203 with ff, clear 0x09000210..0x09000217 and selected GBR-relative fields. Loops have fixed RAM endpoints, no external input.
Disc gone: clear the TOC area, post 07060000 to task 7, write 0x0020 (DCHG) to 0x0a00001e and clear request flags.

Drive states 17 and 18 (after status 81 and 80): Open Tray stages command 0c again in 17 and only clears busy in 18. Other host requests are kept and read the TOC with command 03, status 82 reads it, other reports pick the next drive state.
Stage command 03 (read TOC) with the session in byte 1 and 0x0f000289.
A report is taken only when its checksum matched and no staged command is still waiting for the report after the one that carried it.
Drive states 19, 21 and 22 (TOC read and the seek after it): host requests are kept for later, status code 0 collects the TOC, code 9 ends it, code 4 in state 22 completes the seek.
Class 0x81 payload 0: clear the play settings and restart the other tasks through TRAPA 0x2e with interrupts masked.
Class 0x81 payload 2: the disc-gone reset and command 0c, drive state 17.
Class 0x81 payload 3: play range between track positions from 0x0f000264 and 0x0f000268.
Stage command 09 (seek) to frame r0, also kept as the target 0x0f0002a0. Drive state 4, host status 4.
Class 0x81 payload 5: play the current range, keeping the position when bit 7 of 0x0f00025d is set.
Stage command 06 (read) from target frame 0x0f0002a0. Drive state 4, host status 4 or 8.
Class 0x81 payload 4: play range from a start frame and a frame count.
Class 0x81 payload 6: seek to a track position.
Class 0x81 payload 7: seek to a frame.
Class 0x81 payload 8: pause, or seek to the target when neither playing nor reading.
Stage command 08 (pause). Drive state 5 or 10, host status 1.
Class 0x81 payload 9: command 04, drive state 9, host status 2.
Class 6 payload 0, the standby timer expired: command 05, drive state 8, host status 2.
Class 0x81 payloads 10 and 11: scan forward or backward with command 0a or 0b.
Start frame of a track and the index and end for a track-form command.
T = 1 when the target lies inside the play range 0x0f000298..0x0f00029c.
Normalize a frame or track position and store it as the target 0x0f0002a0.
Class 0x81 payloads 12 and 13: send the Q record or the TOC through 0x23ba.
Class 5 payload 0 from task 5: read again from 0x0f0002b4.
Class 5 payload 2 from task 5: read error, status code 9, pause.
Class 7 payload 0: read from request frame 0x0f0002bc, or from a default frame when it is 0.
Class 7 payload 1, sent after a disc header was recognized: pause (command 08).
Class 7 payload 2, a sector request: read (command 06) from request frame 0x0f0002bc, with the disc-authentication flag set.

Give-up after three failed ring seeks, or a read with no sector by its 150th report under authentication (post 07060003), and class 7 payload 3 at 0x3754: clear the request flags and seek back with command 09.
Class 7 payload 4, an authentication seek: drive state 0x21, request frame 0x0f0002bc copied to target frame 0x0f0002a0, and command 02 to the target frame. Retries enter at 0x3788.
Class 4 payload 0: a read held for a full buffer continues from 0x0f0002c0.
Class 4 payload 1: hold the read and pause in drive state 10.
Read the TOC of the next session announced by a B0 pointer.

Lead-in Q reports: counts them in 0x0f0002e0 (bit 3 of the status in 0x0f0002e4, otherwise 0x0f0002e8), stores track, A0, A1 and A2 entries, B0 session pointers, and seeks to the first frame when the TOC is complete.
The seek after the TOC settled: drive state 11, 07060001 to task 7 and a kept host request dispatched again.
Report in a served drive state. Status code 8 stops the drive: task 7 is told when disc authentication owns the drive, then disc-gone or error handling. Other codes continue at 0x3b48.
Drive report in task 6 by drive state 0x0f0002a5. State 0x21 (authentication seek) continues at 0x40d0.
Report handlers for drive states 4..12.
Status code 3 in drive state 4: start sector delivery through task 5 (05060000 plus the read mode) and set drive state 12.
Status code 4 after a seek or pause: take the position and set drive state 11.
Playing: follow the position, read again after a jump, stop or repeat at the end of the play range.
Drive states 11 and 12: follow the position until the target is reached, seek again after a jump, end a read after 150 reports without a sector.
Target reached: pause in drive state 5, play on in drive state 6 or start a scan.
In drive state 5, start standby timer 06060000 for word 0x0f000260 seconds (180 when 0).

Authentication seek report. At the target position 0x0f0002a0 with bit 2 of the status byte set, report word 0x0f0002d1 goes to 0x0f00027e, words 0x0f0002d6 and 0x0f0002d8 go to 0x0f0002ec and 0x0f0002ee, and 07060002 is posted to task 7. Words 0 and ffff seek again 206 frames further on, twice at most, and the third such report gives up at 0x3750.
Copy r1, r2 and r3 to command bytes 0x0f0002c4..0x0f0002cf. Byte 10 becomes 1 or 2, byte 11 is the pending flag the link reads.
Post 05060003 or 05060007 to task 5 by bits 6 and 1 of 0x0f0002a7.
BCD to binary, and BCD minutes, seconds and frames to a frame count at 0x41b6.
Track and offset of a frame from the TOC at 0x09000064, lead-out 0xaa.
Frame 0x0f000294 from the absolute time of a Q report.
Host status words and Q record for target frame 0x0f0002a0.
Host status bytes and Q record from a drive report.
Write the eight status bytes to the next of the buffers 0x0f00026c and 0x0f000274.
Reset the next status buffer and Q record to ff with the host status code.

Task 5 initializes device registers and local queue state, takes two indices from the shared pool, and waits on its mailbox. Task 6's read requests, the decoder interrupt, the end of DMA channel 0, task 1 and command 30 post its messages.
Mailbox wait through TRAPA 0x23, saved continuation 0x45e2. Setup neither polls hardware nor posts a message.
Task 5's message handling: DMA channel 0 end (0x84), sector pulses locked (0x80), task 6 requests (class 6), task 1 finished (class 1) and command 30 (0x81).
Class 6 payloads 0..9: read start, retry, stop, nothing, subcode on, read after a full buffer, subcode off, resumed read, buffer hold.
A sector arrived: read the frame from its header, synchronize on two sectors in a row, approach the target, stream, check the decoder status by mode and complete the sector.
A read request: target from 0x0f0002b8, a slot prepared for DMA, then the decoder's sector pulse enabled.
The sector pulses are locked: start DMA channel 0 and prepare the next slot.
Task 1 finished a sector: complete the queued slots or send the next marked slot to task 1.
Command 30: connect CD device 0 to a filter or disconnect it.
Stop a read: DMA and decoder off, task 1 started again when correcting, queue flushed to two slots.
Send the oldest queued slot to task 1 (01050010).
Append r1 low-byte index unless ff. Head/tail/count at 0x0f000314, links at 0x0f000354. No validation, count wraps, and the caller must provide a detached tail link.

Decoder queue 0x0f000314: once more than two slots are queued, the head slot is delivered from CD device 0. While 0x0f000788 is not ff the CD device connections are cleared first, so the slot returns to the pool.
Take a pool slot for the next transfer and append it to the decoder queue.
BCD MSF in r1 bits 31..8 to a frame address that includes the 150-frame lead.
Frame address to BCD MSF, the inverse of 0x4e0c, by restoring division against 45000, 4500, 750, 75, 10 and 1.
Take head index from pool at 0x0f000348. Return r1=index or 255 when empty, r2=remaining count. Detach taken link and reset head/tail after last removal.
Take a run of r1 slots from the free pool head.
Append a run that ends at link ff to the free pool tail, then run the pool notification 0x51fa.
Route slot r1 from source r2 through the filters at 0x5264, append it to the destination partition and post 07040000 to task 7 when notify bit 0 is set. Unrouted slots return to the pool.
Slot at position r2 of partition r1. Records 0x0f000600 + 6p hold head, tail, count, notify flags, cursor position and cursor slot. Links live at 0x0f000354.
Return r3 slots from position r2 of partition r1 to the free pool at 0x0f000348.

CD device connection 0x0f000690, filter records 0x0f000420 + 16f (mode bit 6 frame range, bits 0..3 subheader fields, bit 4 inverts the subheader result), true output +2 and false output +3 of 0x0f0005a0 + 4f.
Clear 24 connection ends through 0x54f0: filter sources from 0x5402, partition ends from 0x5408, false outputs from 0x540e.
Clear one filter record. No code reaches it.
Empty a partition into the free pool.
Store a connection for CD devices (0x0f000690) or filters (0x0f0005a0).
Task 4's messages: the filter settings 40, 42, 44 and 46, Reset Selector 48, Calculate Actual Size 52 and Execute FAD Search 55. Each ends with ESEL.
52: words for the host by the get sector length, reading each sector's mode for length 0.
55: the sector with the target frame address, or the nearest frame below it, from a position to the partition's end.
DMA channel 0 end (vector 72): keep the decoder status, start the next transfer and post 05840010 to task 5 through TRAPA 0x2d.
Program DMA channel 0 for a prepared slot: slot + 12, 0x492 words, CHCR0 0x436d.
IRQ7 (vector 71): decoder flags masked with their enables. Bit 4 the sector pulse, bit 5 the subcode.
Lock on the sector pulse: two pulses one sector period apart start the decoder and post 05800012 to task 5.
IRQ7 flag 5: one subcode frame. Hunting counts two block starts (flag 6), locked counts frames by TCNT4 and stores the symbol in the ring. A completed pack posts 02800010 to task 2.
Time in ITU4 counts: the time high part and TCNT4.
Task 2's messages: 02800010 decodes the completed packs, 02810000 sends the next pack to the host, 02030001 frees lock 3.
Q parity of symbols 0..3, one error corrected.
P parity of the pack, up to two errors corrected.
GF(64) powers of alpha, field polynomial x^6 + x + 1.
GF(64) logarithms to base alpha. The log of 0 is 63.
Two-error step: c = alpha^d + alpha^-d gives d for d = 1..23, 0 otherwise.
Command 20 type 1, Get Subcode R-W: WAIT without a pack, else the flags (bit 0 pack data error, bit 1 overrun), 12 words and 02810000 to task 2.
Task 1 waits for source/class 5 and low payload byte 0x10. Accepted work begins at 0x63f2, the sector correction.
Task 1's work for 01050010: correct slot 0x0f00071b and answer 05010011 with the result word 0x0f000718. Slot ff answers nothing.
P, Q and P passes, then up to 5 Q and P pairs as 0x0f000262 allows.
P pass: the 43 columns of 26 words, both bytes of each word.
Q pass: the 26 diagonals of 45 words, both bytes of each word.
P column 42, two lanes.
P columns 2r9 and 2r9+1, four lanes, and the lane correction shared with column 42.
Q diagonals 2r9 and 2r9+1, four lanes, one long read serving both.
GF(2^8) logarithms to base alpha, field polynomial x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1. Entry 0 unused.
Sixteen words XORed after a left shift of four lanes: indexed by the carry out of bit 31 and the inverted bits shifted into 24, 16 and 8.
Commands 61 and 63: busy check, request check 0x6dac, then 0c8100cc for task 12 with the data transfer request.
Command 62: request check 0x6dac, then 0c810062 for task 12. No gate and no busy check.
Command 64: busy check, filter below 24, a count from 1 to the free slots, then 0c810064 for task 12 with the data transfer request.
Task 12 message dispatch: 61..64 from the host, class 3 at the end of a transfer.
Keep a request at 0x0f00071c unless one is not yet taken (T = 1).
Take the kept request into r12 and r13.
End of a sector transfer: return a get and delete's run to the pool, deliver a put's slots, free the transfer lock.
62: connect 0x88 with the partition's end, release the slots to the pool.
61: connect 0x88 with the partition's end, find the first slot, step 0x21.
63: connect 0x88 with the partition's end, unlink the slots, step 0x21.
64: connect 0x88 with the filter, take slots from the pool and clear their first 24 bytes, step 0x20.
Start a type 3 (0x6d78) or type 2 (0x6d7e) transfer, tail-calling 0x23ba.
Check a partition, position and count: ff rejects, 1 waits, 0 fits.
Address and word count of a slot for the get sector length 0x0f0006d8.
Address and word count of a slot for the put sector length 0x0f0006d9.
Commands 65 and 66, Copy and Move Sector Data: destination filter, request check, free slots for 65, then 0d8100cc for task 13.
Command 67, Get Copy Error: ff while task 13 works, 1 after an error, else 0.
Task 13's messages: low byte 65 copies, 66 moves.
65: copy each sector the destination filter's chain passes into a new slot, from device 0x89. ECPY at the end.
66: unlink the run and deliver its slots from device 0x89. ECPY at the end.
Take the request and pair device 0x81 with the source partition's end and 0x89 with the destination filter.
Under the sector lock, T = 1 when either pair changed.
Command 40, Set Filter Range: task 4 sets the start frame and count.
Command 46, Set Filter Connection: task 4 pairs the true output with a partition and the false output with another filter.
Command 48, Reset Selector: task 4 empties partitions and clears connections and filters by flag.
Command 50, Get Buffer Size: free slots (at most 200), 24 partitions, 200 sectors.
Command 60: get sector length from the CR1 low byte, put sector length from the CR2 high byte, ff keeps. 0x40 to 0x0a00001e.
Command 54, Get Sector Info: a sector's frame address and mode 2 subheader.
Record the request for task 4 and post 048100cc, or wait while one is not yet taken.
Answers shared by the buffer commands: 0x91fe, reject, wait and status.
Task 7 initializes disc/header state and waits at 0x77c0. Header-parser exits also target that wait.

Expiry of timer 07070000 (class 7 payload 0). Disc states 2 and 3 store result 0, state 7 keeps the result and other states store 3. A stored result clears 0x0f000788, which blocks later sector delivery.
Class 6 from task 6. Payload 2 continues the authentication seeks at 0x8952.
Payload 7: EFLS with nothing in progress, otherwise state 4 and the end.

Class 4 payload 0, a sector added to the partition: disc state 3 goes to the header scan 0x86d2, 6 to the sector checks 0x8a60, 7 to the extension read 0x8da8, 1 to 0x7954, and 4 releases sectors past the cursor.
A sector added to partition f in disc state 1: dispatch on the step.
Class 3: payload 1 frees the transfer lock.
Free the transfer lock 03070000.
Payload 0 without a root frame: read the volume descriptor, step 1.
Step 1: 01 CD001 and the root directory record.
Read the root directory, step 2.
Parse directory records into the table, up to 256.
Place a file ID against the window: 0 in it (r2 the table index), 1 before it, 2 past it.
Payload 1: read directory record 0x0f00076e, step 3.
Post 06070000 to task 6.
Payload 4: a type 0 transfer of one record.
Payload 5: a type 0 transfer of the window's records.
Payload 2: move the window inside the table, or read the directory again or on.
Skip directory records up to the ID.
Payload 6: the file's frames through filter mode 0x41, step 5.
End a request: EFLS, pause, the state after an abort.
Connect filter and partition f, set the filter record and the notification, post 06070000.

Task 7 class 6 payload 3, and payload 0 while busy: host status 6 gives result 0x11, disc state 7 keeps the result, a header scan with bit 3 of 0x0f0002a7 retries the next frame, other states give result 0 or 3.

Task 7 disc authentication request. Drive state 0, 6 or 7, or nonzero 0x0f00034b, gives result 0. A first track without the data bit gives result 1. A data track continues with a timer and sector reads at 0x85f0.

Data track: start timer 07070000 with duration 200000, connect filter p and partition p for the E0 CR3 partition p, choose frame 150 (or a TOC entry when bit 7 of 0x0f00025f is set), set header scan count 15 and disc state 3, then request sectors.
Disc state 3 sector: take the sector at the cursor through 0x506c and parse it at 0x86ee.
Sector-header state-machine block, r1=raw slot index. Reads payload +0xf8/+0xfc. Exits branch into shared firmware, without an RTS return or complete acceptance decision.
Identifier/mode mismatch processing. External service and traps precede the scan count decision. Copied header fields are not cleared here.
Sets disc state 4 and copies header fields before subsequent state/ID checks. This is not a complete authentication decision.
Copies payload +0xf8/+0xfc to 0x0f00020c/0x0f000210 without local bounds checks.
State byte gates and eight-byte ID comparison select further checks at 0x8874 or continuation at 0x8d00. Copied fields persist on either path.
14000000 decrement/compare/branch iterations precede the branch to 0x8d00.

Disc state 5. TCNT4 selects zone z (0..12) and column c (0..69). Check positions 0x49124 + 1470 * (z + i) + 21 * c for passes 0..2, with exceptions for zones 0 and 12. Then four seeks: 0x3f435, 0x3fe51, the first position plus 0xdea, and the first position.

Seek report (class 6 payload 2). Phases 1 and 3 need a report word within 18 or 20 of the one before. Phases 2 and 3 need report byte 1 >= byte 0 / 2 and byte 3 >= byte 2 / 2. A failure gives result 3 and closes delivery gate 0x0f000788.
Sixteen identifier bytes compared as four big-endian longwords. No string terminator is included.
One pass per check position: disc state 6 and a request for 3 sectors from the position.
Disc state 6 sector: re-scramble it (0x8f1c) and interleave it (0x8f70) into a 294-frame stream. After the third sector, compare the stream from frame 196 with bitmap row zone + pass through 0x8e6e.

Check score 0x0f000789 below 2 gives result 3 and closes the delivery gate. Otherwise result 4. A SEGASYSTEM header also sets ID gate 0x0f0002f9 (and 0x0f0002f8 with the 30-track flag), keeps the header ID at 0x0f0002f0 and stores 1 at 0x0f000786.
Store the result at 0x0f000787 and cancel timer 07070000. Branches arrive from the E0 request at 0x8510, the class 6 path at 0x8494, the header parser at 0x8782, and from 0x8986, 0x89ca and 0x8b74.
Outside disc state 2: disconnect CD device 0, clear the partition notify byte, return sectors past cursor 0x0f00078b to the pool and clear filter p.
After an E0 request, post 06070003 to task 6, restore the saved 04 settings, clear 0x0907adcb and busy flag 0x0f0007b0, write 0x0200 to 0x0a00001e and wait at 0x77c0.

Result 4 is stored on every path here (0x883c, 0x8ba0, 0x8bcc). Clear the expansion area through 0x1b5e and prepare a disc extension through 0x19ec. With an extension, disc state 7 reads its sectors from the header's extension address.
Filter record 0x0f000420 + 16p gets a frame range (count 15, 3 or 0x0f000208 by disc state), partition notify bit 0 is set, CD device 0 is connected to filter p and 06070002 goes to task 6.
Disc state 7 sector: collect it through 0x1a38. After the last sector has been decoded and checked the request completes with result 4 kept.

Compare 106 columns of interleaved bytes with one bitmap row: a8 where the bit is set, 59 where it is clear. A column of n bytes is good when at least (n - m) / 2 match, rounded down, with m 1 for a mask column, 2 for column 8 and 0 otherwise. 11 bad columns in a row stop the walk. 85 good columns add 1 to check score 0x0f000789.
Re-apply the ECMA-130 CD-ROM scrambler to raw sector bytes 12..2351, byte pairs swapped.
Interleave 24-byte frames: each byte moves to its own position 3 to 108 frames later (offsets at 0x90d4).
Bitmap of the SEGA logo: 17 rows of 106 bits, 16 bytes per row, row 0 at the bottom. The checks use rows 0..14.
One bit per column, most significant first. A set bit lowers that column's threshold.
24 byte offsets from a frame start, 72..2615.
Bytes per column, 106 entries, 884 in total.
The status byte of a response: BUSY while a command waits for its reply, ERROR after a read error, otherwise byte 0 of the last status buffer.
Status byte with the data transfer request bit 0x40.
Cached response with the wait bit 0x80.
Command 01: hardware flag, version 1 and longword 0x0f0002fc (MPEG version, drive information, CD block revision). No message.
Command 02: 0xcc words of TOC through task 6 payload 13. Wait status before the drive has a host status.
Command 03: session count and lead-out, or a session's first track and start. No message.
Command 04: standby word and bytes 0x0f000262/0x0f000263, then task 6 payload 0 (reset) or 8 (pause).
Return message 06810002 and mark pending flag at task6 state+74. Response uses cached status. Task 6 handles the message later.
Command 10: play range from two track or frame positions, task 6 payload 3, 4 or 5.
Command 11: task 6 payload 6 (track), 7 (frame), 8 (pause) or 9 (stop).
Command 12: task 6 payload 10 (forward) or 11 (backward).
Command 20 type 0: 5 words of Q record through task 6 payload 12. Type 1 at 0x6354.
Command 70: ffffff posts payload 0 (the root), other IDs in the window that name a directory payload 1.
Command 71: posts payload 2, task 7 places the ID.
Command 72: the window's file count, first ID and end flag.
Command 73, through the data-command gate: 6 words per file, payload 4 for one ID, 5 for ffffff.
Command 74: an ID in the window and an offset below its sectors post payload 6.
Command 75: payload 7, or no message in state 4.
Shared ends of 70..75: state checks, post, reject, wait and the Get File Info response.

ITU3 input capture B (vector 93), one strobe per byte on TIOCB3. A frame is 13 SCI0 transfers: 11 command bytes and their inverted sum out, 11 report bytes and their inverted sum in, then an answer byte (00 for a matching sum). PB2 low starts or restarts a frame.
SCI0 receive (vector 101) after the answer byte. The drive's final byte selects a new packet (00) or a repeat of the last one. Posts 06830000, the drive report, to task 6.

Decoder wrapper. Helper code and constants occupy 0x9904..0x9ce3. Custom register ABI: r1 source, r2 destination, r3 byte length, r0 result (0 or -1). Default decompiler calling conventions are not authoritative for this routine. N = byte length >> 3. Rejects N < 2, processes N-1 eight-byte blocks and checks an XOR trailer after writing output.
Decode loop. Remaining count determines block schedule.
Helper returns here after its manipulated return chain.
Compare intermediate-state XOR accumulators with the final input block.
Restore caller PR and return 0 on match, -1 otherwise.
Literal 0x0f00078c, loaded at 0x9924.
Seed count-derived state and code-as-data constants.
Pointer to 0x99ec, used in return-address differences.
Pointer to marker start at 0x99e4.
Hitachi.PublicKeyCipher. is read as arithmetic constants. The name does not establish a public-key scheme.
Mix state and insert 0x9b3c in saved return chain.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x99ac.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x99be.
Top-first: 9c68,9bf4,993c becomes 9c68,9bf4,9b3c,993c.
Final stage assigns emitted r4/r5 at 0x9b30/0x9b32.
Entered by RTS at 0x9bf6. No PR push, the saved wrapper return is already on stack.
Consume saved 0x993c and return to wrapper.
Per-block entry. All 423 helper instructions execute for each valid block. Custom register/stack convention.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x9c34.
T is always zero. BT always falls through to BSR 0x9c60.
Pop inserted 0x9b3c, then RTS enters the continuation.
Post-accumulation mixing, code constant from live PR+0x10.
Always runs and invokes the saved-return editor.
Two executed instructions also read as one BE32 constant at 0x9a0a.
Commit second accumulator and continue mixing.
DMA channel 2 end (vector 76), the card's video data channel: clear IE, set bit 1 of 0x0f000892 and post 08890008 to task 8's entry 51.

98 (CDC_MpGetTc), entry 8, replaced by the known cards: the frame bank, picture type and temporal reference in CR1 and CR2, the time code in CR3 and CR4, read from the card at 0x0a100022, from entry 37's record, or by the bank in 0x0a100006 from the records at 0x090752e4 and 0x090752f4. The wait path returns with r11 nonzero.
99 (CDC_MpGetPts), entry 9: the longword 0x090752a4 in r13.
9F (CDC_MpGetPictSiz), entry 15: the picture size from the card register 0x0a100022 at indexes 0 and 1, 12 bits each. Waits with bit 3 of 0x0f000897.

A1 (CDC_MpSetWinFpos, CDC_MpSetWinFrat, CDC_MpSetWinDpos, CDC_MpSetWinDsiz, CDC_MpSetWinDofs), entry 17, replaced by the known cards: setting 0..4 from CR1's low byte, values from CR3 and CR4 into 0x0f00085a..0x0f000865, or for the display position and offset into 0x0907531c..0x09075323 and their sum into 0x0f000856. Doubled while bit 3 of 0x0f000854 is set. Bit 0 of CR2 writes 0x0f000856..0x0f000865 to 0x0a100002..0x0a100011.
Task 8, the MPEG task, writes 0x7fff to MPEG card register 0x0a10001a, clears two RAM state regions and waits for a message at 0xa022.
Use low message byte as an unchecked byte offset into the six-pointer table at 0xa034. State-1 resumption can instead use the decoded-disc task-8 hook at 0x09075820.

93. Rejected with ff000000 without a loaded extension. CR2 bit 0 set with the card bit clear posts 08810004 (task 8 activation at 0xa41c). Otherwise the card bit is cleared when bit 0 is clear, the channels stop and 08890000, 088a0000, 088c0000, 09810000 and 08810000 are posted. The response comes from entry 68.
AF, without the expansion table: writes CR4 to a card register at 0x0a100000 or 0x0a180000 plus an even offset, or reads it.
AE, without the expansion table: the word the firmware keeps for a card register, from 0x0f000854 by offset or 0x0f000884.

ITU2 input capture B (vector 89), a falling edge of TIOCB2: three reads of 0x0a100000 ANDed into the video status word 0x0f000846, the MPEG interrupt flags with MPST, MPCM for an interval, entries 38..40, and work for task 8's entry 35 through 0x0f000896 and 088c0010.
Capture B with the card bit clear: count bits 4 and 5 of the status word clear in 0x0f00089e and 0x0f00089f.
Task 8 payload 4: 0x7fff to 0x0a10001a, card channels start (0xa460), MPEG state and card bit cleared (0xa4d0), entry 34 (the ROM's 0xa4f0 sets the card bit), MPED, then entry 32.
Clear 24 internal-RAM longwords and 83 buffer-RAM longwords in descending order. Returns with T=1, with no device reads, calls or message posting.

Entry 34 of the ROM table, from task 8's activation: entry 33, 0x8209 to 0x0a180008 and 0 to 0x0a180000, then 0x67818022 to 0x0f000890 (the card bit among it), -1 to 0x0f000850, 0x0101 to 0x0f000898..0x0f00089d and 20 to 0x090752e0.
Entry 33 of the ROM table: MPEG state from 0x0f000854, then card registers 0x0a100020, 0x0a10001a, 0x0a100014, 0x0a100002 and 0x0a100000.

94 (CDC_MpSetMode), entry 4, replaced by the known cards: the mode from CR1's low byte (2 rejected, 4 the sector buffer mode, bits 0 and 1 still picture and high definition), decode timing and output from CR2 into 0x0f000868 for 0x0a100014, the scan mode from CR3's high byte (bit 1 rejected) into bit 7 of 0x0f000891. Leaving the buffer mode runs entry 33.

95 (CDC_MpPlay), entry 5: rebuilds the byte 0x0f000890 from CR1's low byte and CR2's bytes, and with CR4's low byte bit 5 of it and the decode bit, bit 0 of the word 0x0f000854 for 0x0a100000. Waits with bit 3 of 0x0f000892.

96 (CDC_MpSetDec), entry 6, replaced by the known cards: the audio mute from CR1's low byte into 0x0f000884 for 0x0a180008, the pause (CR2) and freeze (CR4) as bits 2 and 3 of 0x0f000868, bits 0..2 and 4..6 of 0x0f000893 and intervals at 0x0f00088c and 0x0f000888. A new freeze runs entry 37.

97 (CDC_MpOutDsync), entry 7, replaced by the known cards: in still picture the frame bank from CR2 into 0x0f000868, in states 4 and 5 entries 38 and 39 and a decode pulse on 0x0a100000, then 2 added to 0x0f000842 and MPCM. With VSYNC timing in the movie mode only the status response.

A0 (CDC_MpDisp), entry 16, replaced by the known cards, whose A0 can jump here: in still picture the frame bank from CR2 into 0x0f000868, then bit 0 of CR2's high byte clears bit 1 of 0x0f000854 for 0x0a100000, and clear sets it.
Entry 38: count down 0x0f00088c. At 1 reload it from 0x0f00088e, set bit 2 of 0x0f000893 and bit 2 of 0x0f000868 for 0x0a100014.
Entry 39: count down 0x0f000888. At 1 reload it from 0x0f00088a, set bit 6 of 0x0f000893 and bit 3 of 0x0f000868 for 0x0a100014.
Entry 40: clear the 0x0f000868 bits entries 38 and 39 set, running entry 37 for bit 6, and clear bits 2 and 6 of 0x0f000893.
Task 8 offset 16, entry 35: the bits of 0x0f000896 call entries 43..45, 47..49 with entry 36, and 73..75, 85, 46, 41 and 42 by state, count intervals in 0x0f000842, then wait through entry 32.
Entry 41, the video part in state 6: once the video partition holds enough sectors, post 08890008, restore the state from 0x0f000898 and start decoding.
Entry 42, the audio part in state 6: once the audio partition holds 4 sectors, post 088a000c and restore the state from 0x0f000899.
Entry 37: match the low 6 bits of 0x0a100006 against four records at 0x090752e4 and copy the match to 0x09075304.
Entry 36: r11 = 088a000c when 0x090752a8 with 0x090752ad is above 0x090752a4 with 0x090752ae.
Entry 66: status ff with the MPEG status.
Entry 67: the wait response's status byte with the MPEG status.
Entry 68: the status response with the MPEG status from 0x0f00089c, 0x0f000891, 0x0f000842 and 0x0f000844.
90, entry 0: the status response through entry 68.
91, entry 1: the status byte with the longword 0x0f000848, which is cleared, in r12's low 24 bits.
92, entry 2: CR1's low byte and CR2 to 0x0f00084c, then the status response through entry 68.

9A (CDC_MpSetCon), entry 10, replaced and called by the known cards: the audio (CR1, CR2) and video (CR3, CR4) connections, current or next by bit 0 of CR3's high byte, into 0x0907532c, 0x09075328, 0x09075334 and 0x09075330 with states to 2 and request bits in 0x09075388, or cuts. Posts 09810001 to task 9's card work loop.

9D (CDC_MpSetStm), entry 13, replaced by the known cards: stream modes, numbers and channels for audio (CR1, CR2) and video (CR3, CR4) into the records 9E returns, current or next by bit 0 of CR3's high byte.

9B (CDC_MpGetCon), entry 11: two connection records, current (0x0907532c, 0x09075328) or next (0x09075334, 0x09075330) by CR3's high byte, under masks. A current record's last byte becomes ff when its state 0x0f00089c or 0x0f00089d is 1, a next record's when its bit in 0x0f000894 is clear.
9E (CDC_MpGetStm), entry 14: two stream records, current (0x0907533c, 0x09075338) or next (0x09075344, 0x09075340) by CR3's high byte, under masks.
DMA channel 3 end (vector 78), the card's audio data channel: clear IE, set bit 2 of 0x0f000892 and post 088a000c to task 8's entry 72.
9C (CDC_MpChgCon), entry 12: accepted parts of CR2 move 0x0f00089c or 0x0f00089d from 4 to 5, then entry 88, the status response and 08810014 to task 8.
Entry 88, from 9C: parts with bit 0 clear call entry 58 or 59 (stopping DMA channel 2 or 3), clear their bit of 0x0f000894, return to state 1 and call entry 60. Then 0x0907537b = 1.
A2 (CDC_MpSetBcolor), entry 18: CR2 to 0x0a100012 and 0x0f000866.
A3 (CDC_MpSetFade), entry 19: two gains of -8..7 from CR2 into the high byte of 0x0f000854 and 0x0a100000, others rejected.
A4 (CDC_MpSetVeff), entry 20: the word 0x0f00086c for 0x0a10001c from CR2's low byte, CR3 and CR4, and bits 4..7 of 0x0f000854 for 0x0a100000 from CR2's high byte.

A5 (CDC_MpGetImg), entry 21, replaced by the known cards: rejected with output to VDP2, waits while bit 8 of 0x0a100000 is set, otherwise 0x00fe to 0x0a100016 and the display size's product in r12's low 24 bits. r13 stays 0x0a000000.
Shared ends of 9C, A2..A4 and A5: entry 68 (0xb826), 67 (0xb834) or 66 (0xb842), each with r11 = 0.
ITU2 input capture A (vector 88), a falling edge of TIOCA2: entry 56. Nothing is posted.
Entry 56: clear IMFA, entry 57 with channel 3 paused, then the audio error bit 5 of 0x0f000845 and bit 20 of the MPEG interrupt flags, with MPST when masked in.
Entry 57: bit 14 of 0x0a180008 set and cleared again over the kept word 0x0f000884.
Entry 58, from entry 88: stop DMA channel 2 with IE set and clear the video part's bytes, then 3 to 0x0a00000c.
Entry 59, from entry 88: stop DMA channel 3 with IE set and clear the audio part's bytes.
Entry 61, no ROM caller: bit 0 of 0x0a100000 low for 8 loop passes and back.
Entry 60, from entry 88: toggle bit 1 of 0x0f000890.
Task 9 waits for a message before expansion processing at 0xba48.
Task 9 continuation. Payload 0 goes to 0xbbc6, 0x0f000892 bit7 set goes to 0xba5e and other requests continue at 0xbae8.

Task 9 with the card bit set and a nonzero payload: bits 0..3 of 0x09075388 call entries 54, 53, 69 and 70, bits 0..3 of 0x09075389 jump to entries 78, 77, 80 and 79, which return through entry 76 (0xbad6). Repeats until no bit is set, then waits at 0xba46.

Payload 1 returns to the wait. Payloads 2 and above run the five checks listed at 0xbc28 with r0 = 1. Entries 0 and 2 return zero, entries 1, 3 and 4 are the card checks at 0xbcc4, 0xbe7c and 0xbf04. Results collect in 0x0f0007b1 before 0xbb1e acts on them and on request byte 0x0907538a.

After the card checks. A failed check clears the expansion for E0 through 0x1b5e (card status 0001) or sets status byte 1 for E2. Otherwise E0 runs the expansion loader 0x1b06 (status byte 0x0f0007ad = 2, whatever the result) and E2 expansion entry 86 through 0xf8e2 (status byte 0x0f0007ac = 3 for r13 = 0, else 2). Then the request byte and busy clear and 0x0800 (MPED) goes to 0x0a00001e.
Task 9 payload 0 from 93: 3 to 0x0a00000c, 0 to 0x0a10001a. With the card bit set it posts 08090004 to task 8, otherwise clears the MPEG state and writes MPED.
Returns -1. No reference in the ROM.
No reference in the ROM. Expects ffffffff from 0x0a100008 and 0x0a10000a with ffff at 0x0a10001a, and SEGA with fffe.

Check 1: an MPEG-1 video sequence header of 18 words from 0x0907539c to 0x0a10001e on DMA channel 2, one word per falling edge of TIOCA1, the card's video data request (ITU1 capture A). Passes when TE is set after 0x500 loop passes.
No reference in the ROM. Compares what 0x0a100022 returns for registers 3..0 with fields of check 1's header.
Check 3: 0x8209 to 0x0a180008, then four zero words to 0x0a180000 on DMA channel 3, one per falling edge of TIOCA0, the card's audio data request (ITU0 capture A). Passes when TE is set.

Check 4: fills the card memory behind 0x0a100030..0x0a100037, 512 blocks of 1024 bytes, with seed + block + byte offset, reads four words back from each quarter, then clears it without checking the clear.
Random word from the state at 0x090753e8 and TCNT4.
No reference in the ROM. The ready poll with bit 7 of the word at 0x0f000868 cleared.
Card ready: up to 33 polls of bit 0 of 0x0a100034, each after writing r11 to 0x0a100014.
No reference in the ROM. Sets bit 7 of the word at 0x0f000868 and writes it to 0x0a100014.
Fill the card memory with seed + block + byte offset: per block the address (8-byte units) to 0x0a100030, 0xfe00 to 0x0a100032, 0xfffc to 0x0a100034, then 512 words to 0x0a100036.
Read four words at address r8 with 0xfa04 and compare them with the fill pattern for seed r0.
Fill the card memory with r0.

Get MPEG ROM, ROM table entry 86, run by E2 through the stub 0xf8e2. Clears the page count 0x0f0007ae, then for each page from 0x0907538c to 0x09075390 takes a free slot, copies 2048 bytes from 0x0e005000 + 2048 * page between 24 and 280 cleared bytes and files the slot from CD device 3 through the filter. r13 = 0 after the last page, -1 without a free slot.
ROM table entry 81: the free pool head under the sector lock as task 9, kept at 0x0907539a, ff when the pool is empty.
ROM table entry 84: the slot address for slot r1 and the page offset r2 << 11.
ROM table entry 82: clear 24 or 280 bytes from r1 by bit 0 of r5.
ROM table entry 83: copy 2048 bytes from r2 to r1.
ROM table entry 87: pair CD device 3 with the filter at 0x09075399, then deliver the slot at 0x0907539a from device 3, under the sector lock as task 9.

E0 Authenticate Device. CR2 low byte 0 posts 07810008 to task 7 (disc) and 1 posts 09810002 to task 9 (MPEG). An accepted request keeps its message at 0x09075384 and sets busy flag 0x0f0007b0 until the task clears it.
E2 Get MPEG ROM. Requires nonzero 0x0f0002fd (a loaded expansion), filter at most 23, offset at most 0x7ff and offset plus count at most 0x800. Posts 09810004 to task 9.
E1 Get Authentication Result. Subcode 0 returns word 0x0f000786 in CR2, whose low byte 0x0f000787 is the disc result. Subcode 1 returns words 0x0f0007ac and 0x0f0007ae in CR2 and CR4. No message.
A6 (CDC_MpSetImgPos, CDC_MpSetImgSiz), entry 22: position or size for bank 0..3, rounded down to even, at 0x0907539c + 8 * bank + 4 * selection.
MPEG commands 90..AF: entry n = (command & 0x3f) - 16 through the expansion table 0x0907b008.
Stubs for entries 32..88 every four bytes: n into r0, then the jump through the expansion table 0x0907b008 + 4n.
Stubs for entries 89..97: the jump through the ROM table 0xf938 + 4n, firmware services for loaded code.
Jump to entry r0 of the expansion table (0xf912) or the ROM table (0xf91a). r14 is kept, r0 is the target, everything else passes through.
0 in the known revisions. The known card entries let nonzero ROM table entries replace their own only when this byte is greater than the card's version.
ROM table, one longword per entry 0..100: ROM routines for loaded code below 89, firmware services 89..97, then the first sector slot, the partition records and the free pool count.
TOC longwords: control/ADR in bits 31..24 over a frame address. Index 1..99 tracks, 100..102 points A0, A1 and A2, index 0 the B0 lead-out limit.
Decoded disc-extension destination and supplied VBR value location.
Collected encoded disc-extension data. It overlaps the destination with a 0x48-byte gap.
Record 11: lock byte +2, owner +3, waiter link +12. Callers with r11=0x0b070000 select this record with owner token 7.
Current task-record pointer, read by lock services and replaced by task dispatch.
Twelve ready-head words scanned in ascending address order through 0x0f000204. First nonempty queue wins, and +16 links form each ready chain.
Initialization flags, the CR1 low byte of command 04: bit 1 R-W subcode on audio tracks, bit 2 no Mode 2 subheader check, bit 3 Form 2 retries, bit 4 single speed.
Disc flags: bit 5 double speed for the next staged command, cleared by it. Bit 6 disc authentication owns the drive. Bit 7 a B0 report announced another session, kept until the TOC is cleared.
Bit 0 names the status buffer written last: set for 0x0f000274, clear for 0x0f00026c. The status builders flip it.
Play range start (top byte 1 for a track position) and end (top byte the repeat limit).

Command flags: bit 0 stopped, set by a stop, cleared by a seek, pause, read or ring seek. Bit 2 scan requested. Bit 3 busy, cleared at the report of the frame that sends the command or when a request is only answered. Bit 4 scan backward. Bit 5 reply not yet taken, cleared one report later. Status code 0 while bit 3 or 5 is set. Bit 6 standby timer running. Bit 7 the last positioning command was not a read: set by a seek, pause or stop and at a scan's end, cleared by a read or ring seek. Only with it set does status code 4 count as settled, and status code 3 starts no delivery. The disc-gone reset and the reset request clear bits 0 and 7.

Read flags: bit 0 repeats used up, PEND at the next pause. Bit 1 R-W subcode during audio play. Bit 2 retry, host status 8. Bit 3 read error, status code 9. Bit 4 the latest report gave or advanced the frame. Bit 5 a data read. Bit 6 reading, sectors delivered through task 5. Bit 7 the read held by a full buffer.
Staged drive command, 12 bytes: command, frame address (bytes 1..3), parameters, byte 10 = 1 or 2, byte 11 = pending flag.
Latest drive report, 11 bytes: status, then Q-subcode fields or the ring-seek word, frame and two words. Byte +11 is 1 when the checksum matched.
Lead-in reports taken: all at 0x0f0002e0, those with status bit 3 at 0x0f0002e4, the others at 0x0f0002e8.
Link state: outgoing packet +0..+11, received sum +12, byte count +13 (0x80 = repeat the packet), full-save flag +14.
Task 13 flags: bit 0 a request not yet taken, bit 1 a copy runs, bit 2 a move runs, bit 3 the copy or move failed, which command 67 reports.
Bit 0 set while task 4 has not taken the request at 0x0f000738.
32-byte scratch window, output accumulators at +0x10 and +0x14.
Kept copy of the card register 0x0a100000: bit 0 the decode bit, bit 1 set while the display is off, bit 3 clear for high definition, bits 4..7 from A4, the high byte from A3.

Kept copy of the card register 0x0a100014, the decoder's modes: bit 0 VSYNC timing, bit 1 output to VDP2, bit 2 clear while paused, bit 3 clear while frozen, bits 4 and 5 the frame bank, bit 6 movie mode, bit 7 clear in the sector buffer mode.

Play flags, the first byte of the longword that activation sets to 0x67818022: bits 0 and 1 play, bit 2 automatic video transfer, bit 3 a current video connection, bit 4 synchronized play, bit 5 decode off, bit 6 automatic audio transfer, bit 7 the synchronized pause entry 35 keeps.

Decode flags: bit 0 decode stopped, from card status bit 13 clear. Bit 2 from card status bit 12 clear. Bits 5, 4 and 1 set while entry 35 runs its entries for event bits 0, 1 and 2. Bit 6, in the known cards' code, from a GOP start until a picture with a later temporal reference. Bit 7 an interlaced scan.

Card flags: bit 0 a video switch at a stream's end (known cards' code only), bit 1 a DMA channel 2 end, bit 2 a DMA channel 3 end, bit 3 entry 35 running, bit 6 the sector buffer mode, bit 7 the card bit, which opens the MPEG commands and task 9's card work.

Pause flags: bits 0..2 the pause (2 paused, 5 an interval, 0 released), bits 4..6 the freeze the same way. Bit 7, in the known cards' code, the synchronized pause the ROM keeps in bit 7 of the play flags.
Connection flags: bits 0 and 4 the video and audio transfers, which a cut clears. Bits 1 and 5 a next video and audio connection. Bit 4 goes to bit 4 of 0x0a00001a, and with it set bit 7 drives PB6.
Card events for task 8's entry 35, set by the capture B handler 0xa190: bit 0 for bit 11 of the card's status word clear, bit 1 for bit 6, bit 2 for bit 4 (an interval).
Set while code uses a card register: bit 0 0x0a180008, bit 1 0x0a100000, bit 2 0x0a10001a, bit 3 the word 6 read through 0x0a100022. Commands that use the same register wait.

FUNCTION.NAME: firmware_reset
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Entry address supplied by both power-on and manual-reset PC vectors.

FUNCTION.NAME: task6_message_dispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Task 6 continuation after its wait at 0x2796, GBR 0x0f00025c. In drive state 0 every message except a drive report waits again.

FUNCTION.NAME: task6_periodic_status
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: After each drive report: PB6 from the audio pre-emphasis bit in drive states 6 and 12, status words to CR1..CR4 when bit 1 of 0x0a000004 is set, and 0x0400 to 0x0a00001e.

FUNCTION.NAME: drive_disc_gone
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Disc gone: clear the TOC area, post 07060000 to task 7, write 0x0020 (DCHG) to 0x0a00001e and clear request flags.

FUNCTION.NAME: drive_command_stage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Copy r1, r2 and r3 to command bytes 0x0f0002c4..0x0f0002cf. Byte 10 becomes 1 or 2, byte 11 is the pending flag the link reads.

FUNCTION.NAME: drive_notify_task5
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Post 05060003 or 05060007 to task 5 by bits 6 and 1 of 0x0f0002a7.

FUNCTION.NAME: status_from_target
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Host status words and Q record for target frame 0x0f0002a0.

FUNCTION.NAME: status_from_report
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Host status bytes and Q record from a drive report.

FUNCTION.NAME: status_reset
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reset the next status buffer and Q record to ff with the host status code.

FUNCTION.NAME: task5_sector_done
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A sector arrived: read the frame from its header, synchronize on two sectors in a row, approach the target, stream, check the decoder status by mode and complete the sector.

FUNCTION.NAME: task5_read_start
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A read request: target from 0x0f0002b8, a slot prepared for DMA, then the decoder's sector pulse enabled.

FUNCTION.NAME: startup_rom_sum
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Sum every big-endian ROM longword modulo 2^32 and store it at 0x0f000004. No comparison or startup rejection occurs in this routine.

FUNCTION.NAME: exception_illegal_instruction
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Vector 4: restart at 0x0428 without a reset. Vector 12 (0x09ba), SCI1 (0x09c6) and the unused interrupt sources (0x09cc) restart the same way.

FUNCTION.NAME: exception_dma_address_error
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Vector 10: stop all four DMA channels as startup does, 8 to the transfer control 0x0a000002, return. No task is told.

FUNCTION.NAME: exception_ignored
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reserved vectors and TRAPA 0x2f..0x3f return at once. Slot illegal instruction, CPU address error and NMI return the same way from 0x093a, 0x0940 and 0x09b4.

FUNCTION.NAME: diagnostic_report
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reset with PB10 (TEST, TP3) low. SCI1 clocked synchronous sends the ROM sum's low byte, then after a delay a byte built from the diagnostic words, whose bit 2 stays set unless an address line failed.

FUNCTION.NAME: monitor_setup
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SCI1 asynchronous 8N1, BRR1 0x41 (about 9600 bps at 20 MHz), SSR1 cleared, which sends TDR1's last byte again. State at 0x0f000004 cleared, prompt ':'.

FUNCTION.NAME: monitor_loop
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Poll forever with interrupts masked: receive, transmit, a completed line, L's repeat.

FUNCTION.NAME: monitor_command_r
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: R address: area 0 reads only 0x0400 + the low five bits, area 7 only 0x0f000000..0x0f000007. Answers '>', four hex digits and CR.

FUNCTION.NAME: monitor_command_w
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: W address value: a byte (odd address) or word write. Areas 5 and 7 refused.

FUNCTION.NAME: monitor_command_l
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: L address [value]: read or write the address once a loop until the next CR. Areas 0, 5 and 7 refused.

FUNCTION.NAME: startup_task_queues
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Initialize thirteen task records, chain eleven into the first ready head, then select and dispatch task 1 at 0x63dc. Initial frames hold PC/SR only.

FUNCTION.NAME: task_restart
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: TRAPA 0x2e: reset timers, DMA and transfer state, re-create the records of every task except 6 and 14, chain them for a fresh start and dispatch. Task 6 resumes after its trap.

FUNCTION.NAME: task_reinit
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: TRAPA 0x28: initialize the record of task r11 >> 24 again, as at startup.

FUNCTION.NAME: task_wait_message
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Wait for a message with an exception-only frame. Queued messages make the current task ready. A matching partner link can bypass ordinary ready selection.

FUNCTION.NAME: message_send_wait_reply
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: TRAPA 0x20: post r11, run the destination at once, sender (bits 23..16) waits in state 2. Refuses a destination in state 2 or 3. A destination already in a ready queue is looked for in the queue whose head slot lies 16 bytes after its own. For the last four heads (IDs 1, 13, 9 and 14) that slot is in the disc extension's collection state at 0x0f000208..0x0f000217, followed as a record unless it reads 0. From a zero link the search goes on through the ROM longwords at 0x10 and 0x944 to an unaligned longword read at 0x00090019.

FUNCTION.NAME: message_reply
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: TRAPA 0x29: r12 and r13 into the partner's first two mailbox words (+24 and +28), the replier waits in state 3 and the partner runs. No partner: diagnostic 5, r0 = -1.

FUNCTION.NAME: message_post_and_ready
